summary: Papists to return to their places of Abode
abstract: On address of Parliament, all popish recusants to return to their places of abode. Officers to enforce the Acts 1 W. & M. (Papists to leave London) and (for disarming Papists). Suspected persons are to be tendered the oath (7 & 8 Wm. Ill), and in case of refusal the law to be enforced. B. M. C. 21. f. 2 (54) cut. P.C. II (132). Lond. Gaz. 3476. C. J. xii. 517, 522.

opening: William &c. Whereas it hath been humbly
summary: Collection for the Vaudois
abstract: On the petition of Henry Arnault representing the Vaudois on this side the River Cluson, a collection is ordered for their benefit to pay for transplanting them to Germany. Committee appointed. B.L.

abstract: Parliament, prorogued to Thursday, 16 November, -will meet then. All members to attend. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3543. 24 October. 1T°

summary: For apprehending the Author and Printer of a Libel, An Inquiry into the Causes of the Miscarriage of the Scotch-Colony at Darien, &c
abstract: London; Bill & Exec. : 1699[-1700]. On the address of Parliament, .£500 is offered for the discovery and apprehension of the author and £200 for the printer of a libel entitled ‘ An Inquiry into the Causes of the Miscarriage of the Scotch-Colony at Darien, or. An Answer to a Libel, Intituled, A Defence of the Scots Abdicating Darien’. Pardon to any accomplice not the author as well as the reward. Lond. Gaz. 3571 ; C.J. xiii. 123. 29 January.

abstract: All Jesuits and priests who have taken orders from the See of Rome to depart out of this kingdom, and not to return, on pain, &c. Lond. Gaz. 3574. 9 February. N° 4272. 1699-1700: 11-12 William III

abstract: in embassies. The £100 fine in 3 Jas. I all to go to informers. Protestant childi-en of popish parents may have a provision made for them in Chancery. B.L. 24 April.

summary: Collection for the fire in Bermondsey
abstract: Fall per Pearson. On account of a fire in the parish of St. Mary Magdalene, Bermondsey, on 14 June, where damage amounting to £23,079 was done, many families are brought to destitution. 116 houses burnt down. Collection to last for a year.

summary: Mastei’s of Ships to take Passes for Algiers
abstract: Lond. Gaz. 3609. 11 June.

title: A Proclama tion
summary: For enforcing the Acts touching duties on Marriages, Births, and Burials, &c
abstract: Recites Acts 6 & 7 Wm. Ill, 8 Wm. Ill, 9 & 10 Wm. Ill, and 11 & 12 Wm. Ill, appointing Commissioners for enforcing the duties on marriages, births, burials, batchelors, and widowers. These Commissioners are to meet at least once in three months, or oftener, call before them the assessors and collectors, see that registers are kept, and that curates enter in them the name of every person married, buried, christened or born, with their condition or quality, the names of the heirs, &c. (burials), fathers or guardians (birth), and husbands’ places of abode (marriages), on pain of £20 fine. Lond. Gaz. 3661. 10 December.

title: A Proclamation, For Dissolving this present Parliament, and Declaring the Speedy Calling another
abstract: Parliament, prorogued to 16 January, is dissolved. A new Parliament will be summoned for Thursday, 6 February. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 6364 (3664). 19 December. Ifo

title: A Proclamation, For Encouraging Mariners, Seamen, and Landmen to Enter themselves on Board His Majesties Ships of War. Kensington; 26 February l/Of. London : Bill & Exec. : 170j
abstract: A bounty to all who enter before 28 days from date of 30s. to able seamen and 25s. to ordinary seamen or landmen. Soldiers belonging to the marine regiments of the Marquis of Carmarthen and Sir Cloudesley Shovell shall have 25s. bounty. Seamen re-entering a month’s pay. Justices of the Peace to give certificates to those wishing to enter and to send lists to the Navy Commissioners. Conduct money allowed. Deserters for bounty punished. Lond. Gaz. 3683. 28 February.

summary: For the apprehension of Pirates
abstract: Any person who seizes or causes to be seized the captain, one or more of the crew, and the vessel of any pirates shall have one-half of the King’s third, or one-fourth if the ship falls to the King. They must be delivered to any port magistrate in the kingdom, in America to the Governors of Barbados, the Leeward Islands, Jamaica, Bermudos, Virginia, Maryland, New yorke, or the Massachusets Bay in New England, to the Commander at Newfoundland, or in Africa to the Chief of the Eoyal African Company at Cape Corse Castle on the Gold Coast, James Fort in Kiver of Gambia, or at Whiddah in South of Guinea. A pardon will be given to the informer. If the commanding officer, or crew, are seized without the ship, a reward of £100 for the captain and £20 each for the others will be paid on conviction. Informers may enter the sea service and leave it when they like. Pirates confessing may have a pardon for all piracies committed before 24 June, 1701, and may enter the Navy. Commissioners under Great Seal have been sent to the East and West Indies to try pirates. This pardon does not apply to any fresh acts of piracy or to Henry Every alias Bridgeman. Lond. Gaz. 3688. 12 March.

title: A Proclamation, For a General Fast and Humiliation throughout the whole Kingdom
abstract: Friday, 4 April, is appointed a day of humiliation to implore God’s blessing on the consultations of Parliament. The archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 3686. 8 March.

summary: Popish Recusants to return home and stop there
abstract: Being informed that arms are being stored by Papists, in London and suburbs, issues on address of Parliament a Proclamation substantially the same as No. 4274, q.v., with special mention of seizing arms, &c. Lond. Gaz. 3684. 1 March.

title: A Proclamation, For Apprehending John Glover, Alexander Cutting, William Adye, and William Clifton
abstract: London; Bill & Exec. : 1701. Another edition of No. 4286, q.v. B.L. P.C. II (147). P.B.O. 4 (183). N° 4287. On address of Commons, a reward of £100 is offered for the apprehension of John Glover, and £50 each for Alex- 1701-2; 13 William III & 1 Anne ander Cutting, ‘William Adye, and William Clifton, who have endeavoured by bribery to procure election to this present Parliament. B.L. Lend. Gaz. 3692; C.J. xiii. 441. 28 March.

title: A Proclamation, For Dissolving this present Parliament, and Declaring the Speedy Calling another
abstract: Parliament, prorogued to Thursday, 13 November, is dissolved, and another summoned on Tuesday, 30 December, on account of the recognition of the pretended Prince of Wales as King by the King of France. Lond. Gaz. 3757, 12 November.

title: A Proclamation, Commanding all Papists and Reputed Papists to Depart from the Cities of London and Westminster, and from within Ten Miles from the same. Kensington: 11 January 1701
abstract: Recites 3 Jas. I. Popish recusants to leave London under penalty 1 W. & M. Lord Mayor and Justices to remove Papists or tender them the declaration of 30 Charles II. Justices to send notice of refusal to declare to the King's Bench or Quarter Sessions. All Papists to leave London before 19 January. Constables to take a list of all remaining and certify them to the Justices who will proceed as directed. B.L. 14 Januaiy.

abstract: Professes concern for preservation of the religion, laws, and liberties of the country, the Protestant succession, and government in Church and State as by law established. Importance of carrying on prepai-ations for war with France. Lond. Gaz. 3790. 9 March. Ifo

title: A Proclamation For the better Observance of the Act for Laying Duties upon Malt, Mum, Cyder and Perry. St. Jame.s’s: 8 March 1701
abstract: Publishing and enforcing the provisions of ‘an Act for laying Duties upon Malt, Mum, Cyder and Perry ’. All persons having malt in their possession on 9 March to report it to the nearest officer of excise before 10 April 1702, and within six days to pay the duty. Malsters to make a monthly entry of the amount made, and to give notice to the excise of the number, &c., of cisterns, uting-fats, &c., they have or propose to construct, on penalty. B.L. 4 (195). Original signed, P.S.B. 267. Lond. Gaz. 3790. 9 March.

summary: London
abstract: Her to Lutestring By Charles, Earl of Carlisle, Earl Mai’shal during the minority of Thomas, Duke of Norfolk. In pursuance of an order of a Privy Council held at the Cockpit, 8 March, gives notice that it is the Queen’s pleasure all persons wear the deepest mourning (long cloaks excepted) for the late King, to begin on Sunday next [15]. All Lords and Officers of the Household to cover their coaches with black cloth, and not to use varnished or bullion nails in them, except Prince George of Denmark. Hatbands of blach English Alamode covered with black crape will be proper mourning. B.L. 10 March.

All judges and oflBcers to be strict and punish severely all excessive drinking, blasphemy, lewdness, profanation of the Lord’s Day, or other immoral practices, suppress all baudy houses, gaming houses, &c., execute 29 Chas. II and 9 Wm. Ill, and prevent the selling of wine, chocolate, coifee, ale, beer, &c., during hours of Divine Service. B.L. Lend. Gaz. 3796. 28 March.

abstract: Wednesday, 10 June, appointed a day of fasting and humiliation for a blessing on the war with France and Spain. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 3811. 18 May.

title: A Proclamation, For Recalling and Prohibiting Seamen, from Serving Foreign Princes and States
abstract: All seamen in foreign service are to return home, and not accept foreign service or pay. Officers to stop any transportation and seize any person found in foreign service. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3810. 18 May. Ifo

title: Her Majesties most Gracious Declaration, Concerning Ships Stopt before the Declaration of War
abstract: Lond. Gaz. 3815. 3 June. N° 4326. Another edition of No. 4326, q.v.

title: Her Majesties most Gracious Declaration, For the Incouragement of Her Ships of War and Privateers
abstract: All prizes taken and condemned shall be appraised and sold by inch of candle, and after paying duties one-half of the net proceed shall be paid over to the officers and crew of the ships taking it. Her Majesty to have the refusal of ships of war and to pay £10 per gun and £10 per ton, assisting ships to have their accustomed share, privateers to be sold for the captors except one-tenth to the Lord High Admiral of England. The reward to be shared out : captain three-eighths (or if a flag is present, flag one-eighth, captain two-eighths) ; lieutenants and master one-eighth ; boatswain, gunner, purser, carpenter, master’s mates, chirurgeon and chaplain one-eighth; midshipmen, carpenter’s mates, boatswain’s mates, gunners’ mates, corporal, yeomen of the sheets, coxswain, quartermasters, quartermasters’ mates, chirurgeon’s mates, yeomen of the powder room, oneeighth ; trumpeter, quarter-gunner, carpenter’s crew, steward, cook, armourer, steward’s mate, cook’s mate, gunsmith, cooper, swabber, ordinary trumpeter, barber, able seamen, ordinary seamen, two-eighths. Captains to draw up a list after taking a prize, to be compared with the musters. Captains may take as pillage anything found upon or above the|] gun deck. Ten pounds a gun allowed for every ship sunk or destroyed. Privateers may bring prizes into port and sell them, on paying duties, having a customs officer on board, and paying one-tenth to the Lord High Admiral. Medals to be paid for out of Lord High Admiral’s fund. Any one purloining from prizes to lose their share, &c. Lond. Gaz. 3815. 4 June.

title: A Proclamation, For the Apprehending all Persons going to or from France, and also for the Taking and Apprehending of all Deserters from Her Majesties Service in the Army Abroad
abstract: Recites Act of 9 Wm. Ill forbidding English refugees in France to return without licence. Revives the Act. Certain soldiers employed abroad have deserted and returned home. They are to be arrested. £40 reward for the apprehension 3 u 2 of any one attempting to go to France. Officers to apprehend such and also all deserters. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3821. 23 June.

No officer or servant is to buy or sell any office in the Household on pain of displeasure and removal. The Queen, Prince George of Denmark, L. Archbishop of Canterbury, L. Keeper, L. Treasurer, L. President, L. Privy Seal, Duke of Somerset, D. of Schonberg, L. Great Chamberlain, L. Chamberlain, E. of Oxford, E. of Radnor, E. of Nottingham, E. of Rochester, E. of Romney, E. of Ranelagh, L. Dartmouth, Mr. Boyle, L. C. J. Holt, Master of the Rolls, L. C. J. Trevor, Mr. Smith. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3826. 10 July.

abstract: Parliament is prorogued from 8 October to 20 October by Writ Patent under Great Seal. All members to be in attendance. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3843. 17 September.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving
abstract: B.L. 4 November.

summary: Requiring plunder taken at Port St. Mary and Vigo to be returned
abstract: On the expedition to Cadiz great quantities of goods and plate were plundered at Port St. Mary and put on board the men-of-war, whose officers were directed by Sir George Rooke to secure it. Great part of this and the Vigo plunder have been concealed from us. All officers and privates are to give up their plunder within twenty days to a Commis- sioner of prizps, on pain, &c. They will receive a pardon if they do so. After twenty days one-fifth the value of the goods recovered will be paid as a reward to any person giving information. Lend. Gaz. 3871. 18 December.

title: A Proclamation, Concerning Colours to be worn on Board Ships
abstract: Shipmasters have used close imitations of Navy pendants, &c. They are not to wear our Jack, commonly called the Union Jack, without warrant. Merchants are to wear the Flag and Jack White with a Red Cross (St. George’s Cross) passing quite through, and the Red Ensign with a like cross in a canton at the upper corner next the staff. Letters of mark beside the Merchant Flag may wear a Red Jack with the Union Jack in a canton in the upper corner next the staff. A similar flag with seals of office, for Commissioners of Navy, victualling customs, transport, and ordnance. Customs officers to report offenders ; twelve days allowed in Channel and North Seas, six weeks to Cape St. Vincent, ten weeks on this side the equinoctial line, and eight months beyond the line. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3872. 30 December.

title: A Proclamation, For Encouraging Seamen, and Landmen to Enter themselves on Board Her Majesties Ships of War
abstract: B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3877. 4 January. Ifo

title: A Proclamation, Requiring all Seamen and Mariners in Her Majesties Service, forthwith to repair to the Ships of War to which they belong. St. James’s: 15 January 1703
abstract: Recites Art. 17 of 13 Chas. II against deserters. All seamen absent without leave from their ships to return to their own or the nearest ship. Pardon to all deserters returning before 1 February. Names of all returning to duty to be notified. All deserters henceforth to be tried by court martial and suffer death. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3880. 18 January. ifo

title: A Proclamation, For Seizing and Apprehending Captain Coshart, and ... La Touche. St. James’s : 1 February 1703
abstract: .£200 reward each for the apprehension of Captain Coshart and ... La Touche, French subjects, detained in Southampton and now escaped. A free pardon and the reward to any of their aiders (other than Thomas Jackson, Marshal of the prisoners of war at Southampton), who shall apprehend them. B.L. 2 (245). Lond. Gaz. 3885. 6 February.

title: A Proclamation, Commanding all Seamen and Soldiers belonging to the Marine Regiments, and other Regiments, to Render themselves into Her Majesties Service. St. James’s : 1 February 1703
abstract: Great numbers of seamen and marines have deserted. They are to return before 1 March to their ships or the 1702-3 : 1-2 Anne Provost Marshal General in London. Those surrendering before 1 March will receive royal pardon. Those who do not will be tried and executed on apprehension. B.L. (2 copies). Lend. Gaz. 3885. 4 February. I

title: A Proclamation, For Discovering and Apprehending the Murderers of William Harrison and Edward Simmonds. St. James’s: 4 February 1702
abstract: William Harrison and Edward Simmonds were murdered when travelling between Hillingdon and Uxbridge. William Perkins, Thomas Gowlet, Richard Bales, and William Johnson have been indicted for and acquitted of the murder of William Harrison, and Mary Perkins, wife of William, and Dorcas Gowlet, widow, acquitted of that of Edward Simmonds. A free pardon is offered to any of the murderers who shall discover the rest of the persons concerned. All subjects are to discover and apprehend the murderers. B.L. Kot. Pat. p. 3. n. 23. Lond. Gaz. 3886. 9 February. I

title: A Proclamation, Declaring Her Majesties Pleasure for the Distribution of Prize Goods taken at Vigo
abstract: B.L. signed, P.S.B. 270. Kot. Pat. p. 3. n. 24. Lond. Gaz. 3890. 22 February. Ifo

summary: Seamen and Soldiers to return to their Ships
abstract: Refers to Prod. 15 January [No. 4345, q.v.] and 1 February [No. 4348, q.v.]. William Gray, a seaman on the Ipswich, a deserter, was seized and condemned to death by court martial at Spithead by Art. 17 of 13 Charles II. Our Dearest Consort, Prince George of Denmark, Lord High Admiral, has requested pardon for William Gray, and a further opportunity till 10 April for deserters to return. All seamen and soldiers who return to duty by then will be pardoned. But if arrested after that date they shall suffer death according to law. B.L. 27 February. ifo

title: A Proclamation, For the Encouragement of Piety and Virtue, and for the preventing and Punishing of Vice, Prophaneness, and Immorality. St. James’s: 25 February 1702
abstract: B.L. (2 copies). Dalk. 2 (250). P.C. (177). Lond. Gaz. 3893.

abstract: Refers to Prod. 1 June [No. 4329, q.v.]. The duties on fish oyls and the produce of foreign plantations are so great that the captors have no encouragement to take them. In future only those duties are to be charged on prizes as if the fish or plantation produce had been imported in English vessels. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 3915. 19 May.

summary: Proroguing Parliament
abstract: B.L. Lend. Gaz. 3951.

title: A Proclamation, For Discovering and Apprehending the Murderers of Abraham Moore
abstract: Abraham Moore of Buckland Dinham, Somerset, tailor, was murdered 20 August last at night, going to Sir Copleston Warwick Bampfield Bart.’s park in Hardington to watch the game, probably by poachers. A free pardon offered to one or two accomplices who shall give information leading to the arrest of the murderers. B.L.

summary: Brief for a Collection for the Inhabitants of Orange
abstract: A house-to-house collection ordered for 3,000 Protestant refugees from Orange, expelled by Louis XIV. Money to be paid into the Chamber of the City of London. Returns to be made to the Archbishop of Canterbury. Forty-seven trustees appointed, seven to form a quorum. Dalk. 2 (252).

title: A Proclamation, For a General Fast
abstract: On account of the terrible storms of 26 and 27 November last many ships have been lost, houses blown down, timber and cornstacks destroyed — a token of the Divine displeasure. Wednesday, 19 January, is appointed a general and public fast. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. B.L. 4 (230). Original signed, P.S.B. 271 (Month uncertain). Lond. Gaz. 3975. 14 December.

summary: Collection for families of sailors
abstract: Arms Archbishops, have Day A collection to be made throughout England for the families of mariners lost in the great storm [26-27 Nov.]. Lists of contributions to be sent to William Borrett, Esq., Inner Temple. Money to Archbishop of Canterbury.

title: A Proclamation, For Encouraging Seamen and Landmen to Enter themselves on Board Her Maiesties Ships of War. St. James’s : 9 January 1703
abstract: A bounty of two months’ pay to seamen and one month’s pay to landmen who volunteer for the Navy before 10 February. Conduct money paid. Entered men and leave men not to be impressed. Constables, &c. , to arrest seamen and deserters. 20s. and 10s. travelling expenses of over 20 miles (6d. a mile if less) paid for every seaman delivered at a port. Protections to last only six months. Lond. Gaz. 3983. 11 January.

title: A Proclamation, For the Careful Custody and well Ordering of the New River brought from Chadwell and Amwell to the North Part of the City of London. St. James’s : 15 February 1703
abstract: B.L. 22 February.

title: A Proclamation, For Apprehending John Tutchin, John How, and Benjamin Bragg. St. James’s : 24 February 170|
abstract: N°s 4369-77 On address of the House of Commons £100 reward for the apprehension of John Tutchin, and £50 each for John How and Benjamin Bragg. John Tutchin broke the privilege of the House by writing in ‘ the Observator from Wednesday Februaiy the 9th to Saturday February the 12th 1703. Published on Saturday the Twelfth Instant, as Printed by John How, in Talbot-Court in Gracechurch-street ; and sold by Benjamin Bragg, in Avemary-Lane.’ They continue to write, print, and publish scandalous papers and cannot be found. B.L. 2 (256). Lond. Gaz. 3996 ; C.J. xiv. 336. 25 February.

Information to be given to William, D. of Devonshire, Charles, D. of Somerset, Charles, E. of Sunderland, Richard, E. of Scarborough, Charles, Visct. Townshend, Thomas, L. Wharton, and John, L. summary: Westminster

title: A Proclamation, For Discovering and Apm*ehending the Author, Printer, and Publisher of a Libel, Intituled, Legion’s Humble Address to the Lords
abstract: The Grand Jury of Gloucester presented a paper — Legion’s Humble Address to the Lords — to Quarter Sessions as a libel. It has been sent to a Secretary of State by the Justices in Session. £100 reward for the conviction of the author, and £50 for the printer. Accomplices (not the author) shall have pardon and full reward on procuring his conviction. Lond. Gaz. 4023. 29 May. Ifo

title: A Proclamation, For Settling and Ascertaining the Current Rates of Foreign Coins in Her Majesties Colonies and Plantations in America
abstract: 20 dwt. 21 grs., 5s. 6d. ; ecu’s of France or silver lewis, 17 dwt. 12 grs., 4s. 6d. ; crusadoes of Portugal, 11 dwt. 4 grs., 2s. lO^d. ; three gilder pieces of Holland, 21 dwt. 7 grs., 5s. 2id. ; old rix dollars of the Empire, 18 dwt. 10 grs., 4s. 6d. ; other denominations of these coins by their weight. They are valued by Mint assay. After 1 January next no Sevill, Pillar, or Mexico pieces of eight of full weight shall be taken or paid in any plantation at above the rate of 6s. current money, other coins in proportion. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4029. 21 June.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving,

summary: Parliament prorogued to 24 Oct

title: A Proclamation, For Encouraging Seamen and Landmen to Enter themselves on Board Her Maiesties Ships of War
abstract: B.I.. Lond. Gaz. 4081. 19 December. Ifo 4378. Certain seamen from the Fleet in the Streights last year and others have gone inland. All magistrates are to apprehend such straggling seamen and send them to a seaport. Constables will be allowed 20s. for each seaman sent on board the tender. The service of seamen is absolutely necessary for the defence of the kingdom and the protection of trading subjects. Lond. Gaz. 4090. 20 January. jfo 438I.

title: A Proclamation, For the more Effectual Putting in Execution a Law, Intituled, ‘ An Act for Raising Recruits for the Land-Forces and Marines, and for Dispensing with Part of the Act for the Encouragement and Encrease of Shipping and Navigation, during the present War.’
abstract: In consequence of the need of recruits all Justices are to enforce up to 1 March next the Statute of 2 Anne for raising recruits. All able-bodied men without employment, or visible means, who are not Parliamentary voters are to be examined and delivered to the recruiting officers. The Articles of War against mutiny and desertion to be read them, and twenty shillings paid to them, and ten or less to the constable raising them. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4082. 21 December.

summary: All Mariners to repair on board the Fleet

title: A Proclamation, For a General Fast. St. James’s : 2 March 170f. London : Bill & Exec. : 170f
abstract: Wednesday, 4 April, appointed for a general fast to implore God’s blessing on the war. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4102, 8 March. 4335. Anns 158 of or in Seamen in Her Majesty’s service absent without leave are to return by 10 January, those absent on leave by 30 January on pain of being made ‘Run’ on the ship’s books. Four deserters have lately been pardoned. No such clemency will be shown to future offenders. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4082. 24 December.

summary: For apprehending straggling seafaring men

title: A Proclamation, For the due Observance of an Act made in the last Session of Parliament, Intituled, An Act to Prevent all Traiterous Correspondence with Her Majesties Enemies
abstract: Recites the provisions of the Act of last Session. No one after 25 March 1705 shall export arms, ordnance, powder, bullets, pitch, tar, hemp, masts, cordage, iron, or saltpetre to France on pain of high treason. No one who went to France after 4 May 1702 is to return without licence, or being returned is to depart on pain of high treason. No one is to correspond with France under pain, &c. Lond. Gaz. 4111. 3 April.

abstract: Parliament, summoned for Tuesday, 14 June, will be prorogued by Writ Patent under Great Seal, to Thursday, 6 September. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4128. 2 June.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving

summary: Proroguing Parliament
abstract: Parliament, now prorogued to 6 September, is further prorogued to Thursday, 25 October, by Writ Patent under Great Seal, on which day all members are to attend. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4150. 15 August.

summary: Reducing penalties on Seamen who came in after the fixed date
Loss by Fire in Morgans-Lane, Southwark
abstract: Fall per Pearson. N°s 4398-405 certified at Kingston Quarter Sessions, 16 October, by Sir John Buckworth, Bart., Shem Bridges, John Mitchell, Thomas Lant, John Lade, John Cater, William Beeves, and Francis Southard, J.P.s, that on 1 August last a fire broke out in Jacob Bell’s house, Morgan’s Lane, Southwark, doing damage upwards of .£2,706, estimated on oath, they are permitted to collect alms. Money to be sent to Sir Thomas Rawlinson, Lord Mayor, Wm. Fazakerley, Chamberlain, Samuel Lewin, Charles Cox, John Lade, John Cholmley, George Meggot, and Henry Martin. This to be in force for one year from Christmas next.

summary: For the apprehension of the Author and the Printer of ‘ The Memorial of the Church of England,’ &c
abstract: At request of Parliament publishes a resolution of both Houses that the Church of England is safe and flourishing, and that whoever says the contrary is an enemy to the Queen, church, and kingdom. X200 reward for the conviction of the author of a malicious libel, ‘ The Memorial of the Church of England, humbly Offered to the Consideration of all true Lovers of Our Church and Constitution ’ : printed and published by David Edwards of St. Dunstans in the West, for whose conviction £50 is offered. Pardon and reward to him or any one whose evidence will convict the author. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4186; L.J. xviii. 44 ; C.J. xv. 57. 22 December. Ifo

summary: All Mariners to return to their Ships
abstract: All seamen absent on leave or without it are to return to their ships, if at Portsmouth forthwith, at elsewhere before the end of January on pain of being marked ‘ Run ’. Pardon to all who have deserted since 1 November if they return at once. Some straggling seamen have been impressed for soldiers. Justices are to send such as appear to be seamen to the fleet. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4192. 14 January. jj-o 440I,

title: A Proclamation, Fora General Fast. St. James’s: 7 February 1705
abstract: Wednesday, 20 March, is appointed a general fast for imploring God’s blessing on the Army. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 4201. 12 February. Ifo 44Q2,

summary: For All Saints Church in Oxford
abstract: On the petition of the parishioners, certified by Dr. William Delaune, Vice-Chancellor, Michael Cripps, Mayor, Dr. Jonathan Edwards, Principal of Jesus, Dr. John Hammond, Canon of Christ Church, Dr. William Paynter, Rector of Exeter, Dr. Arthur Charlet, Master of University College, Sir Robert Harrison, William Wright, Recorder, Henry White and James Pennell, Aldermen, and John Taylor, Assistant, that the steeple of All Saints fell on Friday, 8 March 1698, and with it the greater part of the Church. Contributions are to be made through the country. Money to be sent to the Vice-Chancellor, Mayor, Dr. Henry Aldrich, Dean of Christ Church, Rev. Dr. Fitz-Herbert Adams, Rector of Lincoln, Dr. Charlet, Master of University College, William Wright, Recorder, and Thomas Rowney, Esq. To last one year. (With an advertisement of ‘The Present State of Parish Churches ’.)

title: A Proclamation, For the Putting in Execution an Act of Parliament for the Encouragement and Encrease of Seamen, and for the better and speedier Manning Her Majesties Fleet, and also for the Encouragement of Seamen and Able-bodied Landmen, voluntarily to Enter themselves in Her Majesties Sea-Service
abstract: Recites Act of last Session, giving power for search warrants, and breaking in doors. Twenty shillings reward to constables for each seaman banded over. Persons harbouring sailors fined £5. Sailors discharged to be paid in cash or by ticket. No seaman on service to be sued for less than £20. No person of 18 bound apprentice to any shipmaster shall be protected if he has been to sea before he was apprenticed. Watermen of the Thames liable to serve when called upon by the Admiralty on pain of fine and suspension. Insolvent debtors owing less than £60 may volunteer, or three Justices of Peace may send them. All except prisoners for debt who enter before 1 May will receive a bounty of two or one month’s pay. Remainder as in Prod. 18 Dec. 1705 [No. 4399, q.v.]. B.L. Lend. Gaz. 4214. 29 March.

title: A Proclamation, For the Putting in Execution the Laws in Force against such Persons as have or shall Endeavour to Pervert Her Majesties Subjects to the Popish Religion
abstract: Recites 23 Eliz. by which it is high treason to pervert subjects to the Romish religion, and 3 James I, to reconcile them with the See of Rome or to be absolved by it, &c. On Address of Commons last session these laws are to be enforced by all Judges and others. Lond. Gaz. 4218 ; C.J. xv. 177, 185. 15 April.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving
abstract: Appoints Thursday, 2 7 J une, as a day of public thanksgiving for the victory of Brabant in the Spanish Netherlands under John, Duke of Marlborough, whereby they are re.stored to Austria under King Charles III, for the victories in Catalonia and other parts of Spain. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 4229. 23 May.

summary: Proroguing Parliament
abstract: London : Bill & Exec. ; 1706. Parliament, now prorogued to 22 October, is further prorogued to Thursday, 21 November, when all members are to attend. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4273.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving. Kensington; 19 November 1706
abstract: Tuesday, 31 December, is appointed a day of public thanksgiving for the great and wonderful successes of this year. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. B.L. 21 November.

title: A Proclamation, For Encouraging Seamen and Landmen to Enter themselves on Board Her Majesties Ships of War. St. James’s : 15 January 1706
abstract: London : Bill & Exec. ; 1706[-7]. A reissue of Prod. 18 December 1705 [No. 4399, q.v.J. Fuller statement as to protected men. No one employed in ordnance, victualling, customs or transport, or the Queen’s watermen to be impressed. Lond. Gaz. 4298.

abstract: Wednesday, 9 April, appointed a fast for the continuance of God’s blessing on the Queen’s armies. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4310. 3 March. Ifo

abstract: Thursday, 1 May, appointed a day of thanksgiving for the Treaty of Union between England and Scotland, and prayer for God’s blessing. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4319. 1 April.

summary: Alterations in the Boyal Style in Prayer Book
abstract: Alterations are made in the prayers ‘ For the Preachers ’, leaving out England and Scotland and inserting Great Britain in the royal title and altering King to Queen. In the occasional offices, 5 November, for realm read England ; 29 May for these three kingdoms read these kingdoms, &c. 20 April.

title: A Proclamation, Declaring Her Majesties Pleasure for Holding the First Parliament of Great Britain, and Appointing the Time and Place of Meeting thereof
abstract: Cites Prod. 29 April [No. 4420, q.v.]. Under 22 Article sixteen peers and forty-five commissioners for Shires and Burghs have been chosen Members of Parliament for Scotland. Parliament is to be holden at Westminster on Thursday, 23 October. AH are to attend. Lond. Gaz. 4338. 7 June.

abstract: Lond. Gaz. 4405 ; C.J. xv. 512, 514. 26 J anuary. * This copy is the one signed by Privy Council of Scotland ; original of Scots proclamation.

summary: Orders concerning Election Petitions, &c
abstract: Sine nota. Question, touching to Matters concerning returns and elections to be heard at the Bar of the House. Questions at trial of elections to be determined by ballot, if desired. Petitions respecting election returns to be laid on the table of a new House before the Speaker is chosen. These to be standing orders. These to be sent to the sheriffs for publication by Mr. Speaker. B. M. 21. h. 4 (32). C. J. XV. 551. Gratis. 4 June 1708.

title: A Proclamation, For the better Recruiting Her Majesties Land-Forces and the Marines. Kensington ; 23 February 1707
abstract: Recites an Act for recruiting of this Session. Justices may between 28 February and 1 March 1708[-9] levy all able-bodied men without visible means of support having no vote. Parish officers to raise them on fine of £5 levied by distress, to receive 20s. each on handing them over to the recruiting officer, and the person raised to receive the same. Every volunteer before 1 May to receive £4, before 1 March 1708[-9] £2, giving a receipt signed by two witnesses. Lists to be sent in duplicate to the Secretary at War on fine of £10. Persons hindering fined £5. First warrants to be returnable 18 March 1707[-8]. Lond. Gaz. 4418. 26 February. ^ This copy is the one signed by the Privy Council of Scotland ; original of Scots proclamation. I

summary: For apprehending the person who has taken the Title of James the Third, &c
abstract: The person who has taken the style and title of James the Third, King of England, and James the Eighth, King of Scotland, has undertaken an invasion with French troops in violation of the Queen’s title to the Crown and the Succession Acts. He is attainted by 13 William III and is to be apprehended. All popish recusants to return home and stay there. All Papists to leave London by 1 1 March. Repeats the Proclamations for disarming, &c.. Papists, as Procl. 26 February 1701, No. 4286, q.v. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4416. 8 March.

title: A Declaration, Requiring all Officers and Soldiers to Observe strict Discipline, and for Payment of their Quarters. St. James’s: 17 March 170f
abstract: The forces will pay their quarters at the usual rates wherever they pass. They are not to be trusted beyond. No disorders or threats to be raised. Publication to be made by beat of drum on arrival. Officers to punish disorder on pain of cashiering, &c., if redress refused complaint to be made to Commander-in-Chief. No game to be disturbed, no quartering in a private house. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4420. 18 March. ‘ Copy signed by Privy Council of Scotland. Ifo

summary: For apprehending James Ogilvie and others, landed from the French fleet
abstract: James Ogilvie the younger of Boyn and others are landed from a French fleet threatening invasion in Scotland. They are to be apprehended for high treason. No one is to aid or conceal them. A suitable reward will be paid. B.L. Lond. Gaz. 4421. 24 March. * Copy signed by Privy Council of Scotland, with order to publish and print 29 March. Ifo

title: A Proclamation, For Dissolving this present Parliament, and Declaring the Speedy Calling of another. Kensington: 15 April
abstract: Lond. Gaz. 4428; C.J. xviii. 571. Priced. 20 April.

summary: For calling a new Parliament
abstract: Refers to Prod. 15 April [No. 4444, q.v.]. Writs will be issued ‘Teste 26 April’ returnable Thursday, 8 July. Lond. Gaz. 4430. Priced. 23 April.

summary: For pardoning all deserters who return to their duty
abstract: Certain soldiers have deserted and withdrawn themselves, whereof some have been apprehended and sentenced to death. All deserters who return to their duty before 20 June next and those already apprehended will receive a free pardon, and are not to be called in question for it in future. Lond. Gaz. 4435. P.B.O. Original Priced. 11 May.

title: A Proclamation, Appointing the Distribution of Prizes taken, and the Bounty for Taking Ships of War or Privateers of the Enemies. Kensington: 20 May
abstract: By Act of last Session the officers and crew of any ship of war or privateer have full property of any lawfully condemned prize, and above that a bounty of £5 for every man in the prize’s crew at the beginning of the engagement. Prizes taken in America also belong to the officers and crew. The ‘ neat proceed ’ is to be divided into eight equal parts. Three-eighths to the captains, if a flag officer is present he has one-eighth of three-eighths ; the marine captains, sea lieutenants, and master one-eighth; the marine lieutenants, boatswain, gunner, purser, carpenter, master’s mate, chirurgeon and chaplain one-eighth ; the midshipmen, cai-penter’s, boatswain’s and gunner’s mates, corporals, yeomen of the sheet, coxswain, quartermaster, quartermaster’s mates, chirurgeon’s mates, yeoman of the powder room, and serjeants of marines one-eighth ; the trumpeters, quarter gunners, carpenter’s crew, steward, cook, armorer, steward’s mate, cook’s mate, gunsmith, cooper, swabber, ordinary trumpeter, barber, able seamen, ordinary seamen, volunteers by letter, and marine soldiers two-eighths. Lists of the crew at taking of prizes to be sent to the Admiralty. Agreements between owners and crew of privateers valid. Shares of ‘ dead ’ and ‘ run ’ seamen unclaimed for 3 years to be paid to Greenwich Hospital, who are to have lists of Navy agents. Lond. Gaz. 4440. Price Two Pence. 27 May.

summary: Touching the trade to Newfoundland, and encouraging the same
abstract: Recites Act 10 and 11 Wm. Ill for the Newfoundland trade, which on address of Parliament is to be enforced. All subjects have liberty to fish at Newfoundland and go on shore for curing, &c., fish, making oil, and cutting wood for repairing stages, train fats, ships, &c. No alien to take any 1708-9; 7 Anne bait or fish. After 25 March no ballast to be emptied in the harbours. No person to destroy any stage, &c. The first person to enter any Creek after 25 March to be Admiral of the Creek, the second the Vice-Admiral, and the third the Bear- Admiral. Inhabitants who have taken any beech, &c., that formerly belonged to fishing ships since 1685 are to give them up to public use before 25 March. No beech to be taken before the arrival of the fishing boats from England, &c. Persons who have built since 1685 may enjoy the same. No by-boat keepers to meddle with fishing conveniences. Every such master to carry two fresh men to sea (one first voyage, one second). Every fishing boat to carry one fresh man in five. No marks are to be cut out of boats, &c. No person to rind trees. The Admirals to keep a journal of all ships, &c., in their harbours. Differences to be settled by the Admirals. Appeal to the commanders of ships of war. Kot. Pat. p. 3. n. 1. d. Lend. Gaz. 4452; see C.J. xv. 644, 648.

summary: Prohibiting Plays, Interludes, Gaming, &c., in May Fair
abstract: A patent for a fair was granted 20 July, 4 Jas. II, under Great Seal to be held at May-Fair in Great Brookfield in the parish of St. Martin’s in the Fields. The Grand Jury of- Middlesex have presented it because, instead of booths for goods, they are built for plays, interludes, and puppet shows, gaming, and other disorderly pastimes, encouraging vice and hindering trade. No plays, shows, gaming, musicmeetings, or other disorderly assemblies to be allowed. Officers to put down disorder. Lond. Gaz. 4536. 29 April.

summary: Suspending the Recruiting Act
abstract: Tuesday, 22 November, is appointed a day of general thanksgiving in England for the victory at Blaregnies, near Mens, in Hainault, under John, Duke of Marlborough. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 4597. 6 October. Ifo

title: A Proclamation, For Putting the Laws in Execution against Forestalling, Regrating, and Engrossing of Corn
abstract: Cites Acts 5 & 6 Ed. VI and 5 Eliz. These Acts and all others are to be enforced in view of the recent rise in the price of corn. Licences to be granted sparingly. All offenders to be prosecuted. Dalk. 2 (311). Lond. Gaz. 4605.

summary: For further pi’oroguing Parliament
abstract: Parliament, now prorogued to Thursday, 6 October, will meet on Tuesday, 15 November, when all members are to attend. Lond. Gaz. 4597. Priced. 6 October. U"®

summary: For a General Thanksgiving
Enforcing Recruiting Act

abstract: Robert Balfoui*, Master of Burleigh, being convicted and sentenced to death for the murder of Henry Stenhouse [see Scotland] has escaped out of the Tolbooth at Edinburgh on 1 January. £200 sterling for his apprehension. This is to be proclaimed and printed. Kot. Pat. p. 6. n. 1. d. Lond. Gaz. 4647. 28 January.

abstract: Wednesday, 15 March, is appointed a day of public fast through England, &c., for pardon and blessing. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 4655. 20 February.

summary: Changing dates for Assizes
abstract: The days for holding the Assizes fixed by the Judges are deferred. The prefixions of the Justices are now published. (Follow the dates for the six circuits.) Lond. Gaz. 4664. Gratis. 16 March.

title: A Proclamation,
summary: All Seamen to repair to their Ships
abstract: London : Ass. : 17[09-]10. All seamen are to repair to their ships by 23 March next. Deserters returning by that date shall not be punished. Those who are apprehended after shall suffer according to law. Lond. Gaz. 4655. 20 February.

title: A Proclamation, For a Publick Thanksgiving
abstract: Tuesday, 7 November, is appointed a day of public thanksgiving in England for the late victory in Spain [Almenara and Saragossa] and elsewhere. Archbishops, &c., to compose a form of prayer. Lond. Gaz. 4750. 28 September.

title: A Proclamation, Requiring Quarantain to be Performed by Ships coming from the Baltick Sea. Hampton Court: 9 November
abstract: 1. All ships from the Baltic to keep 40 days Quarantain, to begin from the time of anchoring in the appointed place. 2. These places for Thames-bound ships to be Standgate Creek on the S. shore of the Medway, opposite to the Isle of Grain, Sharpfleet Creek, and the Lower-end of the Hope. 3. No person or goods to be landed in that time. 4. If after Quarantain there is a clean bill of health, cargo may be landed, except linen, Polonia-wool, hog’s-bristles, spruce yarn, feathers, hemp, and flax, for which order will be taken. 5. Goods imported from Baltic to be landed at Stowfort Island in the Medway and in other ports as ordered. 6. Ships receiving people or goods under Quarantain must undergo it themselves. 7. Persons employed in the hold for taking iron, tar, pipe-staves, timber, &c., from hemp, linen, &c., there to undergo a new Quarantain. 8 and 9. Captains of ships of war and customs officers to enforce Quarantain. Lond. Gaz. 4769. Priced. 14 November.

abstract: arrgant, his 2) of 3) within 4) man thys The Queen wishes to make known the ‘ presompteuos, arrgant, fellonios, rebellios, & trayteros, deads of Shan Onell ’, and * her gratius & mercyful proceding with him ’. He did not come to the Council called in 1556 against mac Connell. In 1557 he delayed joining the expedition against James mac Connell, and when he came he left again after two or three days. In 1558 he was reinstated in loyalty by Sir Henry Sidney. On the news of the death of Queen Mary he murdered his brother, Baron of Dungannon, and dispossessed his father, making himself be proclaimed Oneil. He was summoned to Council in 1559, but refused to come without sureties, Sir W. Fitzwyllyams, Sir Henry Radclif, Sir George Stanley, Marshall of the Army, and Chief Justice Plunket. On coming to Dundalk he swore peace. In 1560 he again refused obedience, and now maintains a traitor, Archbishop of Armagh, and other proclaimed traitors. He is therefore proclaimed traitor. title: SMITH.] The offer and order giuen forth by Sir Thomas Smyth Knight, and Thomas Smyth his sonne, vnto suche as be willing to accompanye the sayde Thomas Smyth the sonne, in his voyage for the inhabiting some partes of the Northe of Irelande
summary: London: 1571
abstract: Tho. Smith, Jun.1 Thomas and place The Queen has granted to Sir Thos. Smith, Knt. and Thomas his son all lands her Majesty’s by inheritance in the country called the Ards and adjacent countrys in Earldom of Ulster, if they can possess them. To those who will help them to possess the land they offer as follows : — To each foot soldier, one plowland of 1 20 Irish acres of arable land, for which Sir Thos. and Thos. S. must pay the Queen 2d. Irish for an Irish acre (24 foot to the pole). The soldier is to pay to Sir Thos., Thos., and their heirs Id. sterling for eveiy English acre (16^ foot to the pole). The first payment to be made 4 years hence, viz. 1576. To each horseman, 2 plowlands (240 acres Irish) which is at the least 500 acres and more English, paying for every English acre as the footman doth. Each footman and horseman, after the arable land is divided, shall have also pasture, meadow, wood and such like necessary. The charge to be paid by a footman, if he be furnished with sufficient armour for a pike, halberd or caliver, with a convenient livery cloak of red colour or carnation with black facing, is .£10 for his victualling and transportation for one whole year, after which time there is hope to find enough provision in the country. The charge of a horseman well horsed and armed for a light horseman with a staff and a case of dags is £20 for victual of him and his horse for 1 year. His cloak of the same colour as the footman’s, in the fashion of the Dutch riding cloaks now used. To avoid ills arising (the Flixe, &c.) from lying uncovered on the ground, on payment of 10s. by a footman or 20s. by a horseman they shall be lodged under canvas and upon beds until houses are found. Those who cannot adventure themselves may pay for a substitute and have the land apportioned, for a footman paying £16. 13s. id. and in proportion to this rate if they desire more land. Any doubting may see the Letters Patent at the sign of the Sunne, in Pauls Churchyard. He may pay his money there to Thomas Smyth, Junior, who adventures in person, or the Treasurer, who will also take payment in kind according as they are needed. 1 MS. signature.

summary: Against the Earl of Desmond and his confederates
abstract: beene her 2) their Seale The Earl of Desmond and his confederates have stated that a new conquest of Ireland and extirpation of the Irish is in contemplation. This is untrue, and the Queen will pardon all concerned except the ringleaders excepted by the Lord Deputy. All subjects are to withdraw from these traitors. Those who come in within 10 days will be pardoned. Rebels will be followed up with fire and sword. The Queen will not allow any subjects to be oppressed or hindered as long as they are obedient. The offence of rebellion, and submission to a foreign and strange potentate being greater than her Deputy may pardon, the Queen has caused this Proclamation to pass the Great Seal, and it has thus the legal force of a Pardon under Great Seal. But any persons may have particular Pardons under Great Seal of Ireland.

summary: Concerning a new coinage and the rate of exchange
abstract: 1601-3 : 43 45 Elizabeth & 1 James I Nos i62_8 To prevent the export of coin, a special Irish coinage of Is., 6d., and 3d. of silver, the Queen’s arms and style on one side, a crowned harp with Posui Deum adjutorem mcum, and copper pence, halfpence and farthings. These coins are to pass immediately at their face values. On and after 10 July no other money is to pass. Exchanges are opened at Dublin, Cork, Galway, Carrickfergus, London, Bristol, and Chester. English money delivered in Ireland will receive a bonus of 6d. in the £ or 18d. on a pound weight payable in England. Irish money will be valued at 1 9s. in the £ payable in England. English money payable in Ireland at 21s. for every £ received in England. Base current coin will be exchanged at face value. Acts against transporting money to be strictly enforced, especially 1 9 Hen. VII. Hot. Pat. Ire. 16 Jas. I. p. 5. d. (Abs. p. 418) ; Rot. Pat. Eliz. Ire. m. 8. summary: Natives to pay the fourth sheaf on planted lands
abstract: Cites recent proclamation announcing that natives might remain on their old lands till May last, paying 20s. English for every quarter of land, and then to depart. They are allowed to reap their crops this half-year, paying 40s. for the half-year ending Allhallowtide [ 1 Nov.], or if much corn is growing, the fourth sheaf. This order not to prejudice any agreement already made. L. Carewe, Treasurer, Marshal, [Sir] Oliver Lambert.

title: A Proclamation declaring the royal care to have the estates of the undertakers preserved in peace, and the strict command laid on the servitors on their behalf

summary: Enforcing certain laws

B. M. Lansd. 159. 269. '

summary: For the rate of wages

In summer half : 2d. master, 1 \d. journeymen, ,1 d. prentice more; gardeners, 8 d. or 1 6d. ; paviors, 1 \d. per yard paving without food. Candles 3 \d. per lb. Rules as to markets, throwing ashes into the street, keeping swine. Turf to be sold forty for Id.

opening: The Complaints lately exhibited vnto Vs by certaine
summary: Approving the Deputy of Ireland
abstract: Certain noblemen complaining of the government of Ireland have been heard by the King in person, and select commissioners have been sent there to make inquiry. This has encouraged them to speak disrespectfully of the King’s Deputy. Though not finally deciding every question raised, the King justifies him in every respect, and will punish any contempt of him. Inferior ministers found in blame will be corrected and punished. P.C. (235). Queen’s 79. A. 2 (237) ; 79. A. 5 (2).

opening: Forasmuch as divers persons in this
summary: Concerning wine licences
abstract: 01. St. Iohn. Owing to the failure of the Deputies of Sir George St. Poll and Sir Henry Yelverton for granting licences for selling wines and aqua vitae the agreements with them are void, and in some cases new licences are granted. All who have had agreements may have them confirmed by the new Deputies on payment of the fine, during one month. After that date mayors, &c., are to shut the doors of all who have not taken out new licences. Copies under the hand of Clerk of Council to be authentic. Youghal 46. If0

title: An Act of State forbidding Spiritual Persons to grant long leases. Dublin : 17 March 1616
abstract: Cites proclamation 21 Oct. 1609, No. 197, q.v. Forbids any spiritual person to make a lease of any ecclesiastical or corporate property for more than 21 years. Any such lease may be brought into Chancery and cancelled. Granters to be punished by royal prerogative. This to be proclaimed. Thomas Dublin, Cane., Armagh, H. Docwra, Geo. Midensis, To. Caufield, 01. Lambart, Jo. King, Dud. Norton, Fr. Annesley.

opening: Whereas the Kings most excellent Maiestie by his Letters Patents
summary: Registering Births, Deaths, Marriages
abstract: vn- Baptismes, 2) 3) cer- Highnes His Majesty hath ordained that all Births, Baptismes, Marriages, and Burialls shall be entered and enrolled from time to time, and for that purpose appoints Sir George Keir to the office of Public Registrar in Ireland. He is to take 6 d. from the parents of every child baptized, 6 d. from every married couple, and 6d. for every burial, to be received by the parson, vicar, curate, or other minister for him. Four deputies appointed, at Dublin for Leinster, at Ardmagh for Vlster, at Corke for Munster, and at Galway for Connaught. Thom. Dublin, Cane., Armagh, Will. Tuamensis, Arthure Chichester, D. Thomond, Ge. Midensis, Edw. Brabazon, Ger. More, Rich. Boyle, 01. Lambert, Burley, Char. Wilmott, Arthure Savage, Henry Docwra, Will. Iones, Dom. Sarsfield, William Methwold, Fr. opening: Whereas the Brittish Vndertakers of the late escheated lands within the province of Vlster
summary: Irish to depart from plantations in Ulster
abstract: The British undertakers are bound by the terms of their letters patents not to plant a mixed plantation of Irish and English, but only of English and inland Scots. As there are a large number of Irish who still reside upon the lands given to planters, His Majesty commands that before the 1st of May next ensuing they shall remove with all their belongings. If they still continue, to be fined 10s. sterling; and if they continue after that, to be fined as the Lord Deputy and Council shall think fit. 1 Deputy printer.
signed: Prosaid Highnes, Oliver Saint Iohn, Thom. Dublin, Cane., Edw. Brabazon, Arthure Sauage, Henry Docwra, Will. Iones, Will. Methwold, Fr. Aungier, Henry Power, Iohn King, lames Hamilton, Dud. Norton, Franc. Annesley

opening: Although this Realme of Ireland hath now for the space of fifteene yeares and vpwards
summary: Against Usury
abstract: vpwards, cessine Highnes Although the country has been peaceful so long, and trade has grown, yet there is great usury, owing to the scarcity of money in this kingdom. The Act made in 3 Hen. VII against usury is strictly to be enforced. This does not apply to mortgages, &c., already paid up, and if within six months after date of this proclamation the mortgagers accept the principal sum of money, it will not apply to them either. Youghal 55.
signed: Oliver Saint Iohn, Thom. Dublin, Cane., Arthure Sauage, Henry Docwra, Will. Iones, Will. Methwold, Fr. Aungier, Henry Power, Iohn King, lames Hamelton, Dud. Norton, Fr. Annesley

I, granted the office of Post Master General to John, Lord Stanhope of Harrington, and also by Proclamation from Greenwich, 15 May, 7 Jas. I, No. 1078 Eng., q.v., forbids using disavowed messengers. Lord Stanhope being desirous of having a duly authorized person in this kingdom, we have appointed Melchior Yan Pelkem, resident in this city.

opening: Whereas the late Lord Deputie and Councell of this Realme hauing duly considered how that the publicke
summary: Against bringing arms into the kingdom
abstract: considered like 2) Warre, Dublin Refers to Act of Council 10 Mar. 1605, 3 Jas. I, No. 185, q.v., that no shipmaster or merchant or factor was to bring to this kingdom without licence from the Privy Council of England any arms or powder, and ordains that no arms, powder, or furniture for wars, such as swords, &e., be brought in without licence. Corporations and towns to state how much powder and munitions they have.
signed: Oliver Saint Iohn, ■ Brabazon, Chari. Wilmot, Will. Iones, Toby Caulfield, Henry Power, Iohn King, Dud. Norton

opening: Whereas the Kings most excellent Majestie
summary: Concerning leases at Athlone
abstract: Quotes royal letter 22 April [1618]. The rents of Athlone and its tithes, fishing, &c., and of the abbeys of the dissolved houses, St. Peter and St. Benedict, were granted to the Lord President of Connaught. Leases are to be granted to inhabitants of the religion of the Established Church of England, by Sir Charles Wilmott, the present Lord President, at rents to be fixed by him and the Lord Deputy to be held in free and common socage. P. R.O. S.P.I. 333 (199'). Certified copy.

abstract: From Procl. 18 July 1621 [No. 284, q.v.].

summary: Concerning the late erected staple for wool
abstract: Grievances having arisen with regard to the late erected staples, it is proclaimed lawful for any person to buy wool for Irish manufacture without belonging to the staple ; any one may be admitted to the Company of Staplers without fine ; no one to ship wool or woolfells except by the staple. Youghal 70 ; see Cal. S.P.I. p. 252.

opening: Whereas the Kings most excellent Maiestie by his Highnesse Letters Patents vnder the great
summary: Patent to F. Kingston & T. Downes
abstract: The patent granted to John Franckton of the office of Printer-General of Ireland to print all books, &c., is now granted to Felix Kingston and Thomas Downes, citizens and stationers of London, assignees and patentees, for and on the behalf of the Company of Stationers of the said city, to the intent this kingdom might be supplied with all manner of lawful books, at easier rates than hitherto. There is daily brought into the kingdom all manner of books, to the prejudice of the said Company. We order therefore a fine of 10s. Irish to be paid for every book thus brought in.
signed: Oliver St. Iohn, Adam Loftus, Cane., Brabazon, Gar. Moore, Charles Wilmot, Arthur Sauage, Henry Docwra, Geo. Shurley, Dominick Sarsfield, Bleuer Hayset, Francis Aungier, Iohn King, Fr. Annesley

title: A Proclamation concerning Alehouses. Dublin : 3 March 1620
abstract: Ireland, charge 2) comthe Refers to a late Act by Deputy and Council touching ale-houses, imposing a tax of 10s. 6 d. upon every person licensed. His Majesty has revoked this Act, and by royal letter, 20 Jan. 1620-1, directs that every person licensed shall pay 3s. 6 d. English yearly while licensed, and appoints a Licensing Bench for every county, to meet yearly between 1 April and last day of June. Every one licensed to have some sign, stake, or bush, to give notice to travellers where they may be entertained. Clerk of the Peace’s fees fixed. Printed licence forms. Youghal 75.
signed: Oliver Grandisone, Adam Loftus, Cane., La. Dublin, Bx-abazon, Gar. Moox-e, Arthur Sauage, Henry Docwra, Geo. Shurley, Dominick Sarsfield, I. Blexxer Hayset, Fi'ancis Aungier, Fr. Annesley, Tho. Roper

title: A Proclamation concerning the Commissioners proceedings
abstract: Majestie, and We * The Commission appointed by His Majesty to remedy civil and ecclesiastical errors, which arrived here in April, sent to the King a certificate containing certain propositions in June. The Privy Council of England has returned them to us with His Majesty’s approbation for enrolment in Chancery. They are to be put in force. These reforms will be printed.
signed: Adam Loftus, Cane., Ki. Powerscourt, Ch. Wilmot, Hen. Valentia, Brabazon, To. Caulfield, Fr. Aungier, Fra. Blundell, Ge. Shurley, Dud. Norton, Fra. Annesley, Fran. Ruisshe, I. King, Ad. Loftus

abstract: and of Giuen Requiring the payment of admeasurement money and other fees and charges concerning the plantations of lands escheated in the Counties of Leitrim, King’s Co., Queen’s Co., Westmeath, Longford, and Ely o Carroll, which were given partly to undertakers, partly to natives.
signed: Adam Loftus, Cane., Ri. Powerscourt, Ch. Wilmot, Hen. Valentia, Brabazon, Fra. Blundell, I. Blever Hayset, Dud. Norton

title: A Proclamation concerning the payment of his Majest. revennue
abstract: ready into pre- All revenue to be paid to the Court of Exchequer here and no other place. Speedy payment of arrears of rent, &c., to be made.

title: A Proclamation for the banishment of wandring Scottish-men
abstract: sort uen at In view of the extraordinary resort of the meaner sort of Scots to this kingdom, disturbing the plantations in the North, and leaving their own places, the King ordains all persons, under the degree of known landed gentlemen, to have a certificate from the Commissioners of the Middleshires of Scotland (sometime the Borders of England and Scotland). Orders for extradition of criminals and others fled out of England and Scotland.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Ri. Powerscourt, Hen. Valentia, To. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Fr. Aungier, Will. Iones, Fra. Blundell, Ge. Shurley, I. Blenerhayset, Dud. Norton, Fra. Annesley, Cha. Coote, Tho. Roper, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation for Farthing Tokens
abstract: Farthings having been found to benefit trade in England, His Majesty orders them to be established here likewise, prohibiting the use of other tokens. They are to be made of copper, having on one side two sceptres crossing under a diadem, on the other side a harp crowned with Iacobus Dei gratia Magnae Britaniae, Franciae, et Hibcrniae Rex, and to be made and uttered by Edward Woodward, Esquire, and Thomas Garret of London, Goldsmith, and their executors and assigns. To be distributed in Dublin, 20s. for 20s. worth of tokens, and taken back at 20s. for 21s. worth of tokens. Ruding ii. 378.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Cha. Wilmot, Hen. Valentia, To. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Aungier, Will. Iones, Fra. Blundell, Ge. Shurley, I. Blenerhayset, Dud. Norton, Fra. Annesley, Tho. Roper, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation against transportation of Corne
abstract: high of thought No wheat, rye, barley, ‘ beare ’, oats, or any other corn or malt made in this realm to be taken out of it. No licences to be used, and no master, owner, or mariner belonging to any ship, &c., to transport any such corn.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., La. Dublin, Thomund, Cha. Wilmot, Hen. Valentia, Gar. Moore, I. Clandeboy, Brabazon, To. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Fr. Aungier, Lau. Esmond, Cha. Coote

title: A Proclamation concerning certaine orders to be observed for the prevention of the dearth of Corne and Graine
abstract: impoverishing such Giuen 1. J. P.’s in every county to find out how much corn and grain each man has in his barn, and what is not required for his maintenance to be taken and sold in open market. 2. No one is to be allowed to buy in the market to sell again. 3. No engrossers or forestallers to be permitted. 4. J. P.’s and officers to portion out the country among themselves. 5. To report once every twenty days to the sheriff of the county. 6. To send up those who refuse to be searched to appear before the Council. 7. To carry out these orders and to send up any recommendations they have.
signed: Heniy Falkland, Hen. Valentia, Fra. Blundell, Geo. Shurley, I. Blener Hayset, Dudly Norton, Tho. Roper, Roger Iones, I. King, Edw. Trevor

title: A Proclamation concerning Iron Ordnance, &c
abstract: 1623-4 : 21 James I His Majesty having been solicited by the members of both Houses of Parliament of England to prevent the transporting of iron ordnance, no one after the last of July is to erect any furnaces, or use any furnace for making iron ordnance or bullets, and no one is to transport ordnance, bullets, sows, or iron oare, or any iron, other than bars of iron wrought with the hammer.
signed: Henry Falkland, Hen. Yalentia, Brabazon, Fra. Blundell, Ge. Shurley, I. Blener Hayset, Will. Parsons, I. King

title: A Proclamation prohibiting the vse of Logwood. Dublin: 13 January 1623
abstract: Kingthis Maiesties Henry Falkland. Logwood is found to be of no use for dyeing, and its importation is stopped. Any logwood coming into the country after the feast of Midsummer next will be seized and burnt ; sheriffs and officers to take special precautions for the discovery of those who use it in dyeing.
signed: Adam Loftus. Cane., Cha. Wilmot, Brabazon, Fr. Aungier, I. Blener Hayset, I. King

title: A Proclamation for the Banishment of Iesuites and Priests &c. Dublin: 21 January 1623
abstract: hauo established twen- Henry Falkland. To remedy the abuses caused by Jesuits and seminary priests, &c., proclamations have been issued : ‘ some by immediate warrant from his Maiestie out of England, and others by authoritie of the Lord Deputie and Councell. ’ . . . All titular Archbishops, Bishops, Vicars generall, Abbots, Pryors, Deanes, Jesuites, Fryers, Seminary Priests, and other Priests, are to leave the kingdom forthwith or within forty days, on pain of displeasure, &c. Any such person or his receiver is then to be committed to prison. Provided that any such person conforming and repairing to church duly and orderly may remain in the kingdom.
signed: Adam Loftus, Cane., Hen. Yalentia, Fra. Aungier, Fra. Blundell, Geo. Shurley, I. Blener Hayset, Dudly Norton, Fra. Annesley, William Parsons, Roger Iones, I. King, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation concerning the Planters in Vlster. Dublin : 21 January 1623
abstract: The Privy Council by letters, dated 12 December last, order proclamation to be made commanding the planters of escheated lands of Ulster, viz. Cavan, Fermanagh, Armagh, Tyrone, Londonderry, and Donegal not to expel the Irish nor allow any to settle or leave for the present.
signed: Adam Loftus, Cane., Hen. Valentia, Fra. Aungier, Fra. Blundell, Ge. Shurley, I. Blener Hayset, Dudly Norton, Fra. Annesley, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, I. King, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation prohibiting the sale of Cattell out of Faires or Markets
abstract: Stolen cattle are being sold at butchers’ houses instead of in the fairs ; all butchers are commanded not to buy privately, or on the highways, but only in markets and fairs, or in the houses of such as are known to be honest. No cattle to be driven away from market after sunset, until sunrise the next day.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Charles Wilmot, Hen. Yalentia, Montgomerie, To. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Fr. Blundell

title: A Proclamation concerning the Officers of the Custome-house. Dublin : 27 February 1623
abstract: directions, such Maje- Having received special directions for the removal of the abuses and frauds by which His Majesty’s customs officers defraud him, we command that all seizures or imposts are to be notified by the customs officers in writing to His Majesty’s Court of Exchequer here. Merchandise not to be made up in cask and barrel, except such as shall be marked and sealed according to the late Act of State.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Ri. Powerscourt, Hen. Valentia, Brabazon, Dudly Norton, Tho. Roper, Roger Iones, Cha. Coote, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation touching Weights and Measures. Dublin: 1 March 1623
abstract: Kingsures the There being no certain standard of measures in Ireland as there is in England, we have made a provisional Act of State that before the feast of St. John Baptist there shall be made two measures of a barrel for wheat, rye, meslane, pease, beanes, and other pulse, malt, oats, and barley, salt, coles, herrings, pilchards, and other things usually measured by the barrel, bushel, or peck, and likewise for the measuring of tallow, beere, ale, oyle, and other liquid things, and one measure of a barrel and half-barrel for the packing of salmon: the former measure to contain 4 bushels or 32 gallons, Winchester measure, the measure for packing salmon to contain 42 gallons. Also balances, Troy and Avoirdupois. Clerks of markets alone allowed to sell these weights and measures. No difference to be made in rent or in buying things by water-measure on shipboard.
signed: Henry Falkland, Ri. Powerscourt, Brabazon, Fra. Blundell, Dudly Norton, Will. Parsons, Cha. Coote, Roger Iones, Adam Loftus

issuer: Lord Deputie and Council Op Ireland
title: A Proclamation concerning Warlike Munition, and wearing Mantles, Trouses, and Skeins
abstract: By previous proclamations, No. 185, &c.,q.v.,no gunpowder, fire-arms, or armour (swords and rapiers or their blades excluded) are to be imported without licence of the English Privy Council. Great quantities have been imported, whence deer are killed, and many riots, burglaries, murders, and even rebellion arise. None to be imported without licence. All powder to be brought into the Ordnance Stores. Towns to keep sufficient for defence, notifying the quantity to the Lord Deputy. Noblemen or shipmasters to buy of the stores. No person wearing Irish mantles or trowses to keep muskets. Any nobleman or gentleman of English dress may seize them. No man to wear after 1 August next any mantles, trowses, or long skeines, or allow them to be worn on pain of contempt. No one wearing Irish dress to be admitted to the Council, any Court, or any Magistrate. Sheriffs to break long skeines, and to take off and cut to pieces any mantles or trowses worn in public. They may be worn in the house. Youghal 107.

summary: Against bringing in Arms without licence
abstract: might daily Maiesties As first part of No. 252, q.v. Licences may be granted for import also by the Lord Deputy and Council. Does not deal with Irish dress. Youghal 97.
signed: Henry Falkland, Hen. Valentia, Brabazon, Fra. Blundell, Dudly Norton, Will. Parsons, Roger Jones

title: Tythes, Offrings and other Ecclesiastical! duties to be taken hereafter by the Incumbents, of the severall Churches in the sixe Escheated Counties of Vlster
abstract: Border double columns * Marriages, oblations and offrings, clarkes wages, christnings, purification of women, burials, mortuaries, corne and hay, wooll, lambe, kid and pigges, foales, milk, calfes, butter, and cheese, egges, geese, firres, and turffe, woode, priuy tithes, apples, hempe and flaxe, hops, wood, hony, waxe, and conyes, fish, gardens, milnes.’ Tithes and Ecclesiastical duties only on these things above mentioned are to be taken, and none others, in the said Counties, for any cause, custom, pretence or challenge whatsoever, as the several incumbents will answer to the contrary at their perils.
signed: Henry Falkland, Brabazon, Fr. Blundell, I. Blener Hayset, Dud. Norton, Tho. Roper, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, Iohn King, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation forbidding the export of pipe staves. Not found. See Cal. S.P.T. p. 66

summary: Proclaiming Charles I
abstract: God dingly. Ma- His Majesty by the death of his father becomes King. He is already proclaimed in England, and sends orders to be proclaimed in Ireland. We declare him our only lawful, lineal, and rightful liege lord. Youghal 103 ; see Cal. S.P.I. p. 4.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Rich. Powerscourt, Tobie Caulfield, Henry Docwra, Franc. Blundell, Dudly Norton, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, Iohn King

summary: The King’s Proclamation to his people
abstract: by Prince Maiesties Henry Falkland. King James having died on Sunday, 27 March last, His Majesty succeeds him, and promises to be just to his subjects ; accordingly they are to be obedient to him. Youghal 104.
signed: Adam Loftus, Cane., Rich. Powerscourt, Tobie Caulfield, Henry Docwra, Franc. Blundell, Dudly Norton, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, Iohn King

title: A Proclamation signifying his Majesties pleasure, That all men being in office of Gouernment at the decease of his most deare and most Royall Father King lames, shall continue till his Majesties further direction
abstract: vnto preiudice Maiesties Continuing in office all presidents, lieutenants, &e. Youghal 104.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Rich. Powerscourt, Tobie Caulfield, Henry Docwra, Franc. Blundell, Dudly Norton, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, Iohn King

title: Lawes, and Orders of Warre, established for the good conduct of the seruice of Ireland
summary: Dublin
abstract: Enconcerne. 2) vponthe discre- Henry Falkland. Forty-six rules for military discipline. ‘ We require the Marshal of the Armie, the Iudge-marshall, the Captaines of Horse and foote in his Maiesties pay, and all other his Maiesties Officers in this Kingdome whom it may concerne, to obserue these Lawes, and to see them put in due execution from time to time. Published the 1 1. day of Iune. 1625. Henrie Falkland.’ Youghal 109.

summary: Against bringing in Arms without licence
abstract: by kearnes not- Another issue of No. 253, q.v.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Lane. Dublin, Chari. Wilmot, Dom. Kinsale, Henry Docwra, Francis Aungier, George Shurley, Adam Loftus

summary: For the issue of warrants to purchase gunpowder
abstract: by money Dublin, His Majesty furnishes powder and arms out of his own magazines at the same prices that it is issued to the army. We have chosen the best qualified persons in all parts of the kingdom, reserving Leinster to ourself, and authorized them to grant warrants to the clerks of the several stores to deliver powder and arms, according to certain instructions given to them by us. Stores : Dublin, Duncannon, Cork, Limerick, Athlone, Galway, Newry, Castle of Monaghan, Carrickfergus, Mountioy, Londonderry. Youghal 118.
signed: Henry Falkland, Persons : Lord Deputy, Lord President, Clanrickard, Sir Thomas Rotheram, Lord Blayney, Lord Caulfield, Sir Edward Treuor, Sir William Caulfield, Charles Paynes, Esq., Sir lames Ireskine, Sir Daniell Leigh, Sir William Stewart, Sir Arthur Basset, Lord Dyllon, Lord Balfoure, Sir Paul Goare, Sir William Cole, Sir Iohn Vaughan, Sir Ralph Bingley, Sir Basill Brookes, Captain Iohn Samford, Sir William Windsor, Sir Francis Cooke, Tristram Berrisford, Sir Moses Hill, Sir Hugh Clatworthy, Sir Hercules Lanford, Viscount Montgomerie, Viscount Claudeboy, Marmaduck Whitchurch, Esq, Ric. Powerscourt, Cha. Wilmot, Dom. Kinsale, Tob. Caulfield, Henry Docwra, Law. Esmond. Dud. Norton, Arth. Tyringham

summary: Against keeping Markets on the Sabbath
abstract: not straightly Ire- Markets are kept weekly on the Sabbath Day in Swords and Lusk, co. Dublin, and in other towns. This is strictly forbidden. All goods offered for sale are to be confiscated, and distributed by the vicars of the town churches for the maintenance of poor scholars or relief of the poor. All sheriffs, &c., to aid, and to publish this proclamation. Youghal 116.
signed: Henrie Falkland, Cha. Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Fr. Aungier, Dud. Norton, Iohn King, Ad. Loftus

summary: Quarantine Orders. Plague in London
abstract: verie Citie 2) for Ireland, In consequence of the plague in London no person is to land at any port without leave from the chief officer, on pain of fine and imprisonment. Leave not to be given till the ship is visited, and the ports from whence she comes and the health of the passengers known. If any persons or wares come from infected or suspected places the wares must be aired for thirty days and the passengers for twenty days. Two houses of wood to be built near Dublin, one for wares, the other for passengers, at the charge of the Fermors of the Customs. Passengers to be provided with meat, drink, lodging, and other necessaries. All other ports to erect two similar houses at the expense of the Fermors of the Customs. No victualler to receive persons from overseas without licence. Ward to be kept in all cities and towns against persons from overseas. Customs officers to take information of ports on oath from shipmasters and others. Youghal 115.
signed: Henrie Falkland, Lancelot Dublin, Cha. Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Dud. Norton, Iohn King, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation for the banishing of idle and wandring persons
abstract: Scotstraightly first. Cites Proclamation 21 Sept. 1622 [No. 241, q.v.]. No Scotsman without lawful business, under the degree of known landed gentleman, is to come to Ireland without a licence from the Commissioners of the Middle Shires, &c. Any Scotsman landed since 10 April last to leave the kingdom within forty days. Shipmasters not to land them on pain of £5 fine, half to informer, and imprisonment. Justices, &c., to imprison strangers. Fugitives from justice to be apprehended and sent back to England or Scotland.
signed: Henrie Falkland, Rich. Powerscourt, Chari. Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Dud. Norton, Roger Iones

title: A Proclamation for the forbidding of Drouers and Butchers to driue Cattle by night, and against buying of any Cattle out of Fayres and Markets
abstract: this of Scotland, As No. 249, q.v.
signed: Rich. Powerscourt, Chari. Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Dud. Norton, Roger Iones

title: An Act of State touching Beggers and wandring persons
abstract: Houses of Correction to be built by Quarter Sessions before 20 Oct. next. Beggars, chapmen, common-rymers or bards, without licence from two Justices to be arrested, whipped naked from the waist upwards till blood comes, and sent to their parish with a testimonial giving the date of the whipping. Dangerous rogues to be banished overseas by the Council. Constables not enforcing the law to be punished by Quarter Sessions. Shipmasters bringing in rogues, &c., to be fined £5, half to informer. Regulations as to jurisdiction. Shipwrecked mariners with a testimonial not to be interfered with. Children under seven and glasse-men of good behaviour exempt. This to be proclaimed.
signed: Henrie Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Rich. Powerscourt, Charles Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Henry Docwra

title: A Proclamation for publike Fasting and Prayer
abstract: England, mandement Lord A weekly fast to be kept on Wednesday for the plague in England. Preachers to preach a sermon. Bishops to send a prayer or prayers to every minister as some of the Cleargie cannot preach.
signed: Henry Falkland, Lancelot Dubl., Rich. Powerscourt, Chari. Wilmot, Tob. Caulfield, Henry Docwra, Fr. Aungier, Dud. Norton, Iohn King

title: A Proclamation for the due administration of Iustice to all his Maiesties Subiects in his kingdome of Ireland
abstract: The Deputy and Council Table in Ireland are not to take cognizance of private causes between party and party, which are to be proceeded with in the ordinary Courts of Justice in the kingdom. Justice is to be equally distributed there to all His Majesty’s subjects without respect of persons. C.J.I. i (1). 177 (17 Feb. 1640-1).

title: A proclamation to forbid the Subiects of the Realme of Ireland, to haue any Trade or Commerce within any the Dominions of the King of Spaine, or the Arch-duchesse. Dublin: 9 January 1625
abstract: and Archof Cites English Procl. 24 Dec. 1625, No. 1458, q.v. This proclamation is to be published by order of Privy Council of England, 29 Dec. No one is to trade with Spain or the Arch-duchess.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Fr. Annesly, William Parsons, Dud. Norton, Thom. Roper, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation concerning the payment of his Maiesties Revenues and Rents into the receipt of the Exchequer
abstract: of with day Assignments of rents and casualties have been made in the hope of stimulating early payment of them into the Exchequer. This has not happened, and no assignments will be made after 29 September next. Severe measures will be taken with tenants not paying their half-yearly rents before the last day of term. This to be proclaimed. Youghal 125.
signed: Henry Falkland, Adam Loftus, Cane., Henry Docwra, Will. Parsons, Dud. Norton, Roger Iones, Adam Loftus

title: A Proclamation against the transportation of Cattle
abstract: of chants Delinquents Henry Falkland. No cattle are to be exported from 10 October next to 1 April on pain of confiscation and fine. Searchers are not to let them pass on any pretext. Reward to informers. The price of meat is too high, and ‘ slaughter time in this kingdome approacheth Youghal 127 ; Cal. p. 159.
signed: Tob. Caulfield, Hen. Docwra, Will. Parsons, Roger Iones, Adam Loftus
