abstract: Orders a fast on Thursday, 3 May, in view of the pestilence; quotes Isaiah lviii. 3. Mayor of Dublin to give notice.

title: A Declaration concerning the Fines to be imposed on the Delinquent English and Brittish Protestants of Munster
abstract: Refers to Order of 1 Jan. 1654[-5], No. 491, q.v. The delinquents have neglected to furnish particulars of their estates. All who submitted before 1 Dec. 1649 and have clear estates in land of .£400 and more (in 1638) or £8,000 goods and chattels at present, and all who remained with the rebels, having estates of £50 per ann. or goods, &c., of £500 are before 10 June to bring in particulars of their estate now and in 1638, to the Commissioners General at Cork-House, Dublin. Every person within the proclamation who neglects this is to be fined two and a half years’ value of their real estate in 1638, and one-eighth their personal estate, to be paid in two equal moieties on 1 August and 1 February next to James Standish, Esq., Receiver-General. In default estates to be sequestered. This to be printed and published.

title: A Declaration, That all Irish Papists l-emaining within Dublin and two Miles of the Line about the same, after the 20 of June next, are to remove thence, and the Cabbins to be pull’d down
abstract: 1655 : 7 Commonwealth N°s 556-64 Irish papists who have not proved their good affection are to leave Dublin, &c., before 20 June next. Those that refuse shall be sent to Connaught. None are to return to Dublin. The governor and mayor are to destroy all cabins. The laws of England in force against unlawful games, rogues, vagrants, &c., to be enforced. Any persons giving evidence of their change from popery to the protestant religion unto Dr. Winter, Col. Markham, Edward Roberts, Esq., Aid. Hutchinson, Aid. Preston, Aid. Cliff, Mr. Rob. Chambers, Mr. Tim Avery, Mr. Iohn Price or two or more of them may remain. This to be printed and published.

title: A Declaration, That all persons holding Custodiums or Leases from the State, and have or do entertain Irish Papists as Tenants therein, are to forfeit their Leases
abstract: Arras 175 the tence General, By instructions 3 February 1652[-3] leases of waste lands were granted to soldiers for five years with the proviso of keeping one-third the land in corn, and other lands for seven years, provided they planted English tenants on them. It appears that Irish rebels and papists have been settled on many of these farms. In future all leases under which Irish papists are tenants are made void and of no effect. Provisions for execution of the order. This to be printed and published. P.E.O. Dub. Minute Book 52 (20 April).

summary: Regulations for licences to Irish servants
abstract: Type headpiece the Whereby to By order of 17 July 1654, No. 531, q.v., all Dublin, Wicklo, Wexford, and Kildare, and part of Catherlagh north of Barrow, to be cleared of Irish papists 1 May 1655. The protestant proprietors have petitioned that some might remain to help in farm labour. Licences may be granted on the motion of protestant employers by (Dublin and Wicklo) Sir Hardress Waller, Col. Hewson, the Mayor of Dublin, Col. Theophilus Iones, Col. Ponsonby, Aid. Hutchinson, William Dixon, Esq. : (Wexford) Lt.-Cols. Brett, Puckle, and Overstreet, Capts. Abel Warren, and Camby, Mr. Hussey ; (Kildare) Sir Paul Davis, Sir Robert Meredith, Sir Iohn Hoey,Col. Hewson, Col. Theophilus Jones, Aid. Hutchinson, Aid. Tygh, Maj. Meredith, Maj. Morgan, Mr. Dixon, Robert Hall, Gent., Capt. Sands ; (Carlo) Col. Pretty, Capts. Bennet, Stopford, Preston, and William Rydout, gent. Licences to run to 20 October, specifying particulars of the person. Irish recusants must not live near bogs, &c., or in scattered houses, &c., &c. This to be printed and published. On 19 October Sir Hardress Waller, Sir John Reynolds, Col. Hewson, and Maj. Morgan to report as to advisability of modifications possible.

summary: Commission of Trial for tories and other Irish rebels
abstract: A reissue of No. 545, q.v., expiring 1 August.

summary: Appointing 5 July a day of humiliation
abstract: With Declaration 25 May [see No. 3049, England] and instructions for collection. This to be printed and published. £1097. 6s. 3d. collected.

title: A Declaration and Commission for three Months Assessment of Ten thousand Pounds by the Month; Beginning the 12th of July 1655, and Ending the 12th of October following

summary: For i-emoving and preventing some mistakes in government
abstract: Ale-houses, profanity, illegal imprisonment, refusal of bail, illegal distress, transportation and assumed jurisdictions, sheriffs’ exactions, blank warrants, no workhouses, letters of favour, &c., are common. Judges of Assize to inquire and punish. Justices of Peace to do their office. Sheriffs to proclaim.

summary: Enforcing Proclamations as to Transplantation
For letting the Commonwealth property
abstract: Cites instructions from Lord Protector as to letting bishops’ lands, &c. All persons wishing to rent such to apply before 1 0 August with full particulars to the commissioners of revenue. Sheriffs to publish.

summary: For a statement of unsatisfied Arrears of Pay
abstract: Lays down the way in which officers and soldiers who have served the Commonwealth of England in Ireland are to make out and authenticate their statements of arrears, which will be sent to England for passing, and debentures issued after in Dublin. This to be printed and published.

summary: Extending the time for compounding for estates
Irish not transplantable to gather into villages
abstract: In consequence of the outrages committed by the tories who find shelter in the scattered dwellings of the Irish all Irish not transplanted into Connaught and Clare are before 20 August next to draw themselves into villages and townships of at least thirty families, more than half a mile at least from any shelter for tories. They are to appoint a headman, tithing man, or constable, who is to see the cattle brought in every night, and a watch set.

title: A Declaration concerning Priests
abstract: Hot found. Thos. Herbert. The Declaration against priests, No. 509, q.v., to be revived.

summary: Taking off restraint on export of provisions
abstract: A free trade and export of commodities would tend to the public good, so that the restraints put by the late commissioners on the export of tallow, butter, hides, beef, pork, and cattle are removed, merchants paying the usual duties.

issuer: Council for the Affairs of Ireland
title: A Declaration And Commission for Three Months Assessment, Of Ten thousand Pounds by the Month ; Beginning the 12th of October 1655, and ending the 12 of January following
abstract: Assessment on thirty-three counties and county towns. This to be printed and published.

summary: Rewards for arrest of tories
abstract: In view of the murders, &c., committed by the tories the following rewards are offered for the persons or heads of their leaders: £30 for Donnogh o’ Derricke commonly called blind Donnogh, £20 for Dermot Ryan, £20 for Art McKreen otherwise called Kavanagh, £5 for James Leigh, £5 for Kelly, and 40s. for any other tory if brought in by a countryman, 20s. if by a soldier.

opening: It is ordered that all Rents and all fee farms
summary: Rents, &c., to be paid into Exchequer by 10 November
abstract: All crown rents, ecclesiastical rents due 29 September last and not paid, are to be paid in to the receipt of the Exchequer by 10 November. Officers of Exchequer to attend and give quittances. Process to be issued against defaulters. This to be printed and published (October 30).

summary: Concerning sons and heirs of unfriendly proprietors
abstract: A Declaration to be prepared for the sons, brothers, and next heirs of proprietors (that have not manifested their constant good affections) to transplant into Connaught and Clare by the 1st of March next (save those of the county of Dublin) who are to be ordered to remove forthwith.

opening: When Wee reflect upon the great
summary: For a fast on 8 November
abstract: Cites Deut. xxxiii. last verse and Ps. cvii., and the sufferings of the Protestants of Savoy. A fast to be kept on Thursday, 8 November, for direction to the Lord Protector in foreign affairs, and a blessing on home undertakings.

opening: Whereas by reason of the late Wars
summary: Resumption of the Receipt of the Exchequer
abstract: The receipt of the Exchequer is again open at the Exchequer Chamber in Dublin. All tenants and farmers to bring in the rents and dues for the half-year ending Michaelmas by the fourth day of Hilary Term. This to be proclaimed by the sheriffs. Merc. Pol. p. 5827.

title: For a solemn fast on 3 April
opening: Whereas His Highness for the reasons expressed
abstract: Cites Declaration, No. 3069, Eng., q.v. A fast to be held on Thursday, 3 April and 17 April. Mayor and sheriffs to give notice. No fairs, markets, &c., to be held or servile work to be done.

issuer: His Highness the Lord Protector’s Council for the Affairs of Ireland
summary: Prolonging the Court of Claims at Athlone
abstract: Many claims are yet undetermined by the dilatoriness of the transplantable persons in prosecuting their claims. The court is allowed to receive all claims up to 20 May next and no more. Inhabitants of Cork, Youghal, or Kinsale, who admitted Sir William St. Leger, and who have continued faithful are exempted, but must prove it. This to be proclaimed, and a return of the proclamation made to Athlone. This to be printed and published.

issuer: His Highness the Lord Protector’s Council for the Affairs of Ireland
opening: Whereas it hath been by many
summary: For discovery and punishment of Jesuits, &c
abstract: Notwithstanding previous Declarations the Jesuits and seminary priests still remain. All mayors, &c., are to search them out and imprison them. The receivergeneral to pay on conviction £5 for every Jesuit or priest, £2 for every harbourer. The informer shall also receive 20 marks from the goods of any popish recusant in the parish where such Jesuit or priest is arrested. This not to apply to any recusant willing to attend public worship or informing. Order to print and publish.

issuer: His Highness the Lord Protector’s Council for the Affairs of Ireland
summary: Against Dish who turn tories or woodkerns
abstract: Since Dermot Ryan and others in county Carlow have betaken themselves to fastnesses and uninhabited places no mercy will be shown to tories and woodkerns. This to be printed and published.

issuer: His Highness the Lord Protector’s Council for Affairs in Ireland
summary: Means for the conversion of the Irish
abstract: [2 ff.] Gothic letter. Quotes Declaration of 17 July 1654, No. 531, q.v., and 23 [sic] May 1655, No. 558, q.v., ordering transplantation. Any one who conforms and takes the abjuration may remain. They must abjure papal supremacy, transubstantiation, purgatoiy, and salvation by works. Persons between eleven and twenty must speak and use English only within a year. All under twelve must be taught English. Proprietors are exempted from this benefit. All Irish within 4 miles of a meeting to attend every Lord’s day, within 6 miles every second at least, further, once a month at least. Children to learn the catechism in English. No Irish to be spoken. 2000 of Mr. Bristowe’s catechism printed in June 1657 (Council Minute Book 48).

issuer: His Highness the Lord Protector’s Council for the Affairs of Ireland
opening: For the better destroying of Wolves
summary: Rewards for the destruction of wolves

title: A Proclamation for a day of thanksgiving
abstract: 5 Nov. to be a day of thanksgiving. The narrative of the defeat of the Spanish fleet to be printed with this order. 200 copies printed.

opening: Whereas divers persons have taken leases
summary: Rents for Commonwealth lands to be paid
abstract: Commonwealth rents for lands in Leinster payable at 25 Dec. to be paid to receivers of the precincts. Order of 13 March 1655[-6] cancelled. This to be printed and published.

title: A Proclamation of Grace to the Tories
abstract: 1656-8 : 8-9 Commonwealth

opening: Forasmuch as many evills do dayly
summary: Enforcing laws against vagrants, ale-houses, &c
abstract: The following Acts are to be printed and published : 33 Hen. VIII, c. 15, Vagabonds ; 10 & 11 Chas. I, c. 4, Houses of Correction: 10 & 11 Chas. I, c. 15, Ale-house Keepers; 11 Chas. I, c. 16, Cosherers ; 15 Chas. I, Ale-house Keepers in Dublin. All justices, &c., to execute them. All Judges of Assize, &c., to give them in charge at their Courts, and inquire as to their execution, reporting to the Council.

summary: For a day of thanksgiving
abstract: Cites Declaration 2 Feb. Friday, 27 February, to be a day of thanksgiving in this nation (20th in Dublin) for the preservation of the Lord Protector. Sheriffs to distribute this declaration to all ministers.

title: A Declaration for putting Irish out of port towns, walled towns, and garrisons. Dublin : before 2 March 1656
abstract: All popish recusants, proprietors and others, dwelling in port towns, walled towns or garrisons, who did not before 15 September 1643 and ever since profess the protestant religion are to remove themselves and their families at least 2 miles away from them before 20 May.

summary: Abolishing transplantation to Colonies
abstract: All orders and licences granted to any persons whatsoever (being now in force) to take up and carry to the West Indies idle and vagabond persons be henceforth made void and null, and it is referred to the care of the Justices of the Peace of the several counties and to the governors of the several precincts and garrisons in this nation that the execution of all such orders be for the future forborne.

title: A Declaration concerning the observation of the Lord’s Day
abstract: An order for it to be printed and sent to the sheriffs to be dispersed and observed accordingly.

title: A Proclamation. Publishing Proclamation of Lord Protector
abstract: Publishing Proclamation, No. 3082, Eng., q.v. Has been printed.

title: A Declaration concerning the Coin
abstract: An order to take this into consideration (Nov. 25).

summary: Appointing Judges for the Court of Claims
abstract: Cites Act for attainder of rebels in Ireland where claims on estates (other than in the eleven counties) are to be entered and prosecuted by 1 June next, before judges appointed by the L. Deputy and Council. The following are appointed : Sir John Temple, Master of the Rolls, Sir Robert Moreby, Chancellor of the Exchequer, Mr. Justice Donnellan, John Sankey, and Thos. Fowler, Esq. All persons to take note.

opening: To the end, faithful and painful
summary: Concerning the appointment of Ministers
abstract: No person to be admitted as a public preacher unless approved by the persons named in the Ordinance for approbation of public preachers, or having a testimonial from two or more godly able ministers of the Cospel. Merc. Pol. p. 366.
signed: Henry Cromwell, W. Steel, Cane., R. Pepys, Miles Corbet, Matthew Thomlinson, William Bury

title: A Proclamation concerning Gunpowder. Dublin : 17 January 1657
abstract: ‘ The proclamation concerning gunpowder to be continued, the title, by the Lord Deputy, or Lord Deputy and Council, disjunctive.’ 300 to be printed.

summary: Reports on ministers and schoolmasters to be made
abstract: Cites Ordinance 23 June 1654. As many ejected persons from England and Scotland have intruded into Ireland, the Justices of Peace at their next meeting are to peruse the list of ministers and schoolmasters allowed by public authority N°s 595-605 in their country and to report the names and abodes of all persons who preach or teach schools without such authority, that authority may be given them or they be removed. This to be printed and published.
signed: Thomas Herbert, W. Steele, Cane., R. Pepys, Miles Corbet, Math. Tomlinson, William Bury

opening: Whereas in and by an Act
summary: All transplanted persons not in Connaught, &c., to be arrested
abstract: Cites provisions of Act for removing certain persons and their families to Connaught and Clare. The Acts are to be enforced. All transplanted or transplantable persons found in Leinster, Ulster, or Munster are to be arrested. If any Jesuits or priests are found the names and examinations are to be sent up at once to the Lord Deputy. This to be printed and published. K.I.D. N. 1. 27 (11).
signed: Thomas Herbert, Henry Cromwell, W. Steele, Cane., R. Pepys, Miles Corbet, Math. Thomlinson, William Bury

title: A Declaration concerning Wolves. Dublin: 11 February 1657
abstract: To be renewed from the determination of the former, No. 581, q.v., and to be continued to the first day of January next. Print.

title: A Proclamation for the levying and payment of Excise. Dublin : 10 March 1657
abstract: Referred to in Order of 9 June, No. 599, q.v.

summary: Concerning the export of Wool
abstract: Enforcing laws against export of wool, except to England and Wales. Collectors to take bonds of double the value that it will be landed in England.

title: A Declaration for encouraging the discovery of concealed lands
abstract: Referred to in orders of 15 December 1658 and 10 Feb. 1658-9.

title: Proclaiming Richard Cromwell Lord Protector
abstract: Richard Cromwell proclaimed at Dublin 10 September. W. Steele, Cane., R. Pepys, Miles Corbet, Wm. Bury. Merc. Pol. p. 841. Ordered to be printed and published. The patent roll is copied from a print by Bladen. jjo qqj

summary: A Proclamation for continuing in Office
abstract: Publishing proclamation of 4 Sept., No. 3100, Eng., q.v. Rot. Pat. Ire. (1658) p. 7. m. 2. Order to print and publish. Patent roll copied from a print by Bladen.

title: A Declaration concerning popish priests
abstract: Order to print and publish forthwith, and that 600 of them be printed.

summary: Public Peace to be preserved
abstract: London reprint. apprehenother Du- To prevent public disturbance soldiers are to return to their quarters, unlawful assemblies are to be stopped, and no engagements, &c., are to be signed. This to be proclaimed to the people and the troops. This to be printed and published. MS. date 25 May. Printed at Dublin by W. Bladen.

summary: Shipmasters to bring return cargoes of coal
abstract: Shipmasters coming to Dublin for cattle were formerly used to bring in cargoes of coal. This custom has been neglected, but is to be enforced, and customs officers are to take bonds from them to do so before clearing ships.

title: A Declara- * tion of several Officers of the Army in Ireland, on behalf of themselves and those under their Commands, holding forth their steadfast resolutions to adhere to the Parliament in defence of its priviledges ; and the just Rights and Liberties of the People of these Nations as Men and Christians
abstract: sinful the Declaration Six resolutions: (1) to adhere to the restored Parliament as promised by Lieut. -Gen. Ludlow, their Commander-in- Chief ; (2) to remain united ; (3) to support a godly, learned, and faithful ministry ; (4) to suppress disturbers ; (5) not to impose on tender consciences ; (6) to protect adherents. Twenty-two signatures, headed by Sir Hardress Waller. Pub. Int. p. 979. Printed at Dublin by special order. MS. date 29 December. U°

title: MONK. A Letter from Gen. Monck in Scotland, to the Commissioners of Parliament in Ireland, Touching his present Actings. For the Commander-in-Chief of the Forces in Ireland, to be communicated to the rest of the Officers of the Army there
abstract: pleased and that Acknowledges a letter of the 4th inst. The army is engaged to the Parliament. A few officers cannot be entrusted with the power of abolishing laws, raising money, choosing generals, &c. Desires successive parliaments and a Council of State on legal foundations. The Parliament to be restored and to put a term to itself. ‘ Dublin. Printed by order.’ MS. date 29 December. 1 At Angel in Cornhill.

title: A Declaration of Sir Hardresse Waller, Major General of the Parliament’s Forces in Ireland, and the Council of Officers there
abstract: ex- Lord after Tuesday, 3 January 1 659[— 60] for Dublin, and Tuesday, 17 January for the rest of Ireland to be a day of thanksgiving [for the return of the Long Parliament]. 1 (218). Firth. Merc. Pub. p. 1014. Printed at Dublin by special order, W. Bladen.

title: A Declaration by The Major-General and Council of Officers in Ireland, concerning their late Actings there, and for the Tryal of such Officers and Souldiers as finde themselves agrieved for being laid aside
summary: Dublin
abstract: Authohorrid give Condemns the action of the English army under Lieut. -Gen. Fleetwood. A certain number of officers were laid aside then. Any officer aggrieved may appeal before 24 March to be tried by court martial. Dr. Ralph King to be judgeadvocate in Dublin. (Signed by twenty-five officers.) Printed at Dublin by W. Bladen. 0Q8.

title: BY THE MAJOR GENERAL OF THE PARLIAMENTS FORCES IN IRELAND, with the advice of the Council of Officers
summary: For arrest of messengers from Duncannon
abstract: behim or Lieut.-Gen. Ludlow, charged with high treason, is endeavouring to gather troops round him at Duncannon. All persons coming out of Duncannon are to be seized and sent to head quarters, unless they have a pass from the officer commanding for parliament.

title: A Declaration of the Lord Broghil and the Officers of the Army of Ireland, in the province of Munster. Cork: 18 February 1659
abstract: Declares for a free Parliament, including those sitting on 11 October 1659 and those excluded in December 1648, except any who have been in arms against Parliament. Forty-four signatures, headed by Brogliill. Tlmrloe Papers, vii. 817 ; Merc. Pol. p. 1187. ]y°

title: To Our Trusty and Well-beloved General Monck to be by him communicated to the President and Council of State, and to the Officers of the Armies under his command
abstract: ever Force published Appeals to Monk, whose armies have complied with their obligations. Encloses a Declaration to be published. Refers to the evils of successive revolutions, and hopes God will inspire him to his duty. Sir John Green vil brings this. Belfast Town Book, p. 85.

title: The Declaration and Engagement of the Army and Forces in Ireland
summary: Adhering to the English authorities
abstract: Sine nota [Dublin : W. Bladen]. by several to Will acquiesce cheerfully in the decisions of the Council of State or Parliament will determine. Fifty-eight signatures. K.I.D. N. 1. 27 (10). Pari. Intelligencer, p. 259 ; Merc. Publicus, p. 254.

title: A Declaration of the General Convention of Ireland, Expressing their Detestation of the unjust Proceedings against the late King, in a pretended High Court of Justice in England
summary: Dublin
abstract: and der Foun- The people of Ireland have not met since 1648. They repudiate the High Court of Justice, the death of the King is murder, contrary to the Solemn League and Covenant. This Declaration to be printed and published. Merc. Civ. p. 25, Merc. Pub. p. 290.

title: A Proclamation. S Proclaiming Charles II
abstract: Account of ceremony of proclamation, Dublin Records, iv. 572. Pari. Intelligencer, p. 337.

title: His Majesties Letter to his Excellencie the Lord General Monck, to be communicated to the Officers of the Army, brought to his Excellency from his Majesties Court at the Hague, By Sir Thomas Clarges. Hague: 26
abstract: Acknowledges receipt of letter of 5 May by Sir Thomas Clarges. Thanks the army for its affection. Promises protection to them, and will punish any who reproach them for the past. Hopes to be with them soon. Authorization, dated Rochester 24 May 1660, to Henry Muddiman to cause this letter to be printed. George Monck.

title: A Declaration of the General Convention of Ireland For suppression of Tories and Woodkerns
summary: Dublin
abstract: Certain persons called tories and woodkerns daily betake themselves in arms to the woods, bogs, mountains, and rob, burn, kill, destroy, &c., the English and other good subjects. Every person so in arms is a rebel and a traitor. £10 for conviction of every leading tory or woodkern, £5 for every common one, £3 for every aider and abettor or reliever. Payment to be made by the collector of the poll money. This to be printed and published.

issuer: Commissioners for Government and Management Op Affairs in Ireland
title: "Begins] Whereas the Lords of His Majesties most lonorable . . . Continuing Excise, &c., till Parliament meets.]
abstract: By letter of the Privy Council, the collection of excise and custom is to continue at the former rates till after the meeting of Parliament or the arrival of the Lord Deputy and Council, on pain of free quarter. Merc. Pub. p. 636. (Lords Justices appointed 3 Nov.). Tf° 620 a. N°s 621-7

summary: Continuing the Excise and New Impost
abstract: The Convention continued the excise and new impost on 26 May to 29 Sept. The Commissioners for Government and Management of Affairs in this kingdom of Ireland, on 24 Sept, continued it until a new parliament should be called. Arrangements are now being made for drafting bills. The excise, &c., is to be paid, especially as the payment of the army depends on it, which would otherwise have to be met by free quarters. Merc. Pub. p. 28; Kingdom’s Intelligencer, p. 35.
signed: Io. Elect. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Dublin Elect., Montgomerie, Io. Bysse, Hen. Tichborne, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith. Theo. Iones

summary: For the redress of grievances
abstract: The King has ordered us to take order for the church, to open courts of justice with all convenient speed, to put down violent extortions and oppressions by soldiers and others, and to prepare bills for the meeting of parliament. All subjects to be obedient and loyal. Mer. Pub. p. 42 ; King. Int. p. 50. Tf°
signed: Io. Elect. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, la. Donelan, Io. Bysse, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

summary: Summoning the General Convention for 22 January
abstract: By royal letter 1 8 Dec. the General Convention is summoned to meet at the Four Courts, Dublin, on 22 January at 9 a.m. where they formerly assembled. Members to be elected in place of those dead. Protection for members and their servants granted.
signed: Io. Elect. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, la. Donelan, Io. Bysse, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

summary: For hearing grievances as to restitution of lands
abstract: Cites in full royal letter 31 Dec. 1660, giving Justices power to suspend or modify decisions as to restitution of lands. Application to be made to the Justices. Waste on all lands in dispute is to be stopped, and timber not to be cut down or sold. Merc. Pub. p. 44 ; King. Int. p. 52.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Can., Mountrath, Io. Elect. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, la. Donelan, Io. Bysse, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

opening: We the Lords Iustices and Council
summary: Adjourning Hilary Term
abstract: Hilary Term adjourned from Odabis Hilarii to Octdbis Purificationis. Revenue payments as usual.
signed: Io. Elect. Armachanus, Io. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith

summary: Pardon to tories and woodkerns coming in
abstract: Certain tories, &c., John Costegin, Edward Cashen, James Shiren, and others have prayed for pardon, not having shed blood. A free pardon to all tories giving up arms and ammunition on or before 18 February and finding recognizances for good behaviour, for all crimes but murder. Any not coming in by then are proclaimed rebels and traitors. All who aid them are to be committed for trial. Reward for arrest of any tories. Army officers to aid in arrest.
signed: Io. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, Hen. Tichborne, la. Donelan, Io. Bysse, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

title: A Proclamation for a day of Humiliation to be kept and observed on the Thirtyeth day of January 1660, being the anniversary of the Murder of King Charles the First of blessed memory. Dublin : 21 January 1660
abstract: 30 January to be day of fasting and humiliation. All ministers and curates to meet at 10 a.m. and read this Proclamation to their parishioners, and exhort them to loyalty and obedience.
signed: Io. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Michael Boyle, Elect. Cork, Cloyn Ross, Montgomerie, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Arthur Hill, Theo. Iones

opening: Whereas We are given to understand by
summary: Against assemblies of Papists, Presbyterians, Independents, &c
abstract: All assemblies of papists, presbyterians, independents, anabaptists, quakers, or other fanatical persons are illegal whether under the names of days of humiliation, thanksgiving, &c., or no. Bishops, sheriffs, magistrates, &c., to stop them and arrest all persons so assembled. Army to assist. All mayors, &c., to publish this proclamation, which is to be publicly fixed up.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, la. Margetson, Elect. Dublin, Montgomerie, Michael Boyle, Elect. Cork, Cloyn Ross, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

opening: Whereas the Kings most excellent Maiesty
summary: For the currency of certain foreign coins
abstract: Cites royal letter of 30 Nov. as to scarcity of coin. The following coins are made current from 2 February : — Gold. Gold rider 6 dwt. 12 gr. at £1. 2s. 6d. and half-rider; Pistoll, French or Spanish, 4 dwt. 8gr. at 16s., and half, double, or quadruple pistoll ; Ducat 2 dwt. 6 gr. at 9s. ; Spanish suffrain 7 dwt. 2 gr. at £1. 8s., and half-suffrain. Silver. Mexico or Sevil piece of eight, Rix-dollar or Crossdollar, 17 dwt. at 4s. 9 d., and half, quarter, and half-quarter dollars; Portugal royal 14 dwt. at 3s. 8 d., and half and quarter-royals; Ducatoon 20 dwt. 16gr. at 5s. 9 d., and half and quarters ; old Peru piece and French Lewis 1 7 dwt. at 4s. 6 d., and half, quarters, and half-quarters. 2d. allowed for each grain deficient in gold, and 3d for each dwt. of silver. Simon 126 ; Cal. p. 197 ; King. Int. p. 92 ; Merc. Pub. p. 84.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, la. Dublin, Montgomerie, Ioh. Raphoe, Mich. Cork, Jerem. Dunensis, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones, Arthur Hill, M. Trevor

summary: For payment of rents for Adventurers’ Lands, &c
abstract: Rents due for adventurers’ lands, soldiers’ lands, and transplanted persons’ lands assigned to payment of arrears before 5 June 1649, and for grants since 23 October 1641, are to be paid. Only the half-year due last Michaelmas (Sept. 29, 1660) will be demanded. Collectors will be appointed in every county. Docquets will be prepared having in columns the proprietors’ names, denomination of the lands, Irish acreage, English acreage. Rent due (Leinster 3d., Munster 2 \d., Connought 1 \d., Ulster Id. per acre). Commissioners will be appointed to fill these in, in duplicate. The Collectors will then demand these rents, which are to be paid forthwith on pain of free quarter.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Montgomerie, Io. Raphoe, Michael Cork, W. Cawlfield, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones, Arthur Hill, M. Trevor

summary: Commission for ascertaining rents due to Crown
abstract: Cites Procl. 7 Feb., No. 630, q.v. Appoints . . . Commissioners for the county of . . . A meeting of proprietors to be held in each barony and the blanks in the docquets filled in. If the ownership has been changed since 29 May the old owner’s name to be ascertained. Note to be taken of divided ownerships, of church and charitable lands, &c. A table of fees due on payment is given. Bonds to be taken of the collectors. Inquiry as to concealed forfeited lands to be made.
signed: Ia. Dublin, Montgomerie, Ioh. Raphoe, Mich. Cork, W. Cawlfield, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Ia. Ware, Theo. Iones, M. Trevor

summary: Commission for appointment of Collectors of Crown Rents
abstract: Cites Procl. 7 Feb., No. 630, q.v. Appoints . . . Collector for county of . . . To enter in a bond for payment to Sir James Ware of sums collected. A table of authorized fees given. Form of the acquittance to be given. Deductions to be made.
signed: Ia. Dublin, Montgomerie, Ioh. Raphoe, Mich. Cork, W. Cawlfield, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Ia. Ware, Theo. Iones, M. Trevor

opening: Whereas a Committee of the General
summary: Against disturbing adventurers or soldiers
abstract: On complaint of a Committee of the General Convention, and consideration of the Declaration of 30 Nov. last for the settlement of Ireland, the adventurers and soldiers or transplanted persons are not to be disturbed in their lands except by legal process, and if any such have been dispossessed they are to be reinstated. Not to hinder any ecclesiastical or charitable lands to be entered on. Merc. Pub. p. 145 ; King. Int. p. 153.
signed: Ia. Dublin, Kildare, Montgomerie, Ioh. Raphoe, Mich. Cork, W. Cawlfield, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Ia. Ware, M. Trevor

title: A Proclamation for the due and speedy execution of the Laws against Drunkenness, Cursing, Swearing, and Prophaning of the Lords Day
abstract: Cites Proclamation 30 May 1660, No. 3211 Eng., q.v. The laws against drunkenness, cursing, swearing, and profaning the Lord’s day to be put in execution. Justices of Peace not executing them will be removed. Officers to see their soldiers keep the law. No innkeepers, &c., to allow persons to remain in their houses after 9 p.m. except lodgers. Ministers to read this proclamation once a month to their congregations. Merc. Pub. p. 158; King. Int. p. 164.
signed: Ia. Dublin, Kildare, Montgomerie, Ioh. Raphoe, Mich. Cork, W. Cawlfield, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Forth, Ia. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones, M. Trevor

summary: Postponing Escheators’ and Feodaries’ Courts
abstract: Escheators’ and Feodaries’ Courts are to be deferred till the first day of next Easter Term. Ia. Dublin, Montgomerie, Massereene, Mich. Cork, W. Cawlfield, Hen. Tichborne, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones.

title: A Proclamation concerning a Parliament to be held May the 8th 1661
abstract: A Parliament is to be held at Dublin 8 May next. Merc. Pub. p. 237.
signed: Io. Armachanus, Ia. Dublin, Montgomery, W. Caulfield, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Io. Bysse, R. Forth, Ia. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

issuer: His Majesties Commissioners for Executing His Gracious Declaration for the Settlement of Ireland
summary: For ascertaining the debt due to adventurers
abstract: Montgomerie, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Io. Bysse, Art. Forbess, Ia. Ware, 01. St. George, Iohn Cole, Au. Mervyn, la. Cuff, Hen. Warren. K.I.D. (14).

summary: Remitting additional duty on exported oxen
abstract: Bonds for the additional impost of 4s. 8 d. per ox are cancelled, the toll to be only 2s. per head. All persons to take notice of this.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, Ia. Dublin, Montgomery, W. Caulfeild, R. Coote, Hen. Tichborne, Io. Bysse, Theo. Iones

title: IRELAND. A Proclamation
summary: Innocent Papists to put in their claims
abstract: 2 May 1661. They are to send in their claims and proofs at once. Montgomerie, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Io. Bysse, Art. Forbess, Iohn Cole, Ia. Cuff, Au. Mervyn. K.I.D. (15).

summary: Adjourning Easter Term to 13 May
abstract: Easter Term is adjourned to the third return, Mensa Paschae, 1 3 May. Revenue payments as usual.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, Kildare, Montgomerie, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Io. Bisse, Fra. Hamilton, Art. Forbess, Ia. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones, Arthur Hill

opening: Whereas it is a certain truth,
summary: For a day of prayer and fast 2 May
abstract: Ordering a day of prayer and fasting on 2 May for the Parliaments of Scotland, now sitting, England and Ireland to meet 8 May. All incumbents, &c., to preach.
signed: Maurice Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, Kildare, Massereene, W. Caulfield, R. Coote, Hen. Tichborne, Tho. Pigot, Io. Bisse, Fra. Hamilton, Art. Forbess, Robert Forth, la. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Iones

summary: Respecting arrears of pay due to officers
abstract: The D. of Albemarle and D. of Ormond have appointed (2 March 1660-1), under authority of Declaration 30 Nov. 1660, Henry, Yisct. Moor of Droghedagh, Arthur, Yisct. Valentia, John, Visct. Massereene, Francis, L. Angyer, John, L. Kingston, Richard, L. Colloony, Sir James Ware, Sir Theophilus Jones, Col. Arthur Hill, Col. Marcus Trevor, Capt. Robert Fits-Gerald, Sir Robert Newcomen, Barf., Sir Arthur Forbess, Bart., Sir Richard Lane, Bart., Sir Patrick Weyms, Sir George Lane, Sir John Stevens, Sir Audley Mervin, Sir William Flower, Col. Chidley Coote, Col. Francis Fowke, Serjeant-Maj. Thomas Harman, Serj-Maj. George Rawden, Capt. Hans Hamilton, Capt. Robert Ward, Capt. Richard Gething, Brian Jones, Esq., Dr. William Perty, Richard Stevens, James Cuff, Samuell Bathurst, and Aid. Daniel Bellingham, or any five to satisfy arrears due to officers and men before 5 June 1649. Any lands set apart for this purpose are to be vacated by fixed days. The lands will be let on fixed days at various towns from 26 April to 27 May. Improvements made during the holding of the late usurpers’ leases will give the holder a preference for new leases. Holders may supplicate for new leases by attorney. Merc. Pub. p. 257. I^o @43.
signed: Io. Armachanus, Massereene, W. Caulfield, R. Coote, Hen. Tichborne, Tho. Pigot, Io. Bisse, Fra. Hamilton, Art. Forbess, Robert Forth, Arthur Hill

title: A Declaration Of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and the Commons in this present Parliament of Ireland assembled, concerning Ecclesiastical Government, and the Book of Common- Prayer
summary: Dublin
abstract: The laws for the government of the Church by the Book of Common Prayer are in full force and are to be obeyed. Magistrates to act severely against contemners of the Prayer Book. This to be read in all Churches the Sunday after receipt . L.J.I. i. 236 ; Cal. S.P.I. p. 334 ; King. Int. p. 357 ; Merc. Pub. p. 349. 2000 copies printed. jjo (344

summary: Concerning grants under usurped powers
abstract: Persons holding land in virtue of grants from the late usurped powers may hold the same for one year from 1 May 1661 paying the like rents. From a citation in Memoranda Rolls, Ire. 13 C. II. m. 41.

title: The Declaration of the Lords Spiritual, and Temporal, and Commons of Ireland assembled in Parliament, concerning his Majesties intended match with the Infanta of Portugal
abstract: Congratulations on the marriage. Vows of loyalty and thanks for his intentions. This to be printed and published. L.J.I. i. 241 ; Cal. S.P.I. p. 338. 1000 printed.

title: A Declaration and Order of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in Parliament assembled, against the Solemn League and Covenant
abstract: The Solemn League and Covenant ‘ was and is against the Laws of God and the fundamental constitution of this Kingdom’, and is to be burnt in all cities, &c., by the common hangman on the next market day. L.J.I. i. 240, 242; King. Int. p. 362; Merc. Pub. p. 371. 1500 printed.

title: A Declaration of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in this present Parliament assembled concerning the continuation of the Customs, Excise, and New-Impost until the first of September next
abstract: Cites Order of Convention continuing these taxes to 1 J une 1661. They are to be continued till 1 September, as the Bill cannot be returned from England in time. L.J.I. i. 243-5 ; King. Int. p. 361 ; Merc. Pub. 370. 50 printed.

summary: Commissions for finding of Offices Post Mortem deferred
abstract: On petition from committee of House of Lords (18 June 1661) against issue of commissions for finding offices post mortem, their issue is deferred to 29 Sept, next, and all escheators, feodaries, &c., to whom commissions are issued are not to proceed on them till then.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, Corke, Kildare, Meath, Barrymore, Donegall, Drogheda, Montgomerie, Ioh. Clogher, Mich. Corke, Ierem. Dunensis, Kingston, R. Coote, Santry, Rob. Meredith

summary: Continuing the Collection of Crown Rents
abstract: last For their Gives names of collectors and commissioners appointed 16 Feb. on Procl. 7 Feb., Nos. 630, 1, 2, q.v. These are to be receivers of the rent due at Easter last under similar terms.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Io. Armachanus, Corke, Barrymore, Donegall, Montgomerie, Ioh. Clogher, Mich. Corke, Ierem. Dunensis, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Tho. Piggott, I. Temple, Fra. Hamilton, M. Trevor

title: A Declaration Of The Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons in this present Parliament assembled : Concerning the continuance of the Customs, Excize, and New Impost, from the First of September next, to the First of December following
summary: Dublin
abstract: Type headpiece Commons New any The payment of customs, excise, and new impost with the arrears to be continued under the same rules as before to 1 December next. All horses, nags, mares, colts, and garrons of 13 handful high or no more, price £ 7 or less, may be exported, paying 2s. per head. This to be printed and published. 1 Sold by John North.

title: A Declaration Of The Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons in the Parliament of Ireland assembled : F or the speedy raising of Moneys for His Majesties Service
summary: Dublin
abstract: As a poll-bill has been transmitted into England for levying money as recommended by the General Convention 1 March 1660[-l], the moneys intended shall be collected on 10 Sept, and paid to Arthur, E. of Anglesey, Vice-Treasurer of Ireland. Not to regulate the payments made by peerage and clergy of Ireland. This to be printed and published.
signed: John Keatinge, Type headpiece Jureason Temporal

summary: Concerning payment of Crown Rents, &c
abstract: Assignations on overdue crown rents have been made and not paid. Cites Declaration 31 July, No. 651, q.v. All persons who fail in the punctual payment of crown rents, and collectors of customs, excise, poll-money, &c., not paying it in due time will be attached by a pursuivant and brought before the Lords Justices, at a cost to them of 2d. per mile each way, to answer their neglect. This to be proclaimed in all public places and fixed up. 1 Sold by John North. TT°
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Ja. Dublin, Shannon, Francis Augier, R. Coote, Santry, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Arthur Hill

summary: Forbidding the making or vending of copper tokens
abstract: Many people have uttered brass stamps at Id. each, getting for 20 d. worth of brass about 20s. of silver, which it is presumed they have exported owing to the scarcity of silver at present. No one is to use these tokens, except to sell them to the original issuer, at the same rates at which they were issued. No one is to make tokens in future except with royal licence. Simon 127; Cal. S.P.I. p. 401.
signed: Mail. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Ja. Dublin, Francis Aungier, R. Coote, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob, Meredith

opening: Whereas the Kings most Excellent Majesty
summary: As to lodgement of claims
abstract: 3 If. Gothic letter. Cites Proclamation 12 July, No. 3311, England, q.v., and Commissioners’ Proclamation 27 March, No. 637, q.v. All claims not lodged must be sent in with particulars before 15 September next. All subdivisions of unregistered estates must be registered. All officers settled on land must put in the debentures under which they claim it and all other particulars. All transplanted persons must send in their claims and the decree of the Court of Athlone and the settlement of the Commissioners at Loughreagh. If this is not done all these claims will be certified into the Court of Exchequer as failing in default. This to be printed and published. R. Coote, Jo. Bysse, Fra. Hamilton, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, 01. St. George, Ric. Lane, Tho. Brown.

summary: For apprehending Halsey and Butler
abstract: . . . Halsey and Walter Butler have been on their keeping in Waterford and Tipperary, stealing, ravishing, burning houses, and murdering. They and all that adhere to them after 20 September are rebels and traitors. None are to aid them. A suitable reward will be paid for their apprehension. Army and other officers to assist.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Shannon, R. Coote, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Edw. Massey

summary: For discovery of concealed lands
abstract: Divers adventurers and others have taken into possession more land than they are entitled to. Every person who by 30 November discovers this to the L. Chief Baron of the Exchequer and proves it shall have a custodiam of the lands at a moderate rent.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Shannon, R. Coote, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Edw. Massey

summary: Against issuing copper or brass tokens
abstract: A reissue of proclamation 17 Aug., No. 653, q.v. Sir Thomas Armstrong has the sole right of issuing tokens, by patent under Great Seal of England. Simon 128 ; Cal. S.P.I. p.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Ja. Dublin, Jo. Bysse, Paul Davys, Drogheda, Shannon, W. Caulfield, Ja. Ware

summary: Concerning officers’ leave of absence
abstract: Two commissioned officers must always be kept with each troop, and at least one with each company. Any officer absenting himself from duty (even if he has leave) when there are not sufficient officers left shall be proceeded against according to the rules and articles of war.

title: A Proclamation Concerning Gun-Powder and Munition
abstract: Cites previous proclamations against import of gunpowder and munitions. Disaffected persons have privately brought in great quantities. No gunpowder is to be imported or bought without licence. A reasonable quantity may be bought by responsible persons. Any gunpowder now owned by private persons to be given up. Every person of honest behaviour and conformable to the English fashion of apparel to arrest importers of powder, and to seize the powder for the King. A reward of half its value given.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, W. Caulfeild, Ja. Donelan, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith

title: A Proclamation Concerning Gun-Powder
abstract: Cites recent Proclamation, No. 659, q.v., against import or sale of gunpowder. Instructions are now issued for the sale of powder by government. Instructions. Cites Proclamations of 1625, No. 253, q.v., and 1635, No. 309, q.v. Gunpowder is sold every day between 9 and 11 a.m. at 20s. English per lb. The licence to buy gunpowder issued free, 6d. fees. Fowlers allowed ; three to a noble, two to a knight, one to a gentleman of £200 English per annum. Fowlers to be known protestants. The names of the persons authorized to give licences follow.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, W. Caulfeild, Ja. Donelan, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith

summary: Fire arms not to be worn while travelling
abstract: No one except Members of the Board, of Parliament, or of the Army, to wear fire-arms when travelling or in any garrison. All such arms to be seized and sent into store. This to be in force till 5 December next. King. Int. p. 743 ; Merc. Pub. p. 747.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Drogheda, Hen. Midensis, Shannon, W. Caulfeild, Santry, R. Coote, Ja. Donelan, Jo. Bysse, Paul Davys, J. Temple, Ja. Ware

summary: Continuing Collectors of Crown Rents, &c
abstract: Cites Proclamation 29 June, No. 648, q.v. The collectors (names given) are continued for the half-year’s dues ending Michaelmas 1661. A list of their duties and the returns they have to make. One shilling in the £ allowed for collection.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Drogheda, Hen. Midensis, Shannon, W. Caulfeild, Santry, R. Coote, Ja. Donelan, Paul Davys, J. Temple, Ja. Ware

summary: Continuing Declaration as to Excise
abstract: Publishing Declaration 31 July, No. 650, q.v. This is continued till 31 Dec. unless Parliament otherwise directs when it meets. Ja. Dublin, Hen. Midensis, W. Caulfeild, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Rob. Meredith. 1 Sold by S. Dancer, Bookseller in Castle Street.

summary: Concerning the payment of Crown Rents
abstract: Cites Proclamation 15 Aug., No. 652, q.v. The army needing money urgently, this must be ‘ declined ’ at present. The auditor-general to certify what new quit rents are unpaid, and the commissioners what inland excise. Acquittances to be prepared for these sums and distributed for satisfaction of warrants for two-thirds of the pay of disbanded soldiers, and for insolvent assignments duly certified. All other revenues except quit rents and inland excise to be paid in to the Exchequer. Table of fees payable.
signed: Ja. Dublin, Hen. Midensis, R. Coote, Ja. Donelan, J. Temple, Robert Forth, Rob. Meredith

title: A Declaration Of The Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in this present Parliament assembled, concerning the continuance of the Customs, Excize and New-Impost, from the last day of November last, to the 25. day of March following
abstract: 7 December 1661. 1661]. Continues payment of excise, &c., from 30 Nov. last to 25 March 1662. Repeals provision as to customs on exported horses. This to be printed and published. C.J.I. i. 464 ; L.J.I. i. 282 ; Cal. S.P.I. p. 476.

opening: Whereas for sundry good Causes and
summary: Proroguing Parliament till 21 January
abstract: Parliament is prorogued until Tuesday, 21 January next.

summary: Concerning an apprehended conspiracy
abstract: Recites letters from Thomas Ash, Alexander Jepson, Capt. Hy. Morton, and Stafford Lighthouse, enclosing a letter from Dublin 18 Nov. 1661 from James Dermot, priest or friar, to James Feilam, popish priest at Kildalky, Co. Meath, containing treasonable and suspicious expressions, quoted at length. On the address of a Committee of Parliament to us on 7 December at 8 p.m., being then in Council, we, after consideration, order all persons transplanted to Connaught or Co. Clare to return thither before 31 December on pain of arrest. The army has been warned and the garrisons strengthened. L.J.I. i. 284; C.J.I. i. 465-6; Cal. S.P.I. p. 476; King. Int. p. 813; Merc. Pub. p. 820. U°
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mountrath, Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Hen. Midensis, W. Caulfeild, Ja. Donelan, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Rob. Meredith

issuer: His Majesties Privy Council of the Kingdom of Ireland
summary: For the arrest of James Feilam, a popish priest
abstract: Type headpiece dipublick answer Recites letter of 18 Nov. 1661 from James Dermot, popish priest, to James Feilam, priest at Kildalky, who has escaped. He is to appear at the Council Board at Dublin on 7 January next. He shall have a safe conduct for all other matters than this letter. £100 reward will be paid for his apprehension between 7 January and 7 February.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, R. Coote, Santry, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith

summary: Proroguing Parliament until 20 February
abstract: Parliament further prorogued until 20 February next.

summary: Concerning complaints as to the Double Poll
abstract: Complaints have been made of the manner of raising the double poll authorized by the Convention 1 March 1660[-l]. All the duplicates of books delivered to the collectors of pollmoney to be sent in to the Receiver- General on pain of proceedings against them. These duplicates are to be taken round to the Judges of Assize, who are to hear and examine all complaints against the collectors, and proceed by law against all offenders, certifying their action to the Council.
signed: General exacting Cir- Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Ja. Dublin, Hen. Tichborne, Ja. Donelan, J. Temple, R. Coote, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith

summary: Parliament prorogued until 4 March
abstract: Parliament further prorogued until 4 March.

summary: Continuing Collectors of Crown Rents
abstract: Continuing collectors (names given) for the half-year ending Easter next. Usual directions.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Ja. Dublin, Kildare, W. Caulfeild, R. Coote, Santry, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

title: An Act For the continuance of the Customs, Excize and New Impost, to the Five and twentieth day of March next
summary: Dublin
abstract: Typo headpiece payment this ex- Continues customs, excise, and new impost to 25 March next. Steers not more than 2s. per head customs, broad cloth imported, 3s. yard excise ; stuffs or bays, 6 d. yard excise ; horses, 2s. a head export ; salt for fish, 3s. 4 d. per hogshead ; beef, 2s. barrel export. This to be printed and published. L.J.I. i. 293.

summary: For release of imprisoned priests, &c., on bond
abstract: Certain popish priests, friars, Jesuits, and others were arrested in December ; they are to be released on bond to do nothing contrary to law. Bonds to be sent by sheriffs to Council within next two months.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Kildare, W. Caulfeild, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Ja. Donelan, J. Temple, Robert Forth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

title: A Declaration Of The Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in this present Parliament Assembled, concerning the continuance of the Customs, Excize, and New-Impost, untill the Four and twentieth of June, 1662
summary: Dublin
Against export of grain without licence
abstract: Cites Act 12 Ed. IV (Ireland) against exporting grain when price is over 10 d. per peck. No grain is to be sent abroad without special licence. All grain for England or Scotland must be covered by bond for landing at a port there, certificate of landing to be returned in six months.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Massereene, Hen. Midensis, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Ja. Donelan, J. Temple, Art. Forbes, Ja. Ware, Eob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

summary: Against Recusants, Non-conformists, and Sectaries
abstract: Eecusants, non-conformists, and sectaries have been indulged and grown worse for clemency. Past offences against the Act of Uniformity will be overlooked, but from this time forward it will be strictly enforced.
signed: Ja. Dublin, Donegall, Drogheda, Conway and Kilulta, Hen. Midensis, Jerem. Dunensis, E. Coote, Hen. Tichborne, Jo. Bysse, Paul Davys, Eobert Forth, Eob. Meredith, Arthur Hill

title: A Declaration Of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons in this present Parliament Assembled, concerning the continuance of the Customs, Excize, and New Impost, until the 24th day of December 1662

summary: Concerning the export of sheep and deer fells, &c
abstract: Cites Act 2 Eliz. (Ire.) concerning export of fells, and the explaining Act of 1 3 Eliz. These Acts are to be enforced so that English artificers may be encouraged to settle here and work at leather trades. Customs officers, merchants, and tradesmen to take careful heed of their provisions.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Hen. Midensis, Joh. Cloghor., Conway and Kilulta, Massereene, W. Caulfeild, Hen. Tichborn, J. Temple, Ja. Ware, Theo. Jones

summary: Brief for a Collection for Castle-Lyons, Co. Cork
abstract: Robert Brown, vicar, Oliver Parr, Henry Parr, Edward Morly, Dennis Kearny, John Patt, petition that on 11 June 1662 Castle-Lyons was burnt, the men being absent at Fermoy fair, losing 31 dwelling-houses and over £1,500 worth of goods. A collection allowed in all Ireland. This to last 9 months from date.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Robert Forth, Eob. Meredith, Theo. Jones, Arthur Hill

summary: Prohibiting the exaction of ‘ Delinquent-Money ’
abstract: The giving of assignments on rents has been forced on the Lords Justices by the delay in paying crown rents. Some soldiers in collecting rents on assignments drive distresses, quarter on them, and demand delinquent-money or riding money. No officers or soldiers are to demand anything more than the amount named in their assignment, on pain of discharge from the army and further punishment.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Ja. Dublin, Hen. Midensis, Joh. Cloghor., Drogheda, Massereene, Santry, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Eobert Forth, Ja. Ware, Theo. Jones, Arthur Hill

summary: Collectors to perfect their accounts this month
abstract: A list of collectors — for the single poll-money, for the first double poll-mqney, for the second double poll-money, &c. They are to account for their receipts into Exchequer before 30 August. The collectors of quit rents in arrears are to settle before the same date. Commissioners to return estreats before 20 August.
signed: Ormond, J. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Drogheda, Anglesey, Mount-Alexander, Falkland, Massereene, Hen. Tichborne, Tho. Pigot, E. Coote, Fra. Hamilton, J. Ware, J. Temple, Robert Forth, Theo. Jones, Mar. Trevor

summary: For the receipt of Crown Rents, &c
abstract: Recites causes which led to giving of assignments. The evils produced by it. It is to be stopped. Any who fail to pay at the appointed time their dues will be prosecuted with all severity. No assignments shall henceforth be granted. Money must be paid in specie. No further delay than the last day of term allowed. This to be proclaimed in all market towns and fixed up publicly.
signed: J. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Falkland, Mich. Corke, Jerem. Dunensis, W. Caulfeild, Santry, Tho. Pigot, J. Temple, Robert Forth, Rob. Meredith

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General and General Governor Op Ireland
summary: Army Officers to return to their quarters
abstract: Many officers are absent from duty, some in England, some in remote parts of the kingdom. All officers (except members of Parliament) to return to quarters forthwith, and not to leave them without special licence. Chief officers of every troop and company to report any neglect of duty by their subordinates.

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General and General Governor Op Ireland
opening: All persons that shall have occasion
summary: Concerning Petitions to the Lord Lieutenant
abstract: Petitions are to be handed to Sir George Lane, secretary. Answers may be expected four days later at the office under the Council Chamber, near the Custom House. Petitioners are not to come to the Castle, or unseasonably solicit the secretaries.

summary: Mexico Pillar Pieces to pass current
abstract: Cites Procl. 29 Jan. 1660[-1], No. 629, q.v. Piece of Eight, Mexico or Civil, Rix Dollar, or Cross Dollar, 17 dvvt., at 4s. 9 d., half, quarter, and half-quarter to pass current. The Mexico Plate pieces or Pillar dollars are of equal fineness and greater weight than the Civil pieces, yet they are often refused. They were included in that Proclamation, and are now declared current at the same rates, provided that the whole piece weigh 17dwt. Troy, and the lesser pieces proportionably. Simon 136; Cal. S.P.I. p. 592. jj° Q3gi
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Meath, Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Orrery, Massareen, Anglesey, Conway and Kilulta, W. Caulfield, Kingston, R. Coote, J. Temple, Ja. Ware

summary: Appointing lading and landing places
abstract: Cites Act for settling subsidy of poundage, &c. , as to the times and places of landing, and Act for excise to same effect. Landing places fixed at Dublin, Wexford, Rosse, Waterford, Dungarvan, Youghal, Cork, Kinsale, Baltimore, Limerick, Galway, Sligoe, Killebeggs, Londonderry, Colerain , Ballitra, Carickfergus, Donoghadee, Strongford, Dundalk and Carlingford, Drogheda. Commissioners of excise may allow pilchards, gross goods, or merchandise to be landed elsewhere.
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Meath, Ossory, Orrery, Massareen, Anglesey, W. Caulfield, Kingston, R. Coote, Conway and Kilulta, J. Temple

summary: Against waste on Adventurers’ Lands
abstract: Repeats order of 9 Jan. 1660[-1], No. 624, q.v., as to waste and cutting of wood on adventurers’ and soldiers’ lands.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Orrery, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Conway and Kilulta, Massareen, Shannon

title: A Proclamation Appointing the Time for putting in of Claims
abstract: Cites Act for execution of the settlement. All claims under the Act are to be put in within 31 days next after the 6th of October.

title: BY HIS MAJESTIES COMMISSIONERS, Appointed for putting in Execution An Act of Parliament, Intituled An Act for the better Execution of His Majesties Gracious Declaration for the Settlement of His Kingdome of Ireland, and Satisfaction of the several Interests of Adventurers, Souldiers, and other His Subjects there. Kings Inns,
abstract: 3 If. Gothic letter. Cites Proclamation 23 Sept., No. 689, q.v. Gives notice of the form of claims to be sent in. The attorneys that will be heard are Ralph Merry, Samuel Bull, Walter Scudamore, Robert Golborne, George Lambert, George Ryder, John Humphrey, John Coghlan, Dominick Dean, Gilbert Fitch, Tho. Heron, George Milner, Tho. Lloyd, Robert Pain, Samuel Mosley, John Brampton, Robert Pugh, John Moland, John Barber, Seaming Phillips, William Westley. King. Int. p. 685 ; Merc. Pub. p. 685. U°
signed: Henry Coventry, Edward Dering, Ri. Raynsford, Tho. Beverley, Edward Smith, Edward Cooke, W. Churchil

opening: Whereas by one Act of Parliament
summary: Enlarging periods for claims
abstract: Under the Act for enlargement, &c., power is given to enlarge the times appointed in the Act for claims, &c. They are now enlarged to 1 April 1663. Times for payments postponed from 1 Nov. 1662 to 15 December 1662. Suspensory powers enlarged to 1 June 1663. This Act of Council to be proclaimed.
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Orrery, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Conway and Kilulta, Massareene, Hen. Tichborne, Dungannon, R. Coote, Kingston, W. Caulfield, San try, Tho. Pigot, Jo. Bysse, Paul Davis, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Arthur Hill

title: A Proclamation For the Suppressing of Unlawful Assemblies
abstract: Cites Procl. 22 Jan. 1660[-1], No. 627, q.v., against unlawful assemblies. Masses have been lately said publicly in Dublin, and conventicles of other sectaries held. The laws must be strictly observed. All dignitaries responsible for seeing that no unlawful assemblies take place in their jurisdiction. All popish pretended clergy or other seducers to be arrested and sent to the Council.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Orrery, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Dungannon, Hen. Midensis, R. Coot, Santry, Jo. Berkeley, Hen. Tichborne, Tho. Pigot, Ja. Donelan, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davis, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones, Arthur Hill

summary: Preservation of game near Dublin
abstract: A reissue of Procl. 3 Aug. 1637, No. 321, q.v., substituting for Naas, the Curragh of Kildare, and for moore-game, hares. Licences for shooting to be obtained from the Master of His Majesties game, or the Lord Lieutenant under bond of £40. No setting dogs to be kept in Ireland.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane. , Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Orrery, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Dungannon, Fran. Aungier, Hen. Midensis, Tho. Pigot, Theo. Jones

summary: Enlarging time for payment of Adventurers’ Rents
abstract: Enlarging time for first half-year’s payments of adventurers’ and soldiers’ rents unto 3 February. An allowance will be made of any surplus if the Commission reduces the rents.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Barrymore, Drogheda, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Shannon, Massereene, Hen. Midensis, Mich. Cork, Fran. Aungier, Tho. Pigot, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General, and General Governor of Ireland
summary: Debts for quarters to be paid
abstract: Any debts incurred for quarters of the troops since 11 February 1 660[— 1 ] are to be claimed in writing from the Earl of Anglesey, Vice-Treasurer, with the tickets of the soldiers to be checked, after which they will be returned till the debts are paid.

summary: Concerning Customs on Foreign and Colonial produce
abstract: Recites provisos of Act for poundage and tonnage as to Navigation Act. Additional duty on silk imported from abroad, half duties on sugar, indicoe, ginger, cotton wool imported from England, rebate only on wines and tobacco imported from England. Aliens to pay double duties of Irish subjects. The following duties lowered for six months (15 Sept. 1662) are continued for a year after, iron value £20 per ton, pays 20s. custom and 20s. excise, silk value 30s. lb. pays 18d. per lb. excise. Plate free of custom and excise. Mercurius Hibernicus (No. 4). 1 Sold by S. Dancer at the sign of the Horse shoe.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Cork, Orrery, Anglesey, Conway and Kilulta, Shannon, Mount- Alexander, Massereene, Henr. Midensis, Jerem. Dunensis, Paul Davys, Robert Forth, R. Meredith, Theo. Jones, Tho. Pigott

summary: Enlarging time for putting in claims
abstract: Cites Act of Council 17 Oct. 1662, No. 691, q.v. Times enlarged for adventurers’ claims, Kildare forfeiture claims, innocent papists’ claims, and for sending in surveys. Sheriffs to proclaim this. P R.O. Dub. 1 (176) ; 1. B. (104) ; 2. A. (65). 1 Sold by S. Dancer next to Bear and Ragged Staff.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Corke, Ossory, Orrery, Shannon, Massereene, Hen. Midensis, Joh. Cloghor., Mich. Corke, Fran. Aungier, Kingston, Santry, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Tho. Pigott

summary: Enforcing payment of Crown Rents and Debts
abstract: Cites proclamation 15 Aug., No. 683, q.v. The payment of dues is now much more in arrear than ever, and the pay of the army is three months in arrear. As it is about to take the field this must be remedied. Distresses will be taken on all who do not pay the Easter Term. Arthur, Earl of Anglesey, Vice-Treasurer, to report the vigorous execution of this order. This to be proclaimed in all towns, courts, &c., throughout the kingdom, and fixed up.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Mount- Alexander, Anglesey, Massereene, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Art. Forbes, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General, and General Governor of Ireland
opening: For the more ready dispatch of such Petitions,
summary: Order as to Petitions, &c
abstract: Type headpiece Warrants Co- Leinster, Connaught, and army business to pass through the hands of Sir George Lane, Munster and Ulster civil business through Thomas Page, Esquire, the Secretaries. Entries to be made at large of all petitions, orders, warrants, &c., which shall pass our signature.

summary: Concerning a late conspiracy
abstract: A conspiracy to seize Dublin Castle on 21 May has been discovered, and some of the conspirators lodged in prison. The Presidents of Munster and Connaught, and all mayors, &c., to search for and arrest all who have a hand in this conspiracy.
signed: Jo. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Kildare, Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Massareene, Hen. Midensis, Joh. Clogher, W. Caulfield, Fran. Angier, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Ja. Donelan, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davys, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones, Tho. Pigott

summary: Parliament prorogued to 21 J uly
abstract: Parliament, now adjourned to 25 May, is further prorogued to 21 July.

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General, and General Governour of Ireland
opening: Forasmuch as for His Majesties Service
summary: All officers to return to quarters
abstract: 1663 : 15 Charles II All officers (including Members of Parliament) to join their commands at once in spite of any leave. printed (13); 54 (437). 1. 12 ‘wherefore’ altered in MS. to ‘whereof’.

opening: Whereas, We have by the blessing
summary: For the arrest of Thomas Blood and others
abstract: £100 reward for the apprehension before 24 June of Thomas Blood, late of Sarny near Dunboine, Col. Daniel Abbot, Major Abel Warren, Andrew MacCormock, a pretended minister of Magherawly, Co. Down, Robert Chambers, a pretended minister, Col. Gilbert Carr (Gibby Carr), John Chamberlin, brewer, John Fooke of Atherdee, Lieut. John Ruxton of the same, Lieut, de la Rock, Maj. Henry Jones of Stelorgan, Co. Dublin, Maj. Alexander Staples of Londonderry, Lieut.-Col. William Moore of Galway and Athlone. No one is to aid them. Unless they surrender within 48 hours they are proclaimed traitors and rebels. printed (14); 68 (560).
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Drogheda. Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Massereene, Dungannon, W. Caulfield, R. Coote, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Jo. Bysse, J. Temple, Paul Davis, Tho. Pigot, Ja. Donelan

summary: Enlarging the periods for sending in claims, &c
abstract: Cites Act of Council 17 Oct. 1662, No. 691, q.v., 18 March 1662-3, Nos. 697, q.v., and 15 April 1663, officers’ arrears. Enlarges all periods fixed for opposing grants, adventurers* claims, Kildare claims, innocent papists, surveys, innocent protestants, bribery and subornation, Connaught lands, cavalier claims, purchased lands in Connaught, certificates of assigned lands, arrears due to officers.
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Mount-Alexander, Drogheda, Anglesey, Massereene, Dungannon, Hen. Midensis, Fran. Aungier, Kingston, J. Temple, Robert Forth, Robert Meredith, Theo. Jones, Tho. Clarges, Tho. Pigott

summary: Enlarging time for payment by Soldiers and Adventurers
abstract: Cites proclamations 17 Oct. 1662, No. 691, q.v., 13 Dec. 1662, No. 694, q.v., 28 Jan. 1662-3, No. 696, q.v., and 18 March 1662-3, No. 697, q.v., enlarging time for first halfyear’s payment of rents by adventurers and soldiers. The time for 1 Nov. 1662 payment enlarged to 21 Nov. 1663, and for the second payment 1 Nov. 1663 to 31 May 1664. This to be proclaimed.
signed: Ormonde, Jo. Armachanus, Ja. Dublin, Anglesey, Ossory, Drogheda, Mount-Alexander, Shannon, Massereene, Dungannon, Hen. Midensis, Santry, J. Temple, Arthur Forbes, Mau. Berkely, Robert Meredith, Theo. Jones, Tho. Pigott

summary: For burning ‘a Collection of some of the Murthers,’ &c
abstract: The printed book ‘ A Collection of some of the Murthers and Massacres committed on the Irish in Ireland since the Twenty third of October, one thousand six hundred forty one : With some Observations and Falsifications on a late Printed Abstract of Murthers, said to be committed by the Irish. Now published by R. S. London, Printed for the Author, 1662 ’, is false, scandalous, and barbarous. The Mayor of Dublin is to burn it publicly on next market day, and all copies he can find by the hands of the common hangman. All copies to be given up within 24 hours.
signed: Ormonde, Ja. Dublin, Mount - Alexander, Anglesey, Shannon, Massareen, Hen. Midensis, Fran. Aungier, J. Temple, Fra. Hamilton, Rob. Forth, G. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith, Tho. Clarges, Tho. Pigott

opening: We cannot but call to mind
summary: Concerning Recusants, &c
abstract: Cites Declaration 30 April 1662, No. 677, q.v. The King’s goodness has not been fully met. He is unwilling to use force, especially as he finds many non-conformists loyal. A stop will be put on all trials for past offences against the Act of Uniformity. No one to expect the same indulgence after 24 December next.
signed: Dublin,. Mount-Alexander, Anglesey, Shannon, Hen. Midensis, Fran. Aungier, R. Coot, Paul Davis, Fra. Hamilton, Rob. Fox-th, J. Bysse, J. Temple, Ja. Ware, G. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith, Tho. Clarges, Edw. Massie, Tho. Pigott

summary: Parliament prorogued until 25 August
abstract: Parliament adjourned to 21 July is further prorogued until 25 August.

summary: Parliament prorogued until 1 October
abstract: Parliament is further prorogued until 1 October next.

summary: For restitution of arms lately seized
abstract: Any arms lately seized may be restored, (1) on certificat of taking the blessed Sacrament of the Communion within the last six months, (2) or on special application to the L. Lieutenant. The Lords Presidents of Munster and Connaught, and the Governors of Counties in Leinster and Ulster are to see the former rules enforced. In case of concealed arms not given up by 10 September they are to be confiscated. Lists are to be made of all persons to whom arms have been restored.
signed: Ormonde, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Kildare, Shannon, Dungannon, Hen. Midensis, Mich. Cork, W. Caulfield, Kingston, J. Temple, Mau. Berkeley, Robert Forth, Ja. Ware, Theo. Jones

title: A Proclamation Concerning Licences for selling all sorts of Wine and Strong-waters by Retail within the Kingdome of Ireland
abstract: By Patent 16 Jan. 12 Chas.* II [1660-1] Sir William Clark and Gilbert Mabbot and the survivor have the office of granting licences for retail of wines and spirits in Ireland. Any one who sells wine or spirits between 1 May 1661 and 1 May 1664 will be punished. Farmers who have received money for licences to pay it over to these agents by 31 October. The lawful interest of Viscount Massereene and Baron Kingston to be regarded.
signed: Ormonde, ^ Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Arran, Massereene, Dungannon, R. Coote, J. Temple, Mau. Berkeley, G. Wentworth, Ja. Ware, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones, Tho. Clarges

summary: Grants under Great Seal of England to be registered in Ireland
abstract: All honours, offices, pardons, lands, granted under Great Seal of England must be enrolled in Ireland within a month from date on pain of disannulling.
signed: Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ja. Dublin, Ossory, Arran, Dungannon, Massareen, R. Coote, J. Temple, Mau. Berkeley, Ja. Ware, Tho. Clarges, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

summary: Parliament prorogued until 17 November
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 1 October to 17 November.

summary: Concerning abduction of children
abstract: Certain persons, wickedly pretending authority, have stolen children to sell them in foreign parts. The Mayors of Dublin and all other cities to arrest such persons and present them at the Assizes for trial. All ships and barques are to be searched for such offenders and such children.
signed: Ormonde, Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Ossory, Arran, Massareen, Dungannon, W. Caulfield, Hen. Titchborne, Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Rob. Meredith, Ja. Ware, Mau. Berkeley, G. Wentworth, Theo. Jones

summary: Enlarging time for lodging of adventurers’ surveys
abstract: By proclamation 20 July 1663 of the Commissioners, adventurers were ordered to lodge their surveys in forty days. On address 9 Sept, signed Ri. Raynsford, Edwai’d Dering, Thomas Beverley, Edward Smith, A. Brodrick, Edward Cooke, W. Churchill, the time is extended to 17 November next. N° 710. N N°s 717-25
signed: Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Dungannon, W. Caulfield, R. Coote, Paul Davys, G. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

summary: Parliament prorogued until 12 January
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 17 Nov. to 12 January next.

summary: Enlarging time for lodging adventurers’ claims
abstract: The time for lodging adventurers’ claims on forfeited lands enlarged by proclamation 9 Sept. 1663, No. 716, q.v., is further enlarged to twelve months after the forty days mentioned on 20 July 1663.

summary: Parliament further prorogued to 3 February
abstract: Parliament is further prorogued from 1 2 Jan. to 3 February.

summary: Parliament prorogued until 17 February
abstract: Parliament is further prorogued from 3 to 17 February next.

summary: Proroguing Parliament till 3 March
abstract: Parliament is further prorogued from 17 Feb. to 3 March.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 19 April
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 3 March to 1 7 April.

summary: Concerning Customs on Foreign and Colonial Produce
abstract: Repeats proclamation 28 Jan. 1662[-3],No. 696, q.v., and extends it for another year.
signed: Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Mich. Dublin, Ossory, Massereene, Dungannon, Hen. Midensis, W. Caulfield, Kingston, Santry, Hen. Tichborne, Mau. Berkeley, Robert Forth, C. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

summary: Enlarging time for payment of second instalment
abstract: Enlarging the time for payment of second instalments of value of lands payable by adventurers from 1 November 1663 to 21 November 1664, when they must pay such instalment according to the best estimate of the value of the lands in 1659. From No. 732, q.v. Has been printed ; see Cal. S.P.I. p. 529. If0

issuer: Lord Lieutenant General, and General Governor of Ireland
summary: Officers to repair to their quarters
abstract: Officers to repair to their quarters within ten days after publication of this if on leave, if absent without leave forthwith, or they will be dismissed.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 25 October
abstract: N°s 726-35 Parliament is further prorogued from 23 Sept, to 25 October.

summary: Officers to return to their quarters
abstract: Many officers are absent from quarters without leave, and others have had leave for harvest. All are to return, those without leave forthwith, those on leave within ten days, and not to leave them without special licence, on pain of dismissal.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 1 December
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 25 Oct. to 1 December.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 17 January
abstract: Parliament further adjourned from 1 Dec. to 17 January.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 20 February
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 17 January to 20 February.

summary: Publishing Declaration 28 October 1664
abstract: Reprinting Order in Council 28 Oct. 1664, No. 3402, Eng., q.v. Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Mich. Dublin, Massereen, Dungannon, Joh. Cloghor., Paul Davys, Fra. Hamilton, Robert Forth, G. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith.

opening: Whereas we have lately seen an order
summary: Suspending an Act of Council of 6 May
abstract: Respiting and suspending the payment of the second instalment ordered by proclamation 6 May 1664, No. 724, q.v., in accordance with a royal letter and Order in Council of 7 December 1664.
signed: Ossoiy, Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Massereene, Hen. Midensis, John Clogher, Fran. Aungier, Fra. Hamilton, Art. Forbes, Rob. Forth, Mau. Berkley, G. Wentworth, Rob. Meredith, Theo. Jones

summary: Parliament prorogued to 10 April
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 20 Feb. to 10 April.

summary: Concerning Customs on foreign produce, &c
abstract: Continuing Proclamation of 27 Feb. 1663-4, No. 723, q.v., for six months more. From No. 745, q.v.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 2 May
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 10 April to 2 May.

summary: For bringing in Crown rents
abstract: Cites proclamations 15 Aug. 1662, No. 683, q.v., and 10 April 1663, No. 698, q.v. Any one failing to bring in N°s 736-44 their rents or dues at the appointed time to be coerced severely. Vice-Treasurer to be responsible for execution. This to be proclaimed and fixed up.
signed: Ja. Armachanus, Mau. Eustace, Cane., Mich. Dublin, Drogheda, Arran, Fran. Aungier, Paul Davis, Hen. Tichborn, Jo. Bysse, Art. Forbese, Robert Forth

summary: Parliament prorogued to 1 June
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 2 May to 1 June.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 4 J uly
abstract: Parliament further prorogued from 1 June to 4 July.

summary: Parliament prorogued to 3 August
