Earl Lauderdale, Col., Sir John Clerk of Pennicook, Lieut. -Col., Alexander Burnet of Carlops, Major for Edinbro’, Lord Belhaven, Col., Laird of Px-estoun Grange, Lieut.-Col., Ensign Robert Sinclair, Major for Haddington, Sir John Home of Blackader, Col., Sir Robert Stuart of Allanbank, Lieut. -Col., Capt. Alexander Cockbui’n of Duns, Major for Berwickshire, Patrick Murray of Livingstoun, Col., James Pringle of Torwoodlie, Lieut.- Col., — Shai’p of Houston, Major, Linlithgow, Peebles, and Selkirk, Master of Burghlie, Col., — Arnot of Auchinmoor Lieut.-Col., — Hay younger of Naughton. Majoi’, for East Fife, Earl Mortoun, Col., — Douglas of Sti’athendre, Lieut.- Col., Orrock of Balram, Major, for Kini’oss and West Fife, Provost Edinburgh, Cel., Lieut. Robert Keith, Lieut.-Col., Capt. James Lindsey, Major, for Edinburgh town. Commissioners of Supply to meet on 9 March and nominate captains, &c. Officers nominated to serve under penalty of fine of 1,000 or 500 mei’ks. All hex-etors to be ready by 12 March with men and 10 days’ pay at 6 d. per day at the meeting places, where the troops are to be kept at drill for 10 days. The heretors of Wigtoun, Kirkcudbright, Air, Dumbarton, Lanerk, and Renfrew are to assemble within three days. The militia, &c., will not be regarded as listed soldiers. All horses worth above 100 merks Scots, whose owners have not sworn allegiance, are to be seized for service. Report to be sent in by 16 March. This to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Pi-oclamation For Calling out of the Heretors, and Requiring the Flanders Officers, and other Officers imployed since His Majesties Accession to the Crown, to come to Edinburgh
abstract: Our dom their Calling out the hei-etors of the southei-n counties on 12 March, under Laird of Kimei-ghame, L. of Stevinson, . . . Craig of Riccartoun, Henry Balfour of Denbug, . . . Lawson of Cavinmoor, . . . Cornwall of Bonhard, . . . Scot of Gilmenscleugh, L. of Cleghorn, . . . Hamilton of Aikenhead, . . . Muir of Glanderstoun, . . . Crafurd of Kilbirnie, . . . Howstoun of that Ilk, Sir William Mackdowgal of Gartland. All the Flanders officers in the kingdom, and all other former officers are to come to Edinburgh and give in their names to Sir Thomas Livingstoun, Commander-in-Chief. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches after sermon, and printed.

title: A Proclamation For a Solemn Day of Humiliation
abstract: France as And On the address of the Commissioners of the General Assembly, Lord’s day, 15 March, is appointed a day of humiliation in Edinburgh, Leith, Cannongate, and West Kirk, 22 March in the rest south of Tay, and 29 March north of Tay. These to be proclaimed, read in parish churches at Edinburgh on Thursday next, by sound of drum on Friday, in all other parish churches the Lord’s day before the fixed day and printed.

title: A Proclamation For Apprehending the persons After-named, as having been in France contrair to the Acts of Parliament
abstract: Cites Act 8, Sess. 4. The following have incurred the penalty of treason. . . . Grahame jun. of Duntroon, Charles Kinnaird, brother of L. Kinnaird, Alexander Maitland, b. of E. of Lauderdale, Capt. Deans, Capt. Ruthven, Lieut. Isaac Threcal, Lieut. Auchmouty, Ensign Alexander Innes, Lieuts. Daniel and John Banes, Ens. William Ramsay (of Hodge’s regiment), Ens. Alexander Sandelands (Wauchope’s regiment), Ens. Laurence Drummond, Capt. Robert Somervail, Capt. William Davidson, Lieut. William Main, Lieut. James Henderson, Ens. Robert Southerland, Ens. Alexander Sinclair, Lieut. John Bell (D’Offerel’s regiment), Ens. William Innes (D’Offerel’s regiment), Ens. William Lyon (same), William and Hugh Southerland, nephews to Maj.-Gen. Southerland, Walter Nisbet, s. of Alexander Nisbet of Craigintinny, William Sinclair, Thomas Clark, Robert Kinloch, William Pearson, Alexander Nisbet, Mr. James Oswald (Chappeland to the Lady Halket), . . . Cuthbert, Capt. Patrick Grahame, Capts. Robert and William Charters, Capt. John Ramsay, Lieut.-Col. Rattray, Lieut.-Col. Oliphant, Lieut.-Col. Douglas, Robert Stuart, Ens. John Menzies, Maj. John Gordon, Capt. James Adamson, Charles Farquharson, Robert King, Capt. John Livingston, Lieut. John Creighton, Sir John Mclain of that Ilk, . . . Irwine of Stepletoun, Capt. . . . Mair. They are said to have returned to Scotland. All sheriffs, &c., are to search for and arrest them, reporting the result of their diligence to the Council by 1 April. No one to relieve them, &c. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation For Seising the Horses and Arms of Papists, and Persons above the Degree of Commons, not Qualified according to the Act of Parliament
abstract: Cites Act. All sheriffs, &c., are to cite all papists and heretors above the degree of Commons in every parish who will not take the oath of allegiance to declare what horses worth more than 100 merks, and what arms they have, and to deliver them up immediately. These to be kept in safe custody by the sheriffs. They are to report the result by 2 April (or 5 May N. of Tay) on fine of 500 merks Scots. Arms, &c., to be taken by force if necessary. Magistrates and officers to swear that they have not returned any valuable horses or arms. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament from the 20 day of March instant, to the 21st day of July next
abstract: Headpiece Britain, riffs And Cites proclamation 5 Nov., No. 3062, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 21 July. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Association Begun to be Subscribed at Edinburgh, April 10, 1696
abstract: Headpiece with Conspiracy De- Acknowledging William’s title, and engaging to defend him against James, and the pretended Prince of Scotland (Prince of Wales), and against invasion or insurrection, and in case of his assassination to defend the succession according to the declaration of the Estates. [Followed by] An authorization to print and sell this under the title of ‘Bond of Association, Subscribed by the Lords of His Majesties Privy Council, by His Majesties Special Allowance’. This is page 2 of a broadside 2 pp. p. 1 is the English Association 3 April: complete in Adv. Pamph. 1 (269).

summary: Sheriffs to report seizures of Arms or Horses
abstract: Da. Moncrieff.1 1 MS. signature. 2 Blanks filled in MS. Rubbed impression of seal.

title: Proclamation For Apprehending Sir George Barclay
abstract: Sir George Barclay, having conspired to assassinate the King, is thought to have escaped to Scotland. £1,000 sterling reward for his arrest, full pardon if he is killed or wounded when resisting arrest. Those who conceal him are traitors. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Crying down the English Milned Crowns and Half-Crowns : Ordaining the Old-Merk and Half-Merk-Pieces to Pass, and stopping the taking of Bullion, at the Mint-house
Proclamation For Crying down the Silver Scots Crown-Piece, and the fourty Shilling, twenty Shilling, ten Shilling, and five Shilling Scots Pieces to their former Rates
abstract: Edinburgh ; H. & S. of A. A. : 1 696. Cites proclamation 12 July 1695, No. 3053, q.v., which is withdrawn. These coins to pass at their former rates. These to be proclaimed and printed. Patrick ii. 259. UD

title: A Proclamation For a Solemn National Fast and Humiliation
abstract: Ireland , as foresaid. On the address of the commissioners appointed by the late General Assembly, Tuesday, 16 June (Tuesday, 30th, N. of Tay) is appointed a day of solemn humiliation and prayer. Fine for neglect £100 Scots, half to judge, half to poor of parish. These to be proclaimed, read in pulpits the Lord’s day before the day fixed, and printed. B.L. Sig. 109. e. 7 (91). Adv. Pamph. 1 (276), 19 (39) ; Procl. I (71). Causes of a solemn Fast (Sig. 109. e. 7 (90)).

title: Proclamation Against Regraiting of Victual, and Forestalled, and Allowing the Importation of Victual free of Publick Burden
abstract: To strictly Proclama- Cites Acts against regrating and forestalling. These Acts are to be enforced. All victual stored up is to be threshed and exposed to sale at the prices of last Candlemas Fiers, or to be escheated. Magistrates to see that the markets are duly regulated. Any person may import foreign victual duty free to 1 September next. These to be proclaimed and printed. B.L. Sig. 109. e. 7 (92). Adv. Pamph. 1 (277); Procl. I (72). Reg. V (71). A reprint in folio with explanation, Aberdeen (145).

title: Letters of Publication Of an Patent Granted by Their Majesties King William and Queen Mary, In favours of the Chirurgions, and Chirurgion Apothecaries of Edinburgh
abstract: [2 ft’.] Roman letter. Gilb. Eliot. On the address of Alexander Monteith, Deacon of the Chirurgions of Edinburgh, that they have a patent of William and Mary, 28 Feb. 1694, confirming their rights under Great Seal, ratified in the last session of Parliament, 17 July 1695, and praying that they be published ; the Privy Council orders it to be published. (Text of Charter follows.) P.C. Reg.

title: A Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament to the Twenty sixth of August next
abstract: Cites proclamation 16 March, No. 3086, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 26 August next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation, For a Solemn Fast and Humiliation
Proclamation Appointing Twenty Shilling to be Payed for every Boll of Foraign Victual that shall be imported
abstract: Kefers to previous proclamations, Nos. 3075, 3078, 3093, q.v., permitting importation of victual. Victual or corn of any sort except malt may be imported free of duty or excise to 1 October next (in consequence of the weather and threatened late harvest), and a bounty of 20s. Scots per boll will be paid on import. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For Paying in the Pole-Money
Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament from August the 26th till September the 8th 1696
abstract: Headpiece Britain Date And Cites proclamation 13 (sic) June, No. 3096, q.v. Parliament is prorogued to 8 September when it will meet. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For Apprehending Henry Every, alias Bridgeman, and sundry other Pirates
abstract: .£500 sterling reward for Every and £50 each for the others named in English proclamation 10 Aug., No. 4200, England, q.v. : no mention of Frenchmen or Danes. They may be known by having Persian and Indian gold and silver. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act of Parliament at Edinburgh, The Fifth day of October, 1696, Anent the Petition given in, and presented to his Grace, his Majesties High Commissioner, and the Right Honorable the Estates of Parliament, By the Magistrates & Town Council of Bamff, in Name and Behalf of their Burgh
abstract: Arms as 239 of twixt Rolls. On a petition showing a commodious harbour in the mouth of the Doveron, built on one side, bare on the other, and thus in time of speat choking the harbour with shingle, and praying for a public contribution on the second Sabbath of March 1697 to build another sea-wall to keep the current vol. ii 465 straight, and that a proclamation be printed, and intimate the Sabbath preceding the appointed day, the petition was granted.

title: Proclamation, Indemnifying Deserters, who shall return betwixt and the First Day of January next to come
abstract: All deserters returning to their colours before 1 January next will be pardoned : all others, and their resetters, severely punished. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act In Favours of The Ministers and Kirk- Session of the Canongate
abstract: By the fire of 7 Nov. current, 37 families have been ruined. A church-door collection in Dalkeith, Haddingtoun, Linlithgow, and Edinburgh (country churches) Presbytery is to be made on 13 December, and a house-to-house collection in Edinburgh, Canongate, Leith, and West-Bark parish : And in St. Johnstoun, Dundee, Montrose, Jedburgh, Aberdeen, Glasgow, and Kelso on the 20 Dec. or following days as the towns decide on church-door or house-to-house collections. The money to be paid to Angus Black and David White, Treasurers, who have given caution. These to be printed and read at the parish churches the Sunday before. Sig. 109. e. 7 (101).

title: A Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament
abstract: Cites proclamation 12 Oct., on prorogation. Parliament is further postponed to 18 March next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Appointing the Commissioners of Supply to be Justices of Peace
abstract: Headpiece France, severally that Cites proclamations 9 and 13 May 1692, Nos. 2938, 2939, q.v., appointing Justices of Peace. All Commissioners of Supply who qualify themselves according to law before 15 Jan. next to be Justices of Peace. These to be proclaimed.

title: Act Discharging Persons to Travel from Edinburgh without Passes
abstract: No one to leave Edinburgh without a pass from one of the Privy Council stating his destination. These to be printed and published.

title: A Proclamation, Calling out the half Foot Militia in some Shires, the Fencible Men in others, and the whole Horse Militia in the Northern Shires
abstract: To be ready at 24 hours’ notice. Commanders appointed. These to be proclaimed and read in paroch churches after sermon.

title: Proclamation Appointing the Heretors of several Shires to be in readiness upon Fourty eight Hours Advertisement, to attend His Majesties Host, and Standard
abstract: Headpiece Britain, and and In view of invasion, all heretors, wadsetters, and liferenters in Edinburgh, Haddingtoun, Berwick, Roxburgh, Selkirk, Peebles, Dumfries, Dumbartoun, Bute, Linlithgow, Stirling, Clackmannan, Fife, Kinross, Wigtoun, Kirkcudbright, Air, Lanerk, Argyll, Renfrew, and Perth are to meet with their horses, arms, and provisions on 48 hours’ notice. This to be proclaimed and printed. (178) , 1 (292) ; Procl. I (85). Reg. Y (64). E.T.C. (157).

title: A Proclamation, Anent Passes and the appearing of Ships upon the Coast
abstract: Headpiece Britain, Kingdom presents In view of invasion, all persons coming into or going out of the kingdom without sufficient passports are to be stopped and reported to a magistrate. Meetings of disaffected persons to be reported. If any number of ships are sighted they are to be reported at once. This to be proclaimed and printed. (179) , 1 (293); Procl. I (84). E.T.C. (156).

title: A Proclamation For a Solemn National Fast and Humiliation
abstract: Britain, ting the On address of the Commissioners for the General Assembly 21 Jan. next is to be a day of humiliation and prayer. These to be proclaimed, read in all parish churches on Sunday, and printed. The causes of this fast, No. 3112, q.v., to be printed herewith.

title: Causes Of a Solemn National Fast and Humiliation, unanimously agreed upon by the Commission appointed by the late General Assembly, met at Edinburgh the 3rd of December 1696
abstract: this great our The tokens of God’s displeasure enumerated. The national sins enumerated. A call to reformation with humiliation. 1 With No. 3111 on the same sheet.

title: A Proclamation, For the Calling out the Levy of One Thousand Men, for the Year 1697
abstract: The 1,000 men required are to be handed over to the officers sent for them, or 24 pounds Scots for each man not delivered. 20 pounds Scots will be paid to each man who joins. Fixed receiving days. Col. George Hamilton to make arrangements. Proportions of each shire 80 to 15. Commissioners appointed for each shire : Sir John Pringle of Sinchel, Laird of Grubet, and the Deputy Sheriff for Roxburghshire, Sir James Murray of Philiphaugh for Selkirk, Sir John Hume of Blacader, Sir John Swintoun of that ilk, or the Dep. Sheriff for Berwick, Earl of Lauderdale with Dep. Sheriff for Edinburgh, Lord Provost with Sir William Anstruther for Edinburgh town, Lairds of Prestongrange and Beanstoun with Dep. Sheriff for Haddington. — Lawson of Cairnmuir with Dep. Sheriff of Peebles for Peebles, Sir Thomas Kirkpatrick of Closburn and — Johnstoun of Elcliesheils for Dumfries, Sir Andrew Agnew of Lochnaw and the Laird of Gaithland for Wigton, Lairds of Ruscoe and Machrimore for Kirkcudbright ; Lairds of Rowalland, Kilbirnie, Cairletoun, and John Muir Provost, and the Dep. Sheriff for Air ; Laii'ds of Craigens, Glanderstoun, Caldwell, and the Dep. Sheriff for Renfrew, Sir Alexander Monro of Bearcrofts, and William Cunninghame of Boquhare for Stirling ; — Rollo of Woodside for Clackmannan, — Hamilton of Udstoun (Dep. Sheriff) and Andrew Kay of Craignethen, — Hamilton of Barncleugh and — Hamilton of Aikenhead for Lanerk ; Lairds of Livingstoun, Dudingstoun, and Pardivan for Linlithgow ; Sir Charles Halket of Pitfirren, Sir James Mogill of Rankellior, Lairds of Randifood, Auchtermarnie, Readil, — Hay younger of Naughton, and Dep. Sheriff for Fyf ; Master of Burghly for Kinross ; L. Ruthven, Sir Colin Campbell of Aberuchle, Lairds of Megnish, Culforgie, Dumbarnie, and Dep. Sheriff for Perth ; — Fullerton of Kinnabeer and — Milne of Balwillo for Forfar ; — Irving of Kincousie and Dep. Sheriff for Kincardine ; Laird of Craigweir, Alexander Duff of Braco, Laird of Munimusk younger, Birkenboog, and Dep. Sheriff for Aberdeen and Bamff ; Lairds of Brodie, Lethim, and Culloden, — Dumbar of Grange, and Dep. Sheriff of Inverness for Elgin, Nairn, and Inverness ; Sir Alexander Mckenzie of Coull, — McKenzie of Redcastle, Laird of Culloden, — Frazer of Rerick, Laird of Balnagoon, Sir Adam Gordon of Dalfollie, Sheriff-Dep. of Sutherland, Laird of Hempriggs, — Sinclair of Brinies for Inverness, Sutherland, and Caithness ; Laird of Ardkinglass, Sir John Campbel of Carrick for Argyle ; Claud Hamilton of Barns, — Colquhoun of Craigtoun for Dumbarton ; Laird of Kelburn for Bute ; James Beakie of Tankerness and the Laird of Grahameshall for Orkney and Zetland. This to be proclaimed.

title: Proclamation Anent old Fourteens, and their Halfs, Cobbs, and Fourty Penny-pieces
abstract: By the Act old 14s. pieces weighing 2 drops 27 grains and their halves weighing proportionately pass current, and others at £3. 4s. the ounce, being a groat for a drop. This is to be Lanerk Troy weight, which is the standart of the weight in this kingdom. Cobbs pass by weight, 14 drops Lanerk weight for 56s. No one to refuse these coins by weight. These to be proclaimed and printed. Patrick ii. 269.

title: Act Anent Deficients of the Levy, one Thousand, six Hundred and Ninety five
abstract: the ed De- Several shires are deficient in the levy of 1695. Sheriffs are to raise the number notified to them as wanting by Sir Patrick Hume, H.M. Solicitor, and deliver them on 25 Jan. (N. of Tay 10 February). Heretors, &c., liable to send and not sending men, fine of 200 merks recoverable in six days. Rewards for deserters will be paid liberally. Proclamation 4 April 1694, No. 3006, q.v., will be rigorously enforced. An account of what has been done to be sent to Council before 25 Feb. These to be printed. B.L. Sig. 109. e. 7 (112). Adv. Pamph. 1 (299); Procl. I (91).

title: Proclamation Discharging all English Vnmilln’d Money to pass, except by Weight, and Allowing and Crying-up the English Milln’d Crown to Three Pound five Shilling, with its Fractions proportionally. Edinburgh : 23 January
abstract: Britain, Privy to Light English un-millned money is only to pass by weight as in England at 4s. Scots the drop, making £3. 4s. Scots the oz. It is to be legal tender at that rate. The silver milln’d crown of England is to pass as £3. 5s. Scots and its fractions proportionately. These to be proclaimed and printed. Patrick ii.

title: Proclamation For Compleating the Levy for the thousand Men, for the year 1697. And in case of deficiency to poynd the Leaders
abstract: Council, missioners Answerable. Cites proclamation 16 Dec., No. 3113, q.v., calling out levies for Col. George Hamilton’s regiment in Flanders, and fixing days for handing over the men or a fine of £24 Scots each. Many shires have made default. Officers will be sent to head-burghs on 20 Feb. Leaders are to deliver their men or their money to them on 1 March, or if not be liable to a fine of £100 Scots. Commissioners of Supply to poynd the goods of these leaders and sell them for the £100 each and the charges not exceeding £10 Scots on each £100. It shall be lawful for the party poynded to redeem them within 6 days for the sum, charges, and 405. Scots for each day. These to be proclaimed, printed, and published. Copies to be sent to the Commissioners of Supply, who are ordered to give the leaders notice in writing of the days for delivery and the penalty they will incur in case of failzie.

title: Proclamation Anent the Stenting Unfree- Traders
abstract: The royal burghs offered free communication of trade to the burghs of barony, regality, and others, on condition they compound with Mr. John Buchan, who is responsible for 10 per cent, of their taxt-roll. The Privy Council order the Commissioners of Supply and Excise to meet at their head-burghs, hear and consider Mr. Buchan’s offers, and if they agree divide the quotas on the burghs of barony and regality and other unfree-traders who accept and agree to make payment accordingly. Unfree-traders who do not compound with Mr. John Buchan will be rigorously proceeded against for the penalties they have incurred. Meetings to be held 1 April (N. of Tay 20 April). Inferior magistrates to administer justice speedily and impartially to Mr. John Buchan against unfree-traders. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Anent the Deficients of the Levies 1693 and 1695
abstract: Cites Act 7, Sess. 4, offering 2,979 foot; Act 33, Sess. 5, levying 1,000 yearly, &c. There are yet many deficient for these levies (1693 and 1695). Commissioners of Supply to meet 11 March (N. of Tay 23 March), and to require the leaders for 1693 and 1695 to produce a discharge of their sufficient number, or within 6 days to produce the men to Col. George Hamilton or his order. Leaders not producing their men will be fined £100 Scots. Commissioners to make returns to Privy Council within 20 days of the meeting on pain, &c. These to be proclaimed and printed. Sig. 109. e. 7 (116). Adv. Pamph. 1 (303); Procl. I (96). N° 3119.

title: A Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament
abstract: Headpiece Britain, by Presents Cites proclamation 3 Dec., No. 3105, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 18 August. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For the better Collecting and Inbringing of what is deficient of the Pole-Money Imposed in Anno 1695
abstract: Recites the Acts concerning the poll-money, now set in tack to John Campbell of Knockrioch and his partners, who are to have the whole benefit. All collectors are to make up their lists and pay in the poll-money within fifteen days, on pain of losing their allowance. Any person deficient of the pollmoney to pay quadruple. The country is not to be oppressed in the recovery of this poll-money, and no one is to be troubled without order. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation For a Solemn National Fast
abstract: On the address of the Commissioners of the General Assembly, Thursday, 27 May, is appointed a day of solemn fasting and prayer, to be observed by all. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches the Lord’s day immediately preceding the fast day, and printed.

title: A Proclamation Discharging Forraign Copper or Brass- Coyn
abstract: Headpiece France rally Ordains Forraign black-money called French doyets and Irish half-pennies have been imported into the country. Not brass or copper coin, not coined at our mint, is to be current. Fine of £10 each time for offering it in payment. All imported to be confiscated. These to be proclaimed and printed. Patrick ii. 271. -

title: Proclamation, Recalling former Acts or Proclamations, declaring Forraign Victual free of Duty, and ordaining all Victuall to he Imported to pay Duty as before the saids former Acts and Proclamation
abstract: Britain, stitute pre- Cites proclamation 6 Aug. 1696, No. 3098, q.v., and Act 29 Dec. 1696. The scarcity being provided for, and there being a prospect of a good harvest, these, proclamation and Act, are discharged. All duties to be levied as before. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament from the Eighteenth Day of August, to the Fifteenth Day of December, 1697
abstract: Headpiece Britain, the Be- Cites proclamation 15 March, No. 3120, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 15 December next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act Discharging any Person to go Aboard of, or Correspond with French Privateers
abstract: bespond Edin- No one is to go on board French privateers or correspond with them, without licence of Privy Council, on pain of treason. These to be printed and published.

title: A Proclamation For the Ready Inbringing of the Annexed and Additional Excise
abstract: se- Tacksmen thereof ; To determine any questions between brewers and excisemen, the Commissioners of the Excise are to meet on first Tuesday in September and every first Tuesday following. Brewers on first Tuesday to bring in an account of their brewings from 1 March last, or an affidavit that they have brewed less than a named quantity. No part of the browst to be sold before an entry of it is made and a permit obtained. Tapsters, &c., to take out a licence and enter into a bond not to sell before excise is paid. Provisions that imported spirits, &c., pay excise, the retailers to be traced. Commissioners not meeting duly liable to summary fine. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches the Sunday before the appointed day, fixed on the church door, and printed.

title: Proclamation For Apprehending five Persons declared Fugitives, by the Commission of Justiciary for the Highlands
abstract: Britain , part Intimation The Commissioners of Justiciary for the middle district of the Highlands report that Duncan Stuart, alias Shankie, Patrick M°ilglass Ferguson, John late Mcgregor in Rennock, Duncan Roy Mcilphatrick late Mcgregor in Pollockro, John Mcclaran Buy in Torray, are fugitives. £10 sterling reward for any of them, dead or alive. Free pardon and reward to any of them that brings in the others. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Against Importing Victual from Ireland
abstract: Britain, ther Prin- A reissue of proclamation, No. 3064, q.v., against import of victual of any sort from Ireland after 1 Sept, on pain of confiscation, half to informer. These to be proclaimed and printed.

summary: Reviving Proclamation 13 March 1694
abstract: Edinburgh : H. & S. of A. A. : 1 697. 3005]. Gilb. Eliot. Arms 246 France and as Recites proclamation 13 March 1694, No. 3004, q.v. It is to be reprint and published at head burghs on western coast and sent to all the collectors of customs, &c., to be affixed on their offices. These to be printed.

title: A Proclamation For Publishing the Peace between His Majesty and the French King
Proclamation For Publishing the Peace betwixt His Majesty and the French King
abstract: The Scots form of the preceding proclamation, No. 3132, q.v.

title: A Proclamation For a Solemn National Thanksgiving
abstract: and feating next : On the address of the Commission of the late General Assembly, 16 Dec. is appointed a day of thanksgiving. These to be proclaimed, read in all pulpits on the Sunday before 16 Dec., printed and published.

title: Letter Congratulatory from the Privy Council of Scotland, to His Majesty upon the Conclusion of the Peace, and His Majesties safe Return
abstract: Headpiece heartily tagious Sub- Congratulations on peace and safe return. Prayers for his welfare.
signed: Marchmont, Canccllar., Melvill, P., Tweeddale, Southerland, Morton, Buchan, Leven, Annandale, Tarbat, Ross, Carmichael, Ruthven, Ja. Stuart, Ad. Cokburn, W. Anstruther, Jo. Maxwell, Arc. Murray, Ard. Muire

title: His Majesties gracious Answer to the foresaid Letter
Proclamation For calling down the French Three-Sous-Pieces to Three shillings Scots, and appointing the Scots Fourtie-pennie-pieces to pass at Three shilling six pennies Scots per piece
abstract: France Council or- The three sous piece French is not worth 35. 6d. Scots, but is to pass at 3s. Scots, and the French crown at 58 5. Scots with its fractions proportionately, the old fourty-penny pieces to pass as 3s. 6d. Scots if the print and vestige of the coin be visible. These to be proclaimed and printed. Patrick ii. 272. 1 Printed as a two page sheet with No. 3138, q.v.

title: A Proclamation Against Persons returning from France without Passes
abstract: Britain, Privy that Those denounced as traitors for going to France in wartime, No. 3084, q.v., and others, are not to return. All sheriffs, &c. , to search for any who have returned without a pass, and arrest them in sure firmance. Customs officers, &c., to note all arrivals. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For Adjourning the currant Parliament to the Eleventh Day of March 1697
abstract: Cites proclamation 29 July, No. 3126, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 1 1 March next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Against Robbers and Vagabounds, &c
abstract: The following Acts are to be enforced : Act 7, Pari. 1 , Jas. I, Jas. II, Pari. 6, c. 21, Act Jas. II, Pari. 11, c. 45, Pari. 12, c. 53, Act Jas. Ill, Pari. 10, c. 78, Act Jas. VII, Pari. 12, c. 147, and all other laws against robbing, thieving, sorning, &c. Security to be taken of all idle and vagabond persons. Day and night watches to be appointed in each parish. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation against Prophaneness
abstract: On the address of the General Assembly the laws against profanity are to be reprinted and enforced. This proclamation and list to be read twice yearly in all churches, first Sunday after Whitsunday and Martinmas. Acts 21 Chas. II, P. 1 . 1, 1 Wm. Ill, P. 5, cap. 1 1 against blasphemy. (2) Against cursing and swearing, Mary, P. 5. 16, Jas. YI, P. 7. 103, Chas. II, P. 1. 1. 19 and P. 2. 3. 22. Observation of the Sabbath, Jas. VI, P. 6. 71, P. 13, c. 159, P. 14. 198, 18 Chas. II, P. 1 and P. 2. 3. 22. Against cursing and beating of parents, Chas. II, P. 1. 1. 20. Against drunkards, Jas. VI, P. 22. 20, &c. Against adultery, Mary, P. 5. 20, P. 9. 74. Against fornication, Jas. VI, P. 1. 13. The Act, P. 1. 5. 13, enforcing penalties against judges for not enforcing these laws. The Act 2 1 of Session 2 of this Parliament, 19 J uly 1690, anent murdering of children (concealment of pregnancy). This to be proclaimed, printed, and published.

title: A Proclamation, For Preventing and Punishing Immorality and Prophaneness
abstract: A reprint of No. 4246, England, q.v.

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the Twenty Eight of June, 1698
abstract: France that these Cites proclamation 9 Dec., No. 3139, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 28 June next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Anent the Poor. Edinburgh : 3 March
abstract: Proclamations 11 Aug. 1692, No. 2945; 29 Aug. 1693, No. 2981 ; 31 July 1694, No. 3015, q.v., to be repi'inted. Act 18, Sess. 3, Pari. 2, Chas. II to be revived. Correction houses to be built at Edinburgh, Haddingtoun, Dunce, Jedburgh, Selkirk, Peebles, Glasgow, Drumfreis, Wigtoun, Kirkcudbright, Air, Dumbarton, Rothesay, Pasley, Stirling, Linlithgow, Culross, Perth, Montross, Aberdeen, Inverness, Elgine, Inverary, St. Andrews Cowper, Kirkaldy, Dumfermling, Dundie, Bamff, Dornoch, Week, Kirkwal, with a large close sufficiently enclosed. Masters and overseers to be appointed before 1 October next on pain of 500 merks quarterly till provided. Sheriffs to report before 1 Dec. The poor to be sent to the correction houses by 1 November next. The ministers and elders of the parish with the lieretors may settle any local questions not determined by law. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation For the Ready Inbringing of the Annexed and Additional Excise
abstract: the Excise upon A reissue of proclamation 3 Aug., No. 3128, q.v., with the substitution of second Tuesday in April for first Tuesday in September.

title: A Proclamation Anent Seminary Priests, Jesuists and Trafficking Papists
abstract: Ireland, That hereof, Cites Acts Jas. VI, Pari. 7, c. 105, Jas. VI, Pari. 11, c. 24, Pari. 12, c. 120, Pari. 16, c. 18, Chas. II, Pari. 1, Sess. 1, c. 8, Pari. 3, c. 6. All sheriffs, &c., to apprehend the priests and Jesuits found and send them to the tolbooth at Edinburgh. Names of resetters of priests, &c., of popish teachers, &c., to be sent to Privy Council. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation For a National Fast
abstract: Ireland, , Defender. Provincial On the address of the Provincial Synod of Lothian and Tweddale, Tuesday, 17 May, is appointed a day of humiliation in their bounds (25 May rest of Scotland S. of Tay, 1 June N. of Tay) in view of the death of cattle and growing scarcity. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches the Lord’s day before the appointed day, and printed. The causes of the fast, No. 3149, q.v., to be printed herewith.

title: Act of the Synod of Lothian and Tweeddale, Anent the Observation of a Fast, with the Causes thereof
abstract: A day of humiliation to be kept on Tuesday, 17 May, in this synod because of (1) growth of vice, drunkenness, irreligion, and murder ; (2) impenitence of the masses ; (3) just displeasure of God shown in famine of men and beasts ; (4) growth of atheism and popery. All are called to praver.

title: A Proclamation, Appointing Skippers to give up Lists of their Passengers
abstract: Britain, riffs be All masters of ships bringing home passengers from abroad to detain them till they are examined by one of the Privy Council or the sheriffs and other officers of the law, and if found suspicious kept prisoner till the order of the Privy Council. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation, Prohibiting the Exportation of Victual furth of this Kingdom
abstract: Headpiece France, Messengers that Owing to the cold and backward season, no meal, oats, pease, barley, or bear are to be exported. B.L. Sig. 109. e. 7 (141). Adv. Pamph. 1 (337); Procl. I (123). E.T.C. (110).

title: A Proclamation, Adjourning the Parliament to the twelfth Day of July, 1698
abstract: Headpiece Britain, Sheriffs pre- Cites proclamation 3 March, No. 3144, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 12 July. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation adjourning the Parliament
abstract: Headpiece Britain, chilly Presents Cites proclamation 7 June, No. 3153, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 19 July. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Against Resetting or Assisting Thomas and Capt. Simeon Frasers Elder and Younger at Beaufort, and their Accomplices
abstract: Thomas Fraser of Beaufort and Capt. Simeon Fraser his son with other broken men have seized Lord Saltoun and Lord Mungo Murray, and others, and carried them away, have fortified some houses, and made captive the Lady Dowager of Lovatt. They have been summoned by a herald and denounced rebels. They are to be treated as enemies. No one is to aid them or their belongings. 4,000 merks Scots reward and indemnity to any accomplice for either of the Frasers, dead or alive. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Pi’oclamation Against Regrating of Victual, and Forestalled, and allowing the Importation of Victual free of Publick Burden
abstract: to by presents A reissue of proclamation 9 June 1696, No. 3093, q.v. Liberty to import till 1 October.

title: A Proclamation of Parliament, For a Solemn National Fast
abstract: the God of On the application of the Commissioners of the General Assembly the second Lord’s day of September next is appointed a fast day for Scotland. These to be printed and published. Fine for non-observance £100 Scots, half to the poor.

title: Act Prorogating the Tollerance for Importing Forraign Victual
abstract: The licence to import victual, No. 3156, q.v., is continued till the second Tuesday of November inclusive. These to be printed and published.

title: Proclamation For the more easie and effectual In-bringing of the Pole-money
abstract: of now Ordains Regulations for meetings of commissioners of shires (second Tuesday of October) for making arrangements to list poleable persons (first Tuesday Nov.). Burgh lists to be made. All lists to be sent to Treasury by 1 Dec. to be delivered to the farmers by third Tuesday of December. Fines for neglect. These to be proclaimed, read in churches before the appointed day, and printed.

title: Act Additional to the Proclamation for the more easie and effectual In-bringing of the Pole-money
Proclamation Discharging Export and allowing Import of Victual
abstract: No victual of any sort is to be exported. All victual to enter free of any customs or public duty. These to be printed and proclaimed.

title: Act and Intimation anent this Current Parliament
abstract: Headpiece Ma- And Messen- As His Majesty’s pleasure is not known, all members are to hold themselves in readiness when his will and pleasure are known. These to be printed and proclaimed.

title: Proclamation, Against Regrating of Victual, and Forestalled, and for Regulating the Mercats
abstract: Cites Acts against regrating and forestalling, which are to be strictly executed. Search to be made for victual in Girnels [Garners]. Meal not to be bought except for private use. Oats and pease not to be resold, except as meal, or by innkeepers and army commissaries. Oats may be bought north of Tay and sold south. Markets to be regulated by law. These to be proclaimed, read in all parish churches, and printed.

title: Proclamation Anent the Collectors of the Pole-Money, and other Points relating thereto
abstract: Our granted pretend Sheriffs are to notify at all church doors that pole is to be paid on 1 Jan. or within 30 days ; during Februaiy the double must be paid, afterwards quadruple. Commissioners of Supply are to convene collectors before 1 Jan., and obtain caution from them for the pole-money, to be paid to William Cockran of Fergusly, farmer of the pole-money. Collectors to retain 1 per cent, of amount collected. These to be proclaimed, printed, and read in all churches on the last Lord’s day of December current.

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament till the Fourteenth day of March next
abstract: Headpiece Britain, riffs presents Parliament, now adjourned to 15 November last past, is further adjourned to 14 March next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act Discharging Privy Councellors and others in publick Trust to go out of this Kingdom
abstract: Headpiece Letter by Ignorance Cites royal letter 13 Dec. Repeats Act 29 Aug. 1693, No. 2980, q.v., to 1 March next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Discharging the Transporting of persons to the Plantations of Forraigners in America
abstract: All persons prohibited — natives or foreigners — from carrying abroad any Scots subjects from date to any foreign plantations, on pain of punishment as men-stealers. These to be proclaimed and printed.

issuer: Commissioners for the Communication of Trade
abstract: [Not found.] All burghs to attend the Commission on fixed dates to decide on their quotas under Act 20 of last Session of Parliament. These to be printed and published.

title: Proclamation for a Solemn National Fast
abstract: and tute preceeding On the address of the General Assembly, 9 March is appointed a day of fasting and humiliation for peace and favourable weather. This to be printed, with the Act of General Assembly, proclaimed, and read in all churches the Lord’s day preceding the appointed day. [On back] Act of Assembly for a fast dated 26 January, signed George Meldrum, Moderator, Jo. Bannatyne.

title: Proclamation Anent the Excise after the first of March next, 1699
abstract: The Excises are now farmed to William Menzies and Alexander Wood of Edinburgh for 5 years from 1 March next. Commissioners of Excise to meet at head burghs on j first Tuesday of April, and of each month after. Arrangements for entry of brewings, for barrels, for licences for YOL. II 4 brewing, for supervision of foreign spirits, &e. Officers to assist the tacksmen. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches before first Tuesday of April, posted up on the doors, and printed.

title: Act and Intimation anent this current Parliament 14 March 1699
summary: Edinburgh

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the 14th of June next
abstract: Headpiece Britain, Privy Presents Cites proclamation 20 Dec., No. 3165, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 14 June. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act Anent the Pole-Money
abstract: the anent Burghs Commissioners of Supply in each shire to meet at once and appoint one of their number per vices to keep court weekly, two days a week, viz. Tuesday and Thursday, magistrates of burghs royal the same ; and there to issue citations to persons liable to penalties for pole-money, with summary execution on conviction. Order to clerks of shires and burghs to show the tacksmen their valuation and stentroll when required, and to help them in every possible way. These to be printed and published. (142) . E.T.C. (113).

title: A Proclamation For Re-establishing the Staple-port at Camphire
abstract: Ire- Our this Cites Treaty between King as Marquess of Camphire, and the royal burghs approved by the States of Zeland and the Convention of Royal Burghs, and ratified under sign manual 20 March. No staple-commodities are to be exported from Scotland to any other port in the Netherlands than Camphire. Customs officers to take security for this. Sailors not to break bulk at any other port. Certificates to be brought back from the Conservator at Camphire. These to be proclaimed and printed. List of Staple Commodities. Wooll, woollen and linen yarn, woollen and linen manufactories, hydes and skins, . . . playding, kerseys, Scots cloath, stockins, salmond, tallow, 3 3 P N°s 3174-83 oyl, all sorts of barrel, flesh, pork, butter, leather dressed and undressed.

title: OF TRADE.] A Proclamation
abstract: Commissioners from burghs to attend second Monday of June. Gives proportions to be paid by each burgh towards the amount paid annually by the burghs. Order to print and publish.

title: Proclamation Anent Prices of Victual
abstract: speciment and Cites proclamation 15 Nov. last, No. 3163, q.v. A market price of oats, barley, wheat, pease, and meal to be set by five of the Commissioners of Supply for each shire (two to be a quorum) on 1 May (1 June N. of Tay). None to sell at any higher price on pain of punishment as usurers and occurers, till 1 September next. The commissioners may, as they think fit, forbid transport of victual from their county. These to be proclaimed and printed. List of 155 names of Commissioners.

title: Proclamation anent the Poor and Correction Houses for them
abstract: P.C. Reg. (Entry book). ‘ Nota. This Proclamation was never proclaimed because there are severall blanks in it which were never filled up, albeit ordered to have been done by the Lord Advocat.’ (But see No. 3184.)

title: Proclamation Allowing the free Transporting of Victual from one Shire to another, and the Importation of Forraign Victual free of Custom, and twenty shilling Scots for each Imported Boll thereof
abstract: in Subjects Pro- Proclamations against forestalled and regrators to be enforced. Liberty to import victual free of duty till 15 Aug. with a bounty of 20s. Scots per boll, to be paid on importation. Free course of victual to all markets in the kingdom at any prices agreed upon. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the 12th of September next
abstract: Cites proclamation 21 March, No. 3172, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 12 Sept. next. These to be proclaimed and printed.
signed: Gilb. Eliot, Headpiece Britain, part Ordains

title: Proclamation Against Exporting of Wool and Importing of Woollen-Cloath, &c
abstract: Cites Acts against exportation of wool, and (1681) against import of woollen goods (except flannel, arras-hangings, and foreign carpets). These Acts are revived for the benefit of manufactories, that the idle and poor may be employed. Instead of the half fines to informers the whole fines is granted them. This to be proclaimed, sent to all customhouses, and printed.

title: OF TRADE.] Act of the Commission For Communication of Trade
abstract: nineling dissolving Cites Act of 30 March last, No. 3175, q.v., to unfree traders. All burghs are to attend at Edinburgh before 3 Aug. No application will be received between then and December. Unfree traders will be prosecuted. These to be printed, proclaimed, and read in all churches. E.T.C. I (114). Reg. f. 35''.

title: Proclamation for Adjourning the Parliament
abstract: Headpiece Britain Our pre Cites proclamation 9 June, No. 3179, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 8 November. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Regulating several Particulars anent the Pole, and Intimating the next Year’s Pole
Proclamation Anent the Poor, and Providing Correction-Houses for them
abstract: Refers to extraordinary dearth which has suspended recent acts and proclamations for the poor. All sheriffs, heretors, commissioners of supply, &c. , are to meet on second Thursday of October next to take order under these proclamations and to send beggars to their homes of three years ago. Correction houses are to be ready by 1 December in Edinburgh, Air, Dumfreis, Glasgow, Stirling, Perth, Dundee, Aberdeen, and Inverness, on a penalty of 500 merks Scots for the poor. Approves proclamation 11 Aug. 1692, No. 2945, q.v., 29 Aug. 1693, No. 2981, q.v., and 31 July 1694, No. 3015, q.v., which are to be reprinted. A report from sheriffs and magistrates to be sent in by 1 Feb. next, on peril. These to be px-oclaimed, read in all parish churches, and printed.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the 5th of March 1700 years
abstract: Cites proclamation 31 Aug., No. 3182, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 5 March 1700. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For a Solemn National Thanksgiving and Publick Prayers
abstract: Edinburgh : H. & S. of A. A. : 1 699. On the address of the Commission of the late General Assembly, 30 Nov. to be a day of thanksgiving for public mercies. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches, printed, and published.

title: Proclamation Discharging the Export, and allowing the Import of Victual
abstract: No grain or victual to be exported (except what is needed for the Company trading to Africa and the Indies) on pain of forfeit and fine. Foreign grain or victual may be imported by natives or foreigners. This to be proclaimed, sent to all custom houses, &c., and printed.

title: Proclamation Anent Petitoning
abstract: Earliest form of No. 3189, q.v. Two proof copies of this proclamation in the Register House, from which it appears that it was originally dated 14 December. ‘Proclamation Intimating His Majesties displeasure with the Address from the Affrican and Indian Company.’ This was first altered to ‘ Intimating His Majesties displeasure with the undutiful and disorderly proceedings to procure subscriptions to ane address from the Company trading to Affrica and the Indies ’ and finally altered to ‘ Anent petitioning ’. Reg. V (80) is endorsed ‘ 23 Dec. 1699. The Coppey of the proclamation produced by Mistress Anderson as her warrand for publishing the proclamation according to this Essay sheet. Ad. Cokburne.’ [L. Justice Clerk.] Reg. V (81) ‘Proclamation produced by Thomas Fender servant to the Solicitor. Twenty third of December. 1699. Ad. Cokburne.’ U°

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the Fourteenth Day of May next 1700
abstract: Cites proclamation 4 Nov., No. 3185, q.v. Pax-liament is further adjourned to 1 4 May. These to be proclaimed and px-inted.

title: Proclamation For a Solemn National Fast
abstract: Ordering a fast on 28 March, the last Thursday of the month. [Follows] Act of the General Assembly anent a solemn national fast and humiliation [14 Feb.] (pp. 3 and 4).

title: OF TRADE.] Act Of the Commission of Parliament for settling the Communication of Trade
abstract: Sine nota. Parliament ac- Cites Act 20, Sess. 7 of Pax-liament concerning unfree tx’aders. Commissionei’s of Supply to meet on last Thursday of April next to receive offers from burghs as to their share of the £100 tax, and report to the Commissionex-s before 3 P 2 1 Jane. All burghs to attend the meeting. Unfree traders since Lambmas 1698 will be prosecuted. These to be printed, proclaimed, and read in all churches. E.T.C. I (160). Reg. f. 39b.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the 21 Day of May instant 1700
Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the fourth day of July 1700
abstract: Headpiece France juctly July Approves adjournment by James D. of Queensberry to June 20. It is further adjourned to 4 July. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Discharging Bonfires and Illuminations
abstract: Headpiece France ly ig- No illuminations or bonfires to be used on public rejoicings on pain of punishment for riot. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament to the 13 day of August next to come
abstract: Headpiece France junctly be Cites proclamation 17 June, No. 3194, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 13 August. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Against a late Resolve, containing an Engagement as to Forraign Stuffs and Cl oaths, and certain Forraign Liquors
abstract: France conjunctly none Though by 12 of 10 Jas. VI and 4 of 1 Chas. II no leagues or bonds are to be entered into, a certain resolve regarding foreign cloths and liquors has been made which is a league. All subjects are discharged from carrying it out. These to be proclaimed and printed. B.L.

title: Proclamation For Apprehending Captains Gavine Hamilton, Kenneth Mackenzie & Kenneth Urquhart
abstract: Headpiece and ing Pre- Capt. Gavine Hamilton, son of Gavine Hamilton of Hill, Capt. Kenneth Mackenzie, and Capt. Kenneth Urquhart were ringleaders of the release of prisoners from the Tolbooth on 20 June, especially of Hugh Paterson and James Watson, accused for seditious pamphlets. £1,200 Scots reward for their apprehension. No one to shelter them, &c. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For a Solemn National Fast
abstract: Headpiece Britain cil keeping On address from the Commission of the General Assembly, Thursday 29 August is appointed a day of fasting and humiliation. This and the Act of the Assembly to be read in all churches on the Lord’s day before. These to be proclaimed and printed. [On backj 31 July. Causes of a solemn national fast and humiliation.

title: Proclamation For Discovering and Apprehending House-breakers, Thieves and Robbers, and their Resetters. Edinburgh : 2 ugust 1700
abstract: France Macers to Housebreaking is on the increase. £100 Scots reward for every thief, robber, or housebreaker punished, and also pardon if an accomplice. All vagrants, &c., to be apprehended. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament to the Twenty second day of October 1700
abstract: France Pursevants be Cites proclamation 1 July, No. 3196, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 22 October. This to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the Twenty ninth day of October instant 1700. Edinburgh: 15 October
abstract: Headpiece and Ireland Printed Cites royal letter of 26 July fixing opening for 22 October, but being detained abroad it is adjourned to 29 October. These to be proclaimed and printed. N° 3202. I JANUARY.- [BY THE PRIVY COUNCIL.] Proclamation For Apprehending Walter Herries. Edinburgh : 1 January 1701. and Ireland ignorance. Walter Herries, chyrurgeon, who went with the first ships to Darien of the Company trading to Africa and the West Indies, is the author of two pamphlets, ‘ A defence of the Scots abdicating Darien, including an answer to the Scots settlement there,’ and of ‘ A Vindication ’ of the said former pamphlet. They are blasphemous, scandalous, and calumnious libels. On the address of the Estates he is to be arrested. £6,000 Scots reward for his arrest. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Against importing of Irish Victual
Act For a general and voluntar Contribution, for Rebuilding the Port and Harbour of Ey mouth
abstract: On the petition of Sir John Home of Blackadder and Sir John Swintoun of that ilk, speaking for the shire of Berwick, as to the need of a harbour between Leith and Humbermouth in Yorkshire, and the advantages of a pier and harbour at Eymouth, a collection through the kingdom is ordered, and George Winram of Eymouth is appointed collector. Money to be paid out on the order of Patrick, Earl of Marchmont, Sir John Home, Sir John Swinton, and Sir Patrick Home. B.L. Sig. 50. f. (40). N° 3205. II MARCH. — [BY THE PRIVY COUNCIL.] Proclamation For A Solemn National Fast. Edinburgh : 11 March 1701. and Degrees ap- On the address of the General Assembly, Thursday 24 April is appointed a day of solemn fasting in Scotland. These and the Act of Assembly to be read in all churches the Lord's day preceding. These to be proclaimed and printed. [With] Act of the General Assembly.
signed: Gilb. Eliot, John Home Collections, Gilb. Eliot

title: Act Erecting an Office of Intelligence, in favours of John Lowson
abstract: For a Servant’s Enquiry Office. Master-housholds, gentlemen, valets, stewards, pages, grieves, gardeners, cooks, porters, coachmen, grooms, footmen, postilions, young boys for waiting on gentlemen, or for change houses, gentlewomen, houskeepers, chamber maids, women stewards and cooks, women for keeping children, ordinary servants, . . . taverners and ticket-runners, with all sorts of nurses . . . ‘ Claps ’ go only in Edinburgh and the ‘ Gazzet ’ is uncertain. Patent to John Lowson and his attorneys to establish an office. No wed-men or wed-wives to intervene in the business. Fee 14s. Scots for wages over £12 Scots. 7s. Scots below. Private owner.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the Seventh day of August next to come
abstract: Headpiece and Ireland Print- Parliament at its rising adjourned to 6 May. It is further adjourned to 7 August. These to be printed and proclaimed.

summary: Order to publish Act of 31 Jan. 1701
abstract: Order to print and publish in all seaports the ‘ Act For Preventing wrongous Imprisonment, and against undue Delays in TryaL,’ 31 Jan. No one to be imprisoned without a warrant. All crimes not capital are bailable. J udges forced to order a trial within 60 days on prisoner’s application. No person to be transported furth of the realm but by his own consent or legal sentence. All who transport any person illegally liable to penalty for wrongous imprisonment if action be taken within 3 years.

title: Proclamation For Rouping the Inland Letter-Office
abstract: The tack of the inland letter office fo George Clark, baillie of Edinburgh, for 5 years expires at Martinmas. It will be rouped on Friday, 1 Aug., between 10 and 12 a.m. in the Exchequer House. These to be printed and proclaimed. E.T.C. I (176).

title: Letters of Publication Of a Commission under the Great Seal, for securing the Peace of the Highlands of Scotland
abstract: 2 If. Roman letter. Gilb. Eliot. Heraulds, as 2) to July, Cites Tenor of Commission, Kensington, 30 May 1701, to nobility and gentry to repress disorder in 12 Highland counties, giving summary powers and jurisdiction, till 1 Nov. 1702, registrat 16 August 1701. Ronald Campbel, sealed, Edinburgh, 19 August. These to be proclaimed, read in all churches after worship on Sabbath days, and printed. The date is explained by the Acta of P.C. ‘The Lords of his Majesties privy Councill Doe hereby appoint their Clerk to cause print the Docket which is at the end of His Majesties warrand of the Commission anent the highlands to be printed therewith.’ The full text of the warrant. Adv. Procl. I (173). B°

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament from the seventh of August instant to the sixth of November next to come
abstract: Headpiece Ireland Defender at Cites proclamation 3 May, No. 3208, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 6 November. These to be proclaimed and published.

title: Proclamation Anent the Excise
abstract: specially Macers be The excise is set in tack to Archibald Dumbar of Thundertoun, Kenneth Mackenzie of Cromartie, Sir William Hope, Capt. Philip Anstruther, William Duff of Diple, James Gordon sen., Gilbert Stuart and Peter Campbel for 3 years from 1st of March last. The usual provisions for meetings of Commissioners of Excise, registration of brewings, imported spirits, & c. In Edinburgh fine for each offence convicted, elsewhere only one fine for each trial. These to be proclaimed, read in churches, and printed.

title: Proclamation Against a Treasonable Paper lately affixed upon the Cross of Edinburgh
abstract: Ireland pretend A declaration of the right of succession of the pretended Prince of Wales on the death of the late King James has been clandestinely fixed on the mercat-cross of Edinburgh. It is to be burnt by the hangman. £6,000 Scots reward for the conviction of those who caused it to be put there with a pardon if an accomplice. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation, Explaining some parts of the Commission for the Justiciary of the Highlands
abstract: Ireland these Commissioners who qualify before 1 January next not to be excluded from the Commission. Power given to the commissioners to adjourn. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation Anent the Staple-Port at Camphire
Proclamation For Adjourning of the Parliament to the 8th of January 1702
abstract: Headpiece and Ireland January Cites proclamation 2 Aug., No. 3212, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 8 January next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act For a Solemn Fast within the Synod of Lothian and Tweeddale
abstract: Address made be On address of the synod, Thursday 20 November is appointed a day of fasting in the bounds of the synod. These to be notified in all pulpits, printed and published. [At back] Causes of a solemn fast, &c. Signed Will. Wisheart, Jo. Sandilands.

title: A Proclamation For Dissolving this present Parliament, and Declaring the Speedy Calling another
abstract: A reprint of No. 4294, England, q.v.

title: Proclamation Anent the Old Fourteen- Shilling-Pieces, and their Halfs, and the old Fourty- Penny-Pieces
abstract: By Act 8 of 6 Session of Parliament, 12 Oct. 1696, the 14s. pieces of 2 drop 27 gr. and their halfs, &c., are to pass in all payments. Some people refuse to receive them. They are to pass — the 40d. pieces at 3s. 6 cl. Scots if there is any part of the print and vestige visible, and the 14s. and 7s. pieces if they are of full weight. This to be printed and published. Patrick ii. 280.

title: Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament from the Eight of January instant, to the Fourteenth of April next 1702
abstract: Headpiece and Ireland Published. Cites proclamation 4 Nov., No. 3217, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 14 April. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Act For a Contribution to the Burgh of Elgine, Anent the Building a Harbour at Lossemouth
abstract: liundred the On the petition of the magistrates of Elgin who have no harbour nearer than Garmouth, 6 miles away, or Findhorn, 10 miles away, and have bought some land at Lossemouth, 3 miles away to build one, and in the last 2 years have cleared it so that seven or eight barks up to 70 or 80 tun burden can lie there ; a public collection on 1 July next is ordered through all the churches in Scotland. James Ogilvie, treasurer of the burgh, to receive it and pay it out at order of Lairds of Grant, Brodie, and Innes.

title: Proclamation Against Deserters and their Resetters
abstract: and Ireland Premisses, As several regiments are about to be embarked, the rules about deserters are to be enforced. Any one entertaining a soldier who has been serving within the last 2 months will be punished for resetting. Deserters who return to their colours before 28 February will be indemnified. Proclamation No. 3209, q.v., against undue pressing or transporting out of the kingdom renewed. These to be proclaimed and printed. N° 3223.

title: Her Majesties most Gracious Letter To the Privy Council
abstract: Having taken the Coronation Oath in Privy Council, the Queen authorizes them to act as the Privy Council, and to publish the enclosed proclamation, No. 3226, q.v., in her name. Promises protection for religion, law, and liberty, and favour.

summary: All Officers &c. in Scotland to continue to Act till new Commissions can be issued
abstract: All officers of State, &c., in Scotland to act on the commissions and instructions of the late King, till new commissions can be prepared and sent down to them.

title: Act and Proclamation For Proclaiming the Right and Title of Queen Ann, as undoubted Soveraign of this Realm
abstract: L. Chancellor, E. Melvill, P.C., E. of Crafurd, Buchan, Lawderdale, Loudown, Leven, Forfar, Visct. Tarbat, Roseberry, L. Montgomery, Ross, Boyle, Polwarth, Sir Hugh Dalrymple, L. Advocate, L. Tliesaurer D . . t, L. Justice Clerk, L. Philiphaugh, L. Halcraig, L. Crossrig, L. Rankeiler, L. Phesdo, Francis Montgomery of Giffan, Sir Ro. Sinclair of Stevenson, Laird of Grant, L. Provost of Edinburgh, Laird of Megginch.

title: Act of Privy Council, Allowing the continuing of the former Seals, Signets and Cashet until renewed, and sustaining all Letters and Diligences, preceeding the 13. instant
abstract: dery ordains Cites as precedent Act of Sederunt 14 Feb. 1685, No. 2590, q.v. Old seals are to be used till new ones are ready, with the distinction ‘by special order until the new seals’, &c. All summons, &c., raised and not perfected are to be allowed to run in due course. The Lords of Session to enter this in their Books of Sederunt. These to be printed and published. B.L. Sig. 109. e. 8 (35). Adv. Procl. I (188). Reg. V (92).

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the 26th May next
abstract: Cites Act 1 7, Sess. 6 as to continuance of Parliament and Declaration of Estates 11 April 1689. Parliament is further adjourned to 26 May. These to be proclaimed, printed, and published.

title: Proclamation Requiring the Oath of Alledgiance and Assurance to be Sworn and Subscribed to her Majesty
abstract: Sheriffs in ig- All persons in any official position whatever before 1 July, and all electors before 1 Aug. are to swear allegiance and sign the assurance. Those who do not to be deprived. Ministers to lose their benefices or stipends, preachers to be banished, tacksmen to lose horses and arms. Both Oath and Assurance are to be taken. These to be proclaimed and printed. [Oath and Assurance follow.]

title: A Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament to the Ninth of June next 1702
abstract: Cites royal letter 19 March and proclamation 24 March, No. 3229, q.v. Parliament is further adjourned to 9 June. These to be proclaimed and published.

title: A Proclamation Declaring War against France and Spain
abstract: Issue for Scotland of proclamation 4 May, No. 4321, England, q.v.

title: Act For A National Fast
abstract: p. 1 of 2 ff. Roman letter. Jo. Mackenzie. an onal of Ordering a fast on Thursday 9 July. This to be proclaimed and printed with the Act of Commission of Assembly. Act follows on pp. 2 and 3.

title: Act For securing the true Protestant Religion, and Presbyterian Government
summary: Edinburgh

title: Act Recognizing Her Majesties Royal Authority
summary: Edinburgh
abstract: late gracious Attempts Acknowledging Queen Anne on her proclamation. It is treason to impugn her right. Oath of Allegiance to be taken and the Assurance subscribed. [Follows] Oath of Allegiance and Assurance.

title: Proclamation Requiring the Oath of Alledgeance and Assurance to be Sworn and Subscribed to Her Majesty
abstract: On Act of Parliament 12 June, proclamation 24 March, No. 3230, q.v., is substantially reissued. All persons to swear and subscribe before 1 Nov. on pain of deprivation and disarmament. These to be proclaimed and printed. Follows the Oath of Alledgeance and the Assurance.

title: Act For a General Collection to the Distressed Inhabitants in the Town of Leith
abstract: On petition stating the destruction caused by an explosion of 33 barrels of powder on 3 July, amounting to <£36,936 Scots, a general collection is ordained before 1 Oct. (1 Nov. N. of Tay) either at kirk doors or from house to house, to be paid to Alexander Mathison.

title: Proclamation Anent the Post-office in favours of the Post-master-general and his Deputs
abstract: Recites complaints of Postmaster General, anent common carriers, ferry at Dundee, and the delay of magistrates. No common carriers or others to carry letters except with goods. Magistrates to settle the question within six hours. Postrunners to have ready passage at all ferries, paying at Dundee 6 d., or with a horse 10 d. Magistrates to aid the Postmaster General in every way. These to be proclaimed and printed. Sig. 109. e. 8 (46). Adv. Procl. I (195).

title: A Proclamation Anent the Pole-money, Imposed in the Year 1698
abstract: and Ireland Edin- As to receipts for pole-money, no one to be proceeded against for pole-money on the two poles of 1698 and 1699. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation For Dissolving of this Current Parliament
abstract: and Ireland Edin- Parliament, now adjourned to 18 August, is dissolved. As Commissioners to treat of a Union are to be nominated, a new Parliament will be called. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Proclamation by Her Majesty For Calling a Parliament
abstract: and Subjects the Owing to the war and the report of the Commissioners for Union, a Parliament is to meet at Edinburgh on 12 November next. All peers and officers of State to attend, and sheriffs to hold elections of fit persons to be Commissioners for this Parliament.

title: Act Appointing the Oath of Alledgeance to be Sworn and Signed, and the Assurance to be signed to Her Majesty, by all Ministers, Preachers of the Gospel, and others therein-mentioned
abstract: Consideration, That of In the two proclamations issued for oath, Nos. 3230, 3237, q.v., there is no provision for ministers, &c. All ministers, masters and doctors, teachers, chaplains, and pedagogues to swear before a magistrate before 1 December next. All ministers, even those already sworn, are to do so. These to be printed and published.

title: Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament to the 6th Day of April next to come
abstract: and Ireland Edinburgh Cites proclamation 25 Aug., No. 3242, q.v. Parliament is adjourned to 6 April next. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: Hex- Majesties most Gracious Letter to the Privy Council of Scotland. St. James’s : 4 February 170§
abstract: and loved of Having by Commission of this date appointed the Privy Council of Scotland, recommends to it the established Church, the protection of dissenters, the execution of the laws, public security, the payment of the troops, &c. This letter to be printed and published.

title: Proclamation For calling a General- Assembly
abstract: Headpiece and Messengers Ignorance : A General Assembly met in March 1702 under the Earl of Marchmont but was dissolved owing to the King’s sickness, a new one being called for 10 March 1703. It is to meet on that day. These to be proclaimed and printed.

title: A Proclamation of Indemnity. St. James’s : 16 March 170§
Proclamation Adjourning the Parliament
abstract: Headpiece Dejunctly these Cites pardon, No. 3247, q.v. Adjourns Parliament to 6 May. These to be proclaimed and printed. I 3 Q 5 MAT.— [BY THE PRIVY COUNCIL.] Act Discharging Foot-men and Lackies to wear Swords during the Parliament. Holy-rood house : 5 May 1703. Sine nota. 3250]. Ro. Forbes. Hundred and pleasure ; Order by High Commissioner and Privy Council that footmen and lackies are not to wear swords during the meeting of Parliament.

title: Order Discharging the casting of Squibs, or any Fireworks upon the Streets on the Sixth Day of May next
abstract: Sine nota. 3249]. Ro. Forbes. Hundred and pleasure ; The High Commissioner and Privy Council forbid the throwing of fireworks on the street during the riding of the Parliament, on pain, &c.

title: A Proclamation Against such as have gone to or stayed in France since Her Majesties Gracious Indemnity
Act And Ordinance For A Fast
abstract: Orders a fast on the last Thursday in August. These to be printed and proclaimed. With Act of Commission of General Assembly.

title: Act Of Her Majesties Privie Council, For A Voluntarie Contribution, for building a Bridge over the Water of Dee
abstract: Sine nota. Seven By all- On the petition of James, Earl of Galloway, William, Visct. Kenmuire, and John, Visct. Stair for Galloway and Kirkcud burgh, showing the dangers of the Water of Dee, which has only one ford, the Blackford of Dee, 12 miles distant from any other, on the road from Ireland to England, and from Galloway to the south. A voluntary contribution is ordered for building a bridge near the Blackford of the Dee. Mr. Andrew Euart, minister at Kells, to be treasurer. B.L. Sig. 50. f. (42).

title: Act In favours of William Baird of Auchmedden
Proclamation For Adjourning the Parliament

Householders, &c., to look after their apprentices, servants, and domestics. Regents and masters of the college to keep their scholars in good order. On notice by the magistrates all persons to go home. Those found in the streets to be punished as rioters. The Courts will be moved from Edinburgh if these riots contiuue. This to be proclaimed, printed, and published.

All persons listed to be handed over to recruiting officer ; commissioners to pay 205. each and 6 d. per day expenses to the person bringing them in. £3 paid to each parish for each recruit raised there. Harvesters free from press between 1 June and 15 October. Bailiff’s followers and assistants not exempt from pressing. B.L. 1 February. Unpriced.

summary: Laws against Papists and Non-jurors to be enforced in Scotland
abstract: Address, to your The Lords have addressed the Queen asking for the laws against papists and non-jurors (who are enlisting men to serve against her) should be put in force. Cites Acts Scot. 23 May 1 W. & M., 6 Anne, 35 Eliz. The Oath of Allegiance is to be tendered to all papists and non-jurors. On their refusal they are to be disarmed and confined to their usual habitations. An account of what is done to be sent to the Solicitor-General of Scotland. Buckingham, P., Dartmouth, C.P.S., Northumberland, W. Bromley, Mar, Bolingbroke, Powlett, Portmore, Rochester, Loudoun, Findlater. Addressed to Justices of Peace of Scotland.
